The drone effort formed part of a broader opening that was rapidly producing publicly announced defense partnerships between Abu Dhabi and Tel Aviv. Four days after Elbit announced its Emirati subsidiary, the UAE's EDGE Group and Israel Aerospace Industries signed a memorandum of understanding to jointly design a series of 17-meter unmanned surface vessels. The proposed vessels would support intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance; border patrol; mine detection and sweeping; submarine detection and anti-submarine warfare; and maritime-security operations, according to the[ companies' announcement](https://substack.com/redirect/57055591-38f7-46d2-bf6b-0b2120ef63ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
On January 3, 2022, Elbit [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/efd3d969-8f62-4b10-b755-af3fdf4b2a6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its first publicly disclosed contract through the Emirati subsidiary: a five-year, approximately $53 million agreement to supply directed infrared countermeasures and electronic-warfare self-protection systems for the UAE Air Force's Airbus A330 tanker transport aircraft.
But that public contract was narrower than the drone and intelligence package Elbit was developing privately.
The UAE's security situation changed dramatically later that month. On January 17, Yemen's Ansarallah movement [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/d3058a8b-eb33-4d1a-bbd6-7cd07631e0d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a missile-and-drone attack on Abu Dhabi. Explosions engulfed three fuel tankers near an Abu Dhabi National Oil Company storage facility, killing three people and wounding six; a separate fire broke out at an extension of Abu Dhabi International Airport. A week later, the UAE said its defenses had intercepted and destroyed two Houthi ballistic missiles targeting Abu Dhabi.
By March, internal correspondence described the Emirati project as urgent, and an Elbit planning memorandum said the system was intended to detect missile and drone launches from beyond the UAE's borders.
"They want the SkEye with the 900," Hagi Topolansky, then an Elbit senior vice president responsible for UAVs and strategic affairs and a former deputy commander of the Israeli Air Force, wrote in a March 8 email. The passage appeared under "Arig," a designation that other documents connect to the UAE. Topolansky relayed an unnamed official's assessment that the transaction would close "within a few weeks," adding that the official was highly optimistic and that the customer was "under pressure."
In a separate line, Topolansky wrote that an unidentified customer "really wants" a laser system and that discussions were progressing well. The email did not identify the customer, the laser product, or its price.
On March 13, emails show that Elbit executive Amir Bettesh circulated a planning memorandum to push forward a deal. The memorandum described an initial proposal for five complete Hermes 900 systems for the UAE--three aircraft per system, or 15 aircraft in total. Each system would include electro-optical sensors with laser target designators, daytime and nighttime SkEye systems, self-protection and electronic-warfare equipment, along with ground equipment and training, noting that a "significant discount" had been applied to the proposed sale at customer request.
According to the memorandum, the systems were intended to maintain surveillance beyond the customer's borders and detect missile and drone launches into the country, but could also be used domestically for "homeland security" missions. The deal was portrayed in the document as queuing up a much larger line of business, stating that "in the next phase the customer intends to procure 15 systems in total--an additional 10 systems beyond the urgent operational requirement (UOR) described above--which will incorporate a broader range of mission payloads."
The memorandum stated that the technical specifications, statement of work, financial offer, draft contract, and executive summary had already been delivered to the customer and were "ready for signature."
## Wish List
While the documents in Haimovich's correspondence show that Elbit was pursuing a substantial Hermes 900 sale to the UAE in 2022 and record detailed Emirati operational requirements they do not confirm whether Abu Dhabi executed the sale at the time or received delivery of the systems.
Other correspondence contained in the archive indicate that talks were proceeding for the provision of Israeli-made UAVs and a much broader range of aerial surveillance and electronic warfare equipment to the Emirates.
On February 28, 2023, two short emails were sent from Haimovich's personal Gmail account to her Elbit address. The subjects of the emails were listed as "Johan 1" and "Johan 2" and the underlying documents include metadata indicating that they were created in July 2022. The attachment in the email "Johan 1" is a photographed document marked confidential and titled "Airborne SIGINT Wish List." The document describes itself as a UAE Armed Forces request to acquire two manned and two unmanned signals-intelligence aircraft. It asked that delivery of the initial aircraft, intelligence systems, and supporting equipment begin within 42 months of a contract's initiation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/046fac9c-3c8f-4ae7-92b4-48f10edae89c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
An "Airborne SIGINT Wish List" included in the Gmail account of Vered Haimovich, vice president of Elbit Systems' UAV Systems Business Unit.
The requested aircraft referenced in the document would combine communications intelligence, electronic intelligence, imagery intelligence, electronic attack, cyber-surveillance, and artificial-intelligence capabilities. The electronic-attack requirement included "cyber/laser/HPM attack." A separate technical document defines "HPM" as high-power microwave.
The document attached to "Johan 2" appears to be a detailed vendor response to the wish list in the first email. The document is marked as unclassified as standalone but classified secret when viewed in conjunction with other information and is labelled as "Commercial in Confidence"--a classification often used to refer to commercially sensitive material. The document proposes possible configurations for large and small manned aircraft and unmanned aircraft, as well as cellular and satellite-communications interception and electronic warfare capabilities.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/40d2558a-796f-4022-b599-73b8bae1d479?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A "request for information" included in the Gmail account of Vered Haimovich, vice president of Elbit Systems' UAV Systems Business Unit.
The correspondence continues with emails--including "Johan 3" and "Johan 4"--containing password-protected draft files whose contents are not visible in the hacked email archive.
## "More relevant and stronger"
The internal Elbit proposals and correspondence concerning the UAE and the sale of Hermes 900 systems and other aerial surveillance tools to Abu Dhabi emerged amid a rapidly expanding Israeli-Emirati military relationship that had evolved after the Abraham Accords from diplomatic normalization into increasingly open defense cooperation.
By September 2022,[ Reuters reported](https://substack.com/redirect/84294b66-fc63-4b8a-a488-c14fc1e788cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Israel had agreed to sell the UAE a SPYDER air-defense system, citing sources familiar with the agreement. Neither government publicly confirmed the details at the time. In 2023, Israel's Ministry of Defense [inaugurated](https://substack.com/redirect/5902e478-ed72-451f-a86a-2ac1674ec86b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its first national pavilion at the IDEX arms exhibition in Abu Dhabi with more than 30 Israeli companies displaying air-defense systems, drones, artificial intelligence, electro-optics, and cyber technology.
In November 2025, Elbit announced an eight-year, $2.3 billion contract for an unnamed international customer. One month later,[ Calcalist reported](https://substack.com/redirect/9eb57072-7311-4557-b784-242a283ba3d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), citing the French publication Intelligence Online, that the customer was the UAE.
The Iron Dome deployment during the 2026 Iran war represents yet another evolution in a relationship that has continued to blossom despite the genocide in Gaza and a regional war triggered by Israel and the U.S., bringing Israeli equipment and personnel to operate inside the Emirates during an active conflict.
Despite keeping many details of its defense cooperation with Israel secret, the UAE has become more vocal about its attachment to Tel Aviv, describing its relationship as one based on shared values and interests.
"Everything that the UAE does with Israel is formal, above board," said Emirati presidential advisor Anwar Gargash in an [interview](https://substack.com/redirect/5dce53ed-586f-428d-a0a2-21ff6c3ebdca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this May. "We don't have to find secret channels to do that, and I feel that that relationship is going to be even stronger, and the Israeli relationship is more relevant and stronger."

On May 12, U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee publicly disclosed a significant development in the military relationship between Israel and the United Arab Emirates amid the war in Iran. "Israel just sent [the UAE] Iron Dome batteries and personnel to help operate them," Huckabee said at an event in Tel Aviv. Huckabee described the deployment as a fruit of the Abraham Accords, calling the Israeli-Emirati relationship "extraordinary." The deployment--as Iranian missiles and drones targeted the region in response to a joint U.S.-Israeli attack--marked the first publicly acknowledged presence of Israeli military personnel and air-defense equipment inside a Gulf monarchy. But the integration of Israeli weapons into the UAE's defenses did not begin with the Iran war. An archive drawn from the email account of Vered Haimovich, a former Israeli military officer who became vice president of Elbit Systems' UAV Systems Business Unit in January 2021, shows how the arms company worked in the aftermath of the Abraham Accords to create a channel for the sale of drones and aerial surveillance equipment to Abu Dhabi. The email archive includes internal documents from Elbit and its Emirati subsidiary, as well as documents identified as request lists from the UAE military to Elbit in the context of negotiating weapons deals. Drop Site conducted cryptographic verification on the email address signatures and also verified non-public contact information for parties referenced in the documents. The email archive was published by Distributed Denial of Secrets and released by Handala, an online hacking group presumed to be tied to the Iranian Ministry of Intelligence. The archive consists of personal messages, newsletters, and advertisements from Haimovich's Gmail account. But it also contains a smaller collection of Elbit correspondence that executives from the company sent to her personal account--along with Elbit documents Haimovich forwarded to her own Gmail account from her Elbit address. The Elbit emails, dating from late 2021 through early 2023, include a detailed April 2022 proposal from Elbit Systems Emirates subsidiary to provide a suite of Hermes 900 drones with supporting equipment and logistical support to Abu Dhabi. The proposal lays out the terms of a deal that would see the Israeli defense manufacturer provide the UAE two Hermes 900 systems comprising six aircraft, SkEye wide-area surveillance sensors, ground-control equipment, training, and logistical support. The proposal identifies Elbit Systems Ltd. as the seller and says the package was intended to meet an "Urgent Operational Requirement" of the UAE. The initial package offered six aircraft and supporting systems for $154 million with additional upgrades that would raise its total value to approximately $225 million. | | ---|---|--- From an Elbit Systems Emirates proposal for a Hermes 900 drone system included in the Gmail account of Vered Haimovich, vice president of Elbit Systems' UAV Systems Business Unit. Other documents also point to a broader Emirati interest in airborne intelligence and electronic-warfare capabilities provided by Israeli firms. One photographed document, labeled "Confidential" and titled "Airborne SIGINT Wish List," describes itself as a UAE Armed Forces request for two manned and two unmanned signals-intelligence aircraft. The request sought systems capable of intercepting cellular and satellite communications and conducting electronic attacks involving cyber operations, lasers, and high-power microwave technology. Neither Elbit nor the Emirati government has publicly confirmed that the UAE has acquired or currently operates Hermes drones, and the documents available in the archive do not include a final purchase order or delivery record, although internal correspondence repeatedly described the Emirati requirements at the time as urgent and stated that an agreement could close within weeks. Despite public proclamations of the close relationship between the two countries by both Emirati and Israeli officials, specific details of their defense relationship have remained largely hidden from the public. In 2025, it was reported that the UAE's Edge Group was in talks with Elbit to purchase the Hermes 900 in a deal that would include "transfer of technology and localized production," from Tel Aviv to Abu Dhabi, marking a rare public acknowledgement of an opaque defense relationship that has slowly been coming out of the shadows since the signing of the Abraham Accords in 2020. Reached for comment, Elbit Systems stated that it "does not comment on business matters relating to its customers," but added, "the materials presented do not accurately reflect the company's business activities." The company did not respond to follow-up questions. The Emirati embassy and Ministry of Defense did not respond to a request for comment. "We need to move quickly" On November 14, 2021, Elbit publicly announced that it had established Elbit Systems Emirates as a subsidiary that would pursue "long-term cooperation" with the UAE Armed Forces, customize systems for Emirati requirements, and lead technology transfers to the country. At the time, both countries were still basking in the glow of the recently signed Abraham Accords, which had helped set the stage for a more overt partnership. "The Abraham Accords provide a sound basis for business collaborations in the region," Elbit executive Ran Kril said in the. Five days earlier, internal correspondence from Haimovich's inbox indicated that Elbit had already received preliminary policy authorization to pursue a Hermes 900 sale to the UAE in a restricted configuration. A November 9 email, written by Elbit executive Michael Edelstein, summarized a meeting the previous day between Elbit CEO Bezhalel Machlis and the head of the Israeli Defense Ministry's Defense Export Controls Agency. Under the heading "United Arab Emirates," Edelstein wrote that the official had given permission to proceed with a "900" drone in an imaging-only configuration. The UAE was also described as an important prospective customer for Israeli arms, though development of the relationship would depend on political conditions. "The potential is considerable, but for internal and external strategic reasons, progress will not be comprehensive immediately," Edelstein wrote. The email also mentioned a list of candidates for weapons exports to other Gulf Arab states, including Saudi Arabia, for whom a C-130 aircraft upgrade is noted in the email as "approved to proceed," along with artillery equipment for the Saudi military. The Israeli Defense Export Controls Agency, the email continued, had approved the sales to Riyadh so long as the artillery equipment did not match planned IDF military upgrades, and despite concerns that "development of relations is progressing slowly" with Saudi Arabia, which is not a signatory to the Abraham Accords and does not maintain official relations with Israel. Qatar is also listed in the email as approved for the sale of an aircraft protection countermeasure system known as , as well as additional signals intelligence equipment to Bahrain. The Qatari, Saudi, and Bahraini embassies did not respond to requests for comment. The same email also addresses the possibility of receiving future export authorization for the sale of offensive weapons for the UAE. The first was Elbit's , a 2,000-pound air-dropped penetrator bomb designed to break through reinforced concrete before exploding. The second was the in Hebrew as "Shrakek"--an Elbit loitering munition, or explosive attack drone, designed to circle over an area before diving into a target. "Pay attention to the 900," Elbit executive Yoram Shmuely wrote when forwarding the summary to Haimovich. "We need to move quickly." Drop Site is reader-supported. Four days after Elbit announced its Emirati subsidiary, the UAE's EDGE Group and Israel Aerospace Industries signed a memorandum of understanding to jointly design a series of 17-meter unmanned surface vessels. The proposed vessels would support intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance; border patrol; mine detection and sweeping; submarine detection and anti-submarine warfare; and maritime-security operations, according to the. On January 3, 2022, Elbit its first publicly disclosed contract through the Emirati subsidiary: a five-year, approximately $53 million agreement to supply directed infrared countermeasures and electronic-warfare self-protection systems for the UAE Air Force's Airbus A330 tanker transport aircraft. But that public contract was narrower than the drone and intelligence package Elbit was developing privately. The UAE's security situation changed dramatically later that month. On January 17, Yemen's Ansarallah movement a missile-and-drone attack on Abu Dhabi. Explosions engulfed three fuel tankers near an Abu Dhabi National Oil Company storage facility, killing three people and wounding six; a separate fire broke out at an extension of Abu Dhabi International Airport. A week later, the UAE said its defenses had intercepted and destroyed two Houthi ballistic missiles targeting Abu Dhabi. By March, internal correspondence described the Emirati project as urgent, and an Elbit planning memorandum said the system was intended to detect missile and drone launches from beyond the UAE's borders. "They want the SkEye with the 900," Hagi Topolansky, then an Elbit senior vice president responsible for UAVs and strategic affairs and a former deputy commander of the Israeli Air Force, wrote in a March 8 email. The passage appeared under "Arig," a designation that other documents connect to the UAE. Topolansky relayed an unnamed official's assessment that the transaction would close "within a few weeks," adding that the official was highly optimistic and that the customer was "under pressure." In a separate line, Topolansky wrote that an unidentified customer "really wants" a laser system and that discussions were progressing well. The email did not identify the customer, the laser product, or its price. On March 13, emails show that Elbit executive Amir Bettesh circulated a planning memorandum to push forward a deal. The memorandum described an initial proposal for five complete Hermes 900 systems for the UAE--three aircraft per system, or 15 aircraft in total. Each system would include electro-optical sensors with laser target designators, daytime and nighttime SkEye systems, self-protection and electronic-warfare equipment, along with ground equipment and training, noting that a "significant discount" had been applied to the proposed sale at customer request. According to the memorandum, the systems were intended to maintain surveillance beyond the customer's borders and detect missile and drone launches into the country, but could also be used domestically for "homeland security" missions. The deal was portrayed in the document as queuing up a much larger line of business, stating that "in the next phase the customer intends to procure 15 systems in total--an additional 10 systems beyond the urgent operational requirement (UOR) described above--which will incorporate a broader range of mission payloads." The memorandum stated that the technical specifications, statement of work, financial offer, draft contract, and executive summary had already been delivered to the customer and were "ready for signature." Wish List While the documents in Haimovich's correspondence show that Elbit was pursuing a substantial Hermes 900 sale to the UAE in 2022 and record detailed Emirati operational requirements they do not confirm whether Abu Dhabi executed the sale at the time or received delivery of the systems. Other correspondence contained in the archive indicate that talks were proceeding for the provision of Israeli-made UAVs and a much broader range of aerial surveillance and electronic warfare equipment to the Emirates. On February 28, 2023, two short emails were sent from Haimovich's personal Gmail account to her Elbit address. The subjects of the emails were listed as "Johan 1" and "Johan 2" and the underlying documents include metadata indicating that they were created in July 2022. The attachment in the email "Johan 1" is a photographed document marked confidential and titled "Airborne SIGINT Wish List." The document describes itself as a UAE Armed Forces request to acquire two manned and two unmanned signals-intelligence aircraft. It asked that delivery of the initial aircraft, intelligence systems, and supporting equipment begin within 42 months of a contract's initiation. | | ---|---|--- An "Airborne SIGINT Wish List" included in the Gmail account of Vered Haimovich, vice president of Elbit Systems' UAV Systems Business Unit. The requested aircraft referenced in the document would combine communications intelligence, electronic intelligence, imagery intelligence, electronic attack, cyber-surveillance, and artificial-intelligence capabilities. The electronic-attack requirement included "cyber/laser/HPM attack." A separate technical document defines "HPM" as high-power microwave. The document attached to "Johan 2" appears to be a detailed vendor response to the wish list in the first email. The document is marked as unclassified as standalone but classified secret when viewed in conjunction with other information and is labelled as "Commercial in Confidence"--a classification often used to refer to commercially sensitive material. The document proposes possible configurations for large and small manned aircraft and unmanned aircraft, as well as cellular and satellite-communications interception and electronic warfare capabilities. | | ---|---|--- A "request for information" included in the Gmail account of Vered Haimovich, vice president of Elbit Systems' UAV Systems Business Unit. The correspondence continues with emails--including "Johan 3" and "Johan 4"--containing password-protected draft files whose contents are not visible in the hacked email archive. "More relevant and stronger" The internal Elbit proposals and correspondence concerning the UAE and the sale of Hermes 900 systems and other aerial surveillance tools to Abu Dhabi emerged amid a rapidly expanding Israeli-Emirati military relationship that had evolved after the Abraham Accords from diplomatic normalization into increasingly open defense cooperation. By September 2022, that Israel had agreed to sell the UAE a SPYDER air-defense system, citing sources familiar with the agreement. Neither government publicly confirmed the details at the time. In 2023, Israel's Ministry of Defense its first national pavilion at the IDEX arms exhibition in Abu Dhabi with more than 30 Israeli companies displaying air-defense systems, drones, artificial intelligence, electro-optics, and cyber technology. In November 2025, Elbit announced an eight-year, $2.3 billion contract for an unnamed international customer. One month later,, citing the French publication Intelligence Online, that the customer was the UAE. The Iron Dome deployment during the 2026 Iran war represents yet another evolution in a relationship that has continued to blossom despite the genocide in Gaza and a regional war triggered by Israel and the U.S., bringing Israeli equipment and personnel to operate inside the Emirates during an active conflict. Despite keeping many details of its defense cooperation with Israel secret, the UAE has become more vocal about its attachment to Tel Aviv, describing its relationship as one based on shared values and interests. "Everything that the UAE does with Israel is formal, above board," said Emirati presidential advisor Anwar Gargash in an this May. "We don't have to find secret channels to do that, and I feel that that relationship is going to be even stronger, and the Israeli relationship is more relevant and stronger." # Will You Support With A $5.00 Donation?
---
| Hi Friend,
When I look at Memphis & District 91 I don't see a map or a voting bloc. I see home -- the neighborhoods that I have lived in, grown in, and work in, the small businesses that hold our block together, the families who show up for each other every single day.
For nearly 6 years, it has been the honor of my life to stand up for you in the Tennessee House. But right now, too many decisions about our schools, our healthcare, and our future are being made for us instead of with us -- often by people who don't live in our zip codes.
I'm running again to keep fighting for: • Fully funded neighborhood schools • Good-paying jobs and workforce pathways • Safer streets built on trust with us involved
But this campaign isn't powered by lobbyists or insiders -- it's powered by you. Keeping our message in front of every voter takes real resources.
Can you chip in $5, $10, or $15 today to help us reach every voter!
Together, we can keep building a Tennessee where opportunity lives on every street -- and where no one gets left behind.
Onward,
Rep. Torrey C. Harris Tennessee House * District 91

| | We are excited to share that the application for our upcoming NextWave Regional Bootcamp for the Midwest Region is NOW LIVE!
The [**NextWave Midwestern Regional Bootcamp**](https://us.list-manage.com/1B3WRfHnxop?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)**will be held in Chicago, IL, from August 26 - 28th**. We are seeking applicants who are interested in, or currently working on, campaigns or for state parties in the Midwest. [**The application will be open until Monday, August 3, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.**](https://us.list-manage.com/wdZQ8vh6B0e?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)
The DNC NextWave Regional Bootcamp is a new, **free training program** that serves to strengthen the pipeline for the next generation of campaign and party staff and prepare them to win down-ballot races for 2026 and beyond.
This three-day, in-person training program provides participants with specialized training based on their campaign experience level and connects them with other campaign talent and professionals in their region. Four NextWave Regional Bootcamps will be held throughout the country in 2026.
**NextWave Regional Bootcamp Tracks** : Participants are placed into one of two tracks to maximize their experience at NextWave:
1. **Campaigns 101:** for current or aspiring field organizers, fellows, and campaign associates with less than two cycles of experience who are looking to strengthen their skills and get exposure to new aspects of campaign and state party work.
2. **Management Track:** for mid-level and senior campaign and state party professionals who understand the technical aspects of campaign work but are looking to expand their skills as managers and leaders in the Democratic ecosystem.

In addition to hands-on training, participants will also have the opportunity to network with other campaign professionals and learn about campaign and state party job opportunities in their region.
---
| [APPLY HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/sgL7_GljkeU?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)
---
| | The DNC will prioritize applicants from the following states for the NextWave Midwestern Regional Bootcamp: Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, South Dakota, and Wisconsin.
After their acceptances, participants will have the opportunity to request lodging support from the DNC for the duration of the training program. Some lodging support may be provided to attendees who need it, but this is not guaranteed. The DNC is unable to provide additional travel support outside of lodging.

PENTAGON CONFIRMS AN 18TH U.S. DEATH AS TRUMP EYES IRAN'S NUCLEAR SITES
What's Happening
* U.S. Central Command carried out another round of strikes on Iran on Tuesday, extending a nightly bombing campaign now well into its second week.
* The Pentagon confirmed an **18th U.S. service member has died** : Spc. Angel Rampersad, 28, of New York — previously listed missing after the July 17 Iranian attack on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan. He joins Sgt. Tyler Feehan, 25, of Hawaii, and Pfc. Isabella Gonzales, 19, of Texas.
* President Trump warned the U.S. could soon strike **Iran's nuclear facilities** ; Tehran vowed "grave consequences."

The Situation
* War Secretary Pete Hegseth told senators Iran is "at the weakest point militarily" in perhaps 47 years, while conceding it "still [has] capabilities."
* Gulf partners Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan reported intercepting fresh Iranian attacks.
* Mediators are pressing for a short ceasefire to revive talks, but negotiations remain stalled.

The Perspective
Every fallen service member is a reminder that this is a real war with real costs, and their sacrifice deserves a mission worthy of it. Degrading a hostile regime that killed Americans and choked the world's most important oil lane is a legitimate aim. But threatening Iran's nuclear sites raises the ceiling on this fight — and before the country climbs another rung, Americans deserve a clear objective and a defined end, not just "weakest in 47 years."

TRUMP HITS CANADA WITH 50% TARIFFS ON CARS, DAIRY, AND ALCOHOL
What's Happening
* President Trump announced **50% tariffs on most Canadian goods** , singling out automobiles, alcohol, and dairy.
* He argued Canada has **unfairly discriminated** against U.S. automakers, distillers, and dairy farmers.

The Situation
* Canada is one of America's largest trading partners, and Ottawa is expected to weigh retaliation.
* Tariffs are paid by U.S. importers and often passed on, so some prices could rise.
* The move lands while gas and grocery costs are already elevated by the Iran war.

The Perspective
Confronting trading partners who tilt the rules in their own favor is overdue, and leverage sometimes requires a credible threat. The catch: a 50% wall is a tax that can boomerang onto American buyers, and picking a fight with a close ally carries its own risks. The test is whether it forces a better deal — or just raises prices.

GRAHAM'S SISTER WILL SEEK A FULL SENATE TERM AT TRUMP'S URGING
What's Happening
* Sen. **Darline Graham Nordone** — appointed to fill her late brother Lindsey Graham's South Carolina seat — announced she will run for a full six-year term.
* Her decision came after President Trump **publicly urged her to run**.

The Situation
* She was sworn in this month to keep the seat in Republican hands after Graham's death.
* She'll still have to win a primary and a general election on her own.
* The seat is a linchpin of a GOP Senate majority that is currently thin on the floor.

The Perspective
Keeping a reliably conservative seat — and Trump's stamp on the race — is a clear win for Republicans heading into a tough midterm map. Appointment is not election, though: a first-time candidate carrying a famous name still has to prove she can hold it at the ballot box.

Peter,
In the span of a single week, ICE agents killed three people.
In Maine, an agent shot and killed Johan Sebastian Duran Guerrero, a 26-year-old with a valid work permit and Social Security number, as he sat in his car with his three-year-old daughter beside him. The next day in Florida, a man was struck and killed by a tractor trailer while fleeing immigration agents. Days before, in Houston, an agent shot and killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a father of three and a small-business owner, as he drove.
There have now been at least 11 murders by ICE since Trump took office. But instead of accountability, the Trump administration is conducting a cover-up. Last week, the FBI was told it will no longer investigate violent incidents involving immigration agents. Those cases will now be investigated by Homeland Security Investigations, a branch of ICE itself.

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | Jacob Davis's Market Brief (ads) | • | Awesomely ---|--- • | Safe Money Report • | Weiss Ratings | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. For half a century, Russia has treated energy not merely as a commodity but as an instrument of state power. Oil financed its military, and gas pipelines gave Moscow leverage over Europe. Foreign governments could criticize and sanction Russia, but sooner or later, many of them still had to buy what Russia was selling. Now Ukraine is turning that arrangement inside out.
After [18 months](https://substack.com/redirect/1e377289-8116-4cd2-8dd9-453e499a7ca1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian refineries, gasoline shortages have forced the Kremlin to turn to [India](https://substack.com/redirect/96249398-2a85-4b0c-883e-ce04511543db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for fuel. The reversal is almost too perfect: [India spent years buying discounted Russian crude](https://substack.com/redirect/045f5ee8-8ecd-49d4-9550-2d2184f9d138?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); now Russia is asking Indian companies to refine it and sell it back as gasoline. A petrostate importing the finished product made from its own principal export is more than an economic inconvenience. It is a strategic humiliation.
Ukraine's attacks have exposed an extraordinary economic imbalance. A drone costing thousands of dollars can travel hundreds of miles into Russian territory and disable refinery equipment worth hundreds of millions. It is the military equivalent of crippling an aircraft carrier with something assembled from the electronics aisle. The attacks have reportedly knocked a [substantial share](https://substack.com/redirect/e6c1e5ce-6c45-4cd2-842c-e3ac3b7b8435?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Russia's refining capacity [out of operation](https://substack.com/redirect/c9617aab-ff5a-40fb-a0f8-6986ad257608?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Russia cannot simply replace what has been lost. Refineries are not warehouses filled with interchangeable machinery. They are sprawling, intricate systems whose operation can depend on a handful of specialized components, many of which Russia struggles to obtain under sanctions. A drone does not need to flatten an [entire complex](https://substack.com/redirect/215dabbf-9f8a-4701-984a-dcd4537d4488?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). It only needs to find the one piece of equipment without which the rest of it cannot function.
Ukraine has exposed the Achilles' heel of the modern petrostate: oil in the ground is useless if you cannot turn it into fuel.
That is why Russia's gasoline shortage should command Washington's attention. The attacks have revealed a vulnerability every modern military shares. A smaller country, with fewer resources and far less conventional firepower, has used cheap, expendable drones to impose enormous costs on infrastructure that is difficult to defend and even harder to replace.
Military bases and critical infrastructure are all large, stationary targets in an age of small, mobile weapons. Offense has become cheap while defense remains ruinously expensive. Unless the United States can close that gap, the same logic now crippling Russian refineries could one day be turned against American infrastructure.
Ukraine has proved that inexpensive drones are becoming one of the organizing forces of modern warfare.
For 80 years, American military dominance rested partly on our ability to build weapons more sophisticated than anyone else's. But sophistication alone is no longer enough. The next advantage will belong to the country that can field unmanned and increasingly autonomous systems in large numbers--and defeat the enemy's systems cheaply and repeatedly. The United States is not there yet.
The Pentagon understands that America needs inexpensive drones of its own, produced by the thousands. But building them is only part of the challenge. The harder question is how to stop them. How do you protect a military base when the airspace above it can be saturated with inexpensive machines? Just as important, how do you do it without allowing the attacker to bankrupt you? It's not feasible to fire million-dollar missiles at cheap drones forever.
The Pentagon has begun responding by establishing the [Joint Interagency Task Force 401](https://substack.com/redirect/09d433b3-f637-4e99-8501-ab1c71256a62?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to unify and accelerate counter-drone efforts across the government. That was a necessary step. But creating an organization is not the same as solving the problem. Responsibility remains divided across services and commands, while funding and procurement move through separate bureaucracies. No single official is clearly responsible for delivering a counter-drone defense that works at scale.
Part of the answer may be directed energy: lasers and high-powered microwaves capable of disabling drones without firing a costly interceptor at every target. These systems will not replace conventional defenses, but they could change the economics of using them.
Once deployed and powered, a laser or microwave system may be able to engage another target for only a few dollars. Its ammunition is, in effect, electricity. Companies such as [Applied Energetics](https://substack.com/redirect/8b01ec79-7ee3-46ac-b197-311536048900?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) are developing systems built around that promise. But promising economics are not the same as proven capability.
Directed-energy weapons still have to work outside the laboratory. Weather can interfere with performance. Smoke and dust can obscure targets. Power and cooling requirements can limit where a system is deployed.
The Pentagon should therefore reward demonstrated battlefield performance, not theoretical elegance. It should invest in systems that can defeat moving drones and coordinated attacks under realistic conditions. That discipline is what separates a promising technology from an actual military capability.
Ukraine has taught the world that military advantage no longer belongs automatically to the side with the most expensive equipment. Increasingly, it belongs to the side that can produce, deploy, lose, and replace inexpensive systems faster than its adversary can destroy them.
The next war may be decided not by which country can build the most exquisite weapon, but by which can survive the ugliest arithmetic: hundreds of cheap machines arriving faster thaect the need for next generation of public and private partnerships."n expensive defenses can stop them.
America still has the money, engineering talent, and industrial capacity to solve that problem. What it does not have is unlimited time--or any remaining excuse to treat counter-drone defense as a problem for the future.
Russia's refineries have already shown what that future looks like.

The shift--roughly 82% to under 70% of women married by age 30 between the 1970s and 1980s--reflects one of the most rapid structural breaks in U.S. marriage patterns on record. While different Census tabulations quote slightly different baselines (some show ~85-91% in 1970, with sharp drops accelerating through the 1980s), the causal story is consistent: it wasn't a single change, but a convergence of legal, economic, technological, and cultural shifts that matured right in that window.

Here are the main drivers that broke the old norm of early marriage:

1\. **Women 's Economic Independence Became Mainstream**

By the late 1970s and 1980s, women's labor-force participation and wages had risen enough that marriage was no longer an economic necessity for many. As Brookings researchers noted, in 1970 about **44% of women ages 30-50 had no independent earnings**; by later decades that was down to 25%. As women gained control over their own finances, they could support delays in marriage to pursue careers or simply remain single without facing destitution.

2\. **The Birth Control Pill 's Generational Ripple Effect**

The pill was approved in 1960, but its full social impact hit the cohorts coming of age in the 1970s and 1980s. By the time those women reached their late 20s, they had spent a decade with reliable, legal contraception that let them invest in college and careers without the "biological clock" pressure to marry early. Harvard economists Claudia Goldin and Lawrence Katz found that early legal access to the pill significantly **delayed marriage and motherhood** and increased women's professional occupation rates.

3\. **No-Fault Divorce Became Nationwide**

California passed the first no-fault divorce law in 1969, and by the late 1970s most states had followed. The practical effect was twofold:
\- It made **exit from marriage easier**, reducing the "security" marriage once offered and making young people more cautious about marrying young.
\- Divorce rates peaked around **1979-1981**. Watching that wave made many delay or avoid marriage until they felt more certain.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a8d0196c-a11d-4105-9afd-036ee503bdb2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
4\. **Cohabitation Went Mainstream as an Alternative**

Living together without marrying shifted from fringe to normal during the 1980s. Sociological estimates suggest that by the mid-to-late 1980s, **about half of all first marriages were preceded by cohabitation**. This gave couples a way to test partnerships, share expenses, and delay--or skip--the formal marriage step entirely.

5\. **Higher Education and Career Prioritization**

The 1970s and 1980s were the first decades in which large numbers of women pursued four-year degrees and professional careers as the default path rather than the exception. Title IX (1972) expanded access, and by the 1980s women were beginning to outpace men in college enrollment in many fields. More time in school and early career building naturally pushed marriage ages back.

6\. **Changing Male Economic Prospects and Rising "Material" Expectations**

The 1970s stagflation and the industrial restructuring of the early 1980s eroded the "family wage" many working-class men had relied on. At the same time, cultural expectations for what a stable marriage required (housing, dual incomes, financial security) rose. Researchers note that **deteriorating economic prospects for non-college men** and heightened material expectations for marriage contributed to lower marriage rates, particularly among less-educated groups.

**Bottom Line**

The 1970s-to-1980s drop was the tipping point where marriage shifted from a near-universal early-life milestone to an optional, later-life capstone. The women who would have married at 22 in 1970 were instead graduating college, starting careers, cohabiting, or simply choosing to remain single in 1985--because the legal, economic, and technological constraints that once made early marriage the only viable path had largely dissolved.

**We’re the _DLCC_ – _not_ the DNC. Let me explain: ** _The DLCC is_ dedicated to winning Democratic control of state legislatures. _The DLCC is_ the campaign arm for more than 3,000 state legislators and thousands of candidates across all 50 states. _The DLCC's candidates are_ leading with a first-hand understanding of the challenges and priorities of their communities. Back when I first launched this campaign, I received a message on social media offering to take me to see parts of the district I've never been to before. A former UPS driver in northern Campbell and Claiborne counties, Bob told me that since I was running to represent the people of East Tennessee, he wanted to introduce me to people who had never had real representation.
Last Friday, I took him up on his offer, and **we spent 8 hours making good on his promise to take me off the beaten path in TN-02.**
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/e4279573-8cd6-4c07-9331-469ca30cb7e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
We followed back roads through Royal Blue and Pioneer and visited the TWRA headquarters to learn if screwworm was going to be an issue for the elk herd, and what that would mean for the local economy. Experts shared that screwworm isn't a concern (yet), but **folks did tell us that manufacturing jobs have dried up.**
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/76ce1380-4301-4154-ad49-aa50e14aad78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
"How many times has Burchett been up here?" Bob asked one man at one such stop. He shrugged. "Never that I know of."
Then we went to the Jellico Hospital, which shut down in 2024. There was a printed sign on the door that gave the address of **the nearest hospital in Kentucky where folks could seek care if they were having a medical emergency -- over 30 minutes away.**
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/79336e59-9220-45a4-becf-099cc58ddb52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
As we made our way through Morley, White Oak, Anthras, Eagan, Clairfield, and Clear Fork, we stopped anywhere the community gathered. At each stop, Bob would share that he used to be the UPS driver, then would gesture at me. "This is Michaela Barnett. She's running to represent us, and she's the real deal. I told her I could introduce her to folks who have never had real representation." When he said this, I think every single head nodded knowingly.
**Healthcare workers shared how challenging it has been since Jellico closed, and that many areas have no ambulance service.**
**Store owners said getting merchandise was getting more and more expensive, and that jobs had been steadily drying up.**
**Grandparents are caring for grandkids on fixed incomes, and having a hard time paying all the bills.**
At the secondhand shop next to the Dayspring Health Clinic at Clairfield, we asked what we could do to help. "Many of the families do their back-to-school shopping here, because we're much cheaper than Goodwill," they told us. More than anything, we need kids' clothes in all sizes." (_We 're doing a clothing drive to fulfill this need! See details at the end of this email_).
We made our way back down through Habersham, Wynn, and Duff, before crossing back into familiar terrain in LaFollette.
**I 've known for a long time that the more rural parts of our district have been hit hardest by failed policies and ineffective representation.** It was sobering, though not surprising, to hear residents' stories of how they have personally been impacted by these failures.
Do you know what _was_ surprising?
In Pioneer, when I introduced myself to one man, he nodded. "I think I've seen you online. Good luck!" In White Oak, I knocked on someone's door, and the woman answering greeted me like an old friend. She's been following the campaign, and was delighted I'd come to say hello.
In Clairfield, a woman at the Community Clothing Center said, "I thought that was you! I saw you at the LaFollette picnic last weekend. I have your sign in my car!"
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/aac738c5-d133-4ef4-8047-1001936a7edf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In Clear Fork, a group of volunteers was giving away school supplies at the Volunteer Fire Department. They were closing up for the day, and one woman who thought I was stopping for supplies rushed to unpack some for me. When I explained who I was and that I was just stopping to introduce myself to the folks there, another woman overheard and approached.
"Michaela? I live on the other side of Claiborne county! I have your sign in my yard!"
The same thing happened at the Tomato Festival in Grainger county on Saturday. I stopped to say hello to a couple's adorable dogs after buying some tomatoes, and after a doubletake, the woman said: "Are you Michaela? Oh my gosh, I follow you! We love what you're doing. I can't believe we're meeting you here!"
On our drive Friday, Amelia and I ran out of business cards. We're planning to go back with literature and yard signs when we bring school clothes up for the Community Clothing Center in Clairfield.
**Here 's what last weekend tells me: our message - that government **_**can**_**and** _**should**_**serve East Tennesseans - has reached the furthest corners of our district.**
That we _do_ deserve healthcare we can afford, investments in our infrastructure and our workforce. That East Tennessee should be a place where hard work puts you ahead. That our seniors should be able to retire in dignity, and our young people shouldn't have to move away to find opportunity.
_**That there is more that unites us than divides us.**_
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/2e8a37d6-a56f-4446-89da-cce446501a0c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Details on the Clothing Drive for the Community Clothing Center in Clairfield:**
* **When:** July 21 - August 8
* **Where:** Campaign Headquarters (Printshop Beer Co: 1532 Island Home Avenue, Mondays - Thursdays from 10 to 4) _**plus any Michaela for Tennessee campaign event from July 21 - August 8!**_
* **Condition:** Gently used (no stained, dirty, or torn items)
* **Sizes:** All children's sizes, kindergarten through young adult

**Most-needed items:**
* Jeans & pants
* T-shirts, long-sleeve shirts, sweaters
* Shorts & leggings
* Jackets & coats
* Shoes & sneakers
* Backpacks & purses

Questions? Reply to this email, or reach out to [cavalry@michaelafortennessee.com](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1cf972b2-b2ff-409a-9798-db6be4d8c8e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

name: Governor Katie Hobbs
subject: My MAGA opponent
body:
[ ](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260722-1.twbMjE&refcode=em-20260722-1&t=1&akid=1645%2E1086043%2Et9QFiH)
Peter,
**I will officially face off against MAGA extremist Andy Biggs in the general election this November.**
**[Rush a split donation of $5 between me and Wes Moore to kickstart our re-election campaign as we enter the final chapter of this toss-up race.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260722-1.twbMjE&refcode=em-20260722-1&t=2&akid=1645%2E1086043%2Et9QFiH)**
If you don’t know who Biggs is, he is nearly identical to my 2022 opponent, Kari Lake, who we narrowly defeated by less than 1 percent of the vote.
He’s denied the 2020 election results and pushed bogus conspiracy theories, he’s attacked our reproductive rights, and he’s loyally supported every part of the MAGA agenda that’s actively hurting Arizona’s working families.
We’re not surprised Biggs won this primary -- **he was hand-picked by Donald Trump and backed by far-right groups like Turning Point USA** long before he became the official Republican nominee for governor.
Now, _the full force of the Republican machine_ will rapidly pour their resources from millionaires, billionaires, and super PACs into this race in an attempt to defeat me and flip Arizona ahead of the 2028 presidential election.
My mission while running for re-election is two-fold: to prevent a far-right election denier and Trump loyalist from taking power and wreaking havoc in Arizona, and to keep delivering lower costs and better outcomes for ALL Arizonans.
But if 2022 taught me anything, it’s that I need people like you in my corner if I’m going to win and defend Arizona from Biggs, Trump, and MAGA. **We won by 17,117 votes last time around, and we can expect this November’s election to be just as close.**
**[That’s why I’m urgently asking: will you pitch in ANY amount to me and Wes Moore to power our campaigns to victory between now and November 3rd?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260722-1.twbMjE&refcode=em-20260722-1&t=3&akid=1645%2E1086043%2Et9QFiH)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260722-1.twbMjE&amount=5&refcode=em-20260722-1&t=22&akid=1645%2E1086043%2Et9QFiH)**
I can’t thank you enough. Let’s go WIN!
-- Katie Hobbs

subject: The numbers Ohio didn’t want you to see 👀
body:
It took reporters digging through state records to find this.| | | |
---
| | | Hi Peter, I want to show you a number, and then I want to show you how I found out about it. Google, Meta, and Amazon each just locked in $600 million in sales tax exemptions from the state of Ohio... **EACH** ... good for up to 40 years. Add it up across all the companies getting in on this, and Ohio's on the hook for at least $2.3 billion. And that number's uncapped, so it can climb higher. In exchange, most of these facilities have committed to about 30 permanent jobs each. You read that right, not 30,000. **THIRTY**. Plus, nobody voted on this. These deals were signed under the Kasich administration, and the numbers stayed buried until reporters had to go dig them out of state records this year. When the Tax Department finally admitted what it was really costing us, the number was [$1.6 billion lost in 2025 alone](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135772097/635283302/1238660529?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ0OTEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNjFjYWY3YzUtZGQ4NS1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=xv3lGa2bz2f3Lsq9dS8LkYFWkD8yuuv6_QJdlmfs5lk=&emci=d8989faf-2085-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=61caf7c5-dd85-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=2142258)... a lot more than what the state told us to expect. I don't think most Ohioans are against companies investing here. But I think most Ohioans would like to know when their state signs away a billion dollars. The State Treasurer doesn't write tax law and can't undo these contracts, I'm not going to stand here and tell you otherwise. But the Treasurer's office**DOES** have a legal duty to look out for how the state's money is handled, and that includes saying something when a deal this size gets kept _this_ quiet. That's the kind of Treasurer I'm running to be. Transparent by default, not by lawsuit. Your investment in our campaign is an investment in a more transparent Ohio government. **Click[HERE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135772098/635283303/-1215145462?refcode=721em&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ0OTEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNjFjYWY3YzUtZGQ4NS1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=xv3lGa2bz2f3Lsq9dS8LkYFWkD8yuuv6_QJdlmfs5lk=) to chip in**! https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sethforohioweb?refcode=721em Thanks for reading this far,

The week in Mississippi, from The Mississippi Wire. https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/zvj5r2wea5?e=5703353baa

TheMISSISSIPPI WIRE
Latest News, Greatest State

Wednesday, July 22, 2026 A Publication of the
Mississippi Center for Public Policy MississippiWire.News

NEWS
Bertha Brings Tropical Storm Warning to All Three Coast Counties (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=bertha-brings-tropical-storm-warning-to-all-three-coast-counties)
The National Weather Service placed Hancock, Harrison, and Jackson counties under a tropical storm warning as Bertha pushes along the Gulf Coast with 50 mph winds.
Continue reading → (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=bertha-brings-tropical-storm-warning-to-all-three-coast-counties)
Scholarship Tax Credit will be big news for Mississippi (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=scholarship-tax-credit-will-be-big-news-for-mississippi)
Mississippi has opted into the new federal scholarship tax credit, which from 2027 will let taxpayers send up to $1,700 of their federal taxes to organizations funding scholarships at local schools.
Read → (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=scholarship-tax-credit-will-be-big-news-for-mississippi)
Former Sen. John Polk of Hattiesburg Dies at 77 (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=former-sen-john-polk-of-hattiesburg-dies-at-77)
The Hattiesburg Republican served 14 years in the state Senate, chairing the Business and Financial Institutions Committee and serving as vice chair of Appropriations.
Read → (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=former-sen-john-polk-of-hattiesburg-dies-at-77)
Reeves Asks Trump to Declare Disaster for Eight Counties Hit by Tropical Storm Arthur (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=reeves-asks-trump-to-declare-disaster-for-eight-counties-hit-by-tropical-storm-a)
Gov. Tate Reeves has asked President Trump to issue a Major Disaster Declaration for eight Mississippi counties battered by the remnants of Tropical Storm Arthur in June, opening the door to federal aid for storm-hit families and local governments.
Read → (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=reeves-asks-trump-to-declare-disaster-for-eight-counties-hit-by-tropical-storm-a)
Local News
Digital Tax Collections Up Roughly $600,000, Mayor Tells Council TUPELO — Mayor Todd Jordan told the city council that internet use-tax collections are up about $600,000 this year, and a Barnes Crossing drainage project came in about $400,000 under budget. (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=digital-tax-collections-up-roughly-600-000-mayor-tells-council) Aluminum Dynamics Adds $200 Million and 100 Jobs in the Golden Triangle LOWNDES — The company behind what was Mississippi’s largest-ever economic development commitment is expanding again in Lowndes County, Gov. Tate Reeves announced Tuesday. (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=aluminum-dynamics-adds-200-million-and-100-jobs-in-the-golden-triangle) Legislature Returns for Special Session on Expired Youth Court Laws JACKSON — Gov. Tate Reeves has called lawmakers back to Jackson at 3 p.m. Wednesday to replace youth court confidentiality statutes that lapsed June 30, after the state Supreme Court stepped in to revive
them. (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=legislature-returns-for-special-session-on-expired-youth-court-laws)

Schools
Mississippi Teachers Get $748 Each for Classroom Supplies, Delivered by Digital Wallet (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=mississippi-teachers-get-748-each-for-classroom-supplies-delivered-by-digital-wa)
State Education Enhancement Funds reach districts Wednesday. For the first time the money moves through ClassWallet, a digital platform that tracks spending and collects receipts automatically.
Read → (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=mississippi-teachers-get-748-each-for-classroom-supplies-delivered-by-digital-wa)
National
As a Trump tariff expires, a new one takes its place (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=as-a-trump-tariff-expires-a-new-one-takes-its-place)
Read → (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=as-a-trump-tariff-expires-a-new-one-takes-its-place)
Trump highlights election integrity threats, accuses China of meddling (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=trump-highlights-election-integrity-threats-accuses-china-of-meddling)
In a primetime address Thursday, President Donald Trump highlighted the need for election integrity while accusing China of meddling in U.S.
Read → (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=trump-highlights-election-integrity-threats-accuses-china-of-meddling)
Opinion
I Care for a Medically Complex Child. That’s Why I Want the Fraud Rooted Out. (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=i-care-for-a-medically-complex-child-that-s-why-i-want-the-fraud-rooted-out)
Read → (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=i-care-for-a-medically-complex-child-that-s-why-i-want-the-fraud-rooted-out)
They wrote Mississippi off. Today we're thriving. (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=they-wrote-mississippi-off-today-we-re-thriving)
$79 billion invested since 2020. xAI, Amazon and Aluminum Dynamics chose Mississippi over anywhere on earth. What changed was never the soil — it was the rules we chose to live by.
Read → (https://mississippiwire.news/article.html?slug=they-wrote-mississippi-off-today-we-re-thriving)

President Donald Trump and the USPS Board of Governors named former Waste Management CEO David Steiner to lead the Postal Service. Steiner was most recently the lead independent director at FedEx, a USPS competitor.
Brian Renfroe, president of the National Association of Letter Carriers — a union representing nearly 300,000 active and retired letter carriers — called the decision to place Steiner at the head of the USPS " an aggressive step toward handing America's mail system over to corporate interests ."

Friend, Route 66 just turned 100.
For generations, it's been more than just a highway. It's the iconic diners and neon signs. The mom-and-pop businesses. The roadside attractions. The memories made with the windows down and New Mexico stretching out ahead. For 100 years, Route 66 has connected our communities and helped tell the story of our state. It reminds us that no matter where you're headed, the people you meet along the way matter most.
**_Today, we're celebrating that incredible history and what comes next._**

The next chapter of New Mexico's story should be one where working families can afford to get ahead, every child has access to a great education, small businesses have the opportunity to succeed, and every community can thrive.

body:

Hi Peter — Mark Jacob here, contributor at COURIER.

Prediction markets are perfect examples of how Donald Trump and the
oligarchs who conspire with him are building a nation of chumps, a society
of suckers.

They're online betting parlors by another name, and they're notoriously
vulnerable to insider trading. Trump wants his own agency to have
exclusive authority over them, with no regulation by the states. His
eldest son has financial ties to the top two. And CNBC and CNN both have
financial deals to promote Kalshi while treating its numbers as news.

I wrote this week about the insider bets, the fake influencer wins, and
the networks getting paid.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1003&refcode=20260722_MJ&akid=168%2E344797%2EFsqwx8 ]Before you read on, I hope you'll consider supporting COURIER. When the
biggest business networks are taking money from the companies they cover,
independent journalism is what's left.

Thanks for reading,
Mark Jacob
COURIER Contributor

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1004&refcode=20260722_MJ&akid=168%2E344797%2EFsqwx8 ][IMG]

Trump and prediction markets are building a society of suckers
The convicted felon in the White House loves shadowy financial schemes
that benefit insiders
By Mark Jacob

Prediction markets are perfect examples of how Donald Trump and the
oligarchs who conspire with him are building a nation of chumps, a society
of suckers.

These markets are online betting parlors by another name. They allow
people to wager on a wide variety of questions, from "Next prime minister
of Ethiopia?" to "Where will 'Janice STFU' by Drake rank on the Billboard
Hot 100 chart dated Aug 1, 2026?"

Prediction markets are sometimes described as a testament to "the wisdom
of crowds," but such wisdom has its limits. The markets are notoriously
vulnerable to insider trading, which means people who control events or
have private knowledge of what will happen can make a killing.

Trump, who loves gray-area, funny-money opportunities like cryptocurrency
and prediction markets, has made his position clear. He wants his
Commodity Futures Trading Commission to have "exclusive authority" over
prediction markets, with no regulation by the states. "We cannot have SCUM
like Chris Christie, Letitia James, Tim Walz, and JB Pritzker setting the
rules!" Trump wrote in May.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1005&refcode=20260722_MJ&akid=168%2E344797%2EFsqwx8 ]DONATE

Trump's CFTC chairman, Michael Selig, doesn't look like much of a
watchdog. This month, he praised prediction markets as "an interesting
hedging tool" that helps companies "manage risk." And the president's
eldest son, Donald Trump Jr., is a booster, too. He has financial ties to
the top two prediction markets, serving as an investor and unpaid adviser
for Polymarket and a paid adviser for Kalshi.

Major news media are also in cahoots. CNBC and CNN treat Kalshi's numbers
as if they're news, and both have financial deals to promote the company.
CNBC sometimes fails to disclose that relationship when reporting on
Kalshi, according to an excellent report by Aaron Rupar and Judd Legum.
CNBC says it discloses its financial link only when it is "directly
relevant to the story."

CNN's deal with Kalshi is exclusive, which means CNN can't cite other
prediction markets in its coverage, a network source told The New Yorker.
If the coverage of Kalshi's wagers were actually news instead of just
sneaky product placement, why wouldn't CNN occasionally cite other
prediction markets, too?

While CNBC and CNN continue this gross perversion of their journalistic
mission, other news outlets are doing fine jobs of exposing the ways these
markets make our country more dishonest and exploitative. Among the most
damning reports:

* About 0.1% of accounts on Polymarket collect about two-thirds of the
profits, according to a Wall Street Journal analysis.
* In a stunningly dodgy tactic, Polymarket created "clone" sites on
which social media influencers made fake bets before posting videos
claiming they had turned $500 into $100,000.
* The Associated Press reported that a group of new accounts on
Polymarket made highly specific, well-timed bets on whether the U.S.
and Iran would reach a ceasefire on April 7, resulting in hundreds of
thousands of dollars in profits. At least 50 accounts placed
substantial "Yes" bets before Trump announced the ceasefire on Truth
Social at around 6:30 pm ET. These were the first bets made by those
wallets.
* Some prediction markets let people bet on wildfires. Experts are
sounding the alarm, CNN reports, fearing it risks incentivizing arson.
* Kalshi will soon begin taking bets on the outcomes of clinical drug
trials. Nothing bad could come from that, right?
* Trump's teleprompter operator is suspected of using his inside
knowledge to win more than $100,000 betting on Kalshi about what the
president would say in his major speeches.
* Spotify removed about 500,000 streams from Malcolm Todd's song
"Earrings" after its strong performance on the charts was linked to
manipulation tied to Kalshi bets.
* Polymarket pays "influencers" to insert its product into social media
conversations. Among them: former Politico reporter Rachael Bade,
former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene, anti-trans activist Riley Gaines,
leftist commentator Brian Krassenstein, and right-wing podcaster Benny
Johnson (who was also funded by Russia, supposedly without his
knowledge).
* Billionaire Peter Thiel, the money man behind JD Vance's political
career, is a major investor in Polymarket.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1006&refcode=20260722_MJ&akid=168%2E344797%2EFsqwx8 ]DONATE

The greed of Team Trump and the mainstream media have empowered prediction
markets to separate many people from their money while allowing a few to
quietly profit from dodgy schemes.

CNBC and CNN aren't the only media companies with prediction market ties.
Polymarket has a partnership with Dow Jones, publisher of the Wall Street
Journal, though it must be said that some of the most negative stories
about prediction markets have appeared in the WSJ.

Polymarket also has a cooperation agreement with Substack, the publishing
platform for this newsletter, which is sponsored by COURIER Newsroom. I
have had no dealings with any prediction market and pledge to never take
their money.

If you see a journalist or influencer posting positively about a
prediction market on social media, ask them in the comments whether they
have any financial ties. I have done that myself and aim to do it more
often.

Prediction markets, as currently operated, stink to high heaven.
