Residents and local landscapers--many of whom also live in New Canaan--raised concerns about inconsistencies in the ordinance, unequal treatment of homeowners, landscapers and municipal workers, enforcement questions, and the limited time provided for implementation. In response, more than 1,000 registered voters signed a petition requesting a townwide referendum. While serving on the Greenwich RTM Health and Human Services Committee , I reviewed many of these same issues. As a physician, I believe environmental concerns and excessive noise should be considered. But public health also includes the health and safety of the workers doing this physically demanding job every day. Important concerns include the weight of some commercial battery-powered equipment, worker ergonomics, orthopedic injury risks, battery life, charging limitations, costs for small businesses, and whether some electric blowers are actually quieter than comparable gas models. There is also a basic fairness problem. Homeowners, landscapers and municipal workers should not be treated differently without a clear and practical justification. Property size also matters. In more densely populated areas the noise from your neighbor's leaf blowing is potentially more disruptive than in areas of two acre or more zoning. Larger properties also need more powerful machines. Even in my town of Greenwich, where we have a stricter ordinance regarding gas blowers, in the fall we allow the 2 acre and larger lots to begin using gas powered blowers almost a month earlier than the rest of the town. For those reasons, I encourage New Canaan residents to Vote No. A No vote is not a vote against cleaner technology or quieter neighborhoods. It is a vote against an inconsistent ordinance as currently written and an opportunity for the Town to develop a fairer, more practical policy. A better ordinance could consider actual sound levels, limited hours of operation, property size, worker safety, realistic transition periods and reasonable exemptions applied consistently. Burdening the police department with enforcement will either distract them from more essential services or requiring the hiring of additional of police officers. Vote Residents who will be away on Saturday should vote by absentee ballot through the Town Clerk 's Office. Eligible voters may vote in person or designate a family member to pick up and return their completed absentee ballot. There are no evening absentee voting hours for this referendum. Important Dates Wednesday, July 22: 8:00 AM-3:00 PM Thursday, July 23: 8:00 AM-3:00 PM Friday, July 24: 8:00 AM-1:00 PM Referendum Day Saturday, July 25 10:00 AM -8:00 PM New Canaan High School Vote No because the ordinance, as written, is inconsistent, unfair and was implemented without enough time for residents and local businesses to adapt. Your vote is your voice. Please encourage your family, friends and neighbors to vote as well.** Thanks for reading The Goldstein Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work. # The attacks on Drop Site News are intensifying
### The threats keep coming. We keep publishing.
| | | [Drop Site News](https://substack.com/@dropsitenews)
---
| Jul 22
---
| [](https://substack.com/@dropsitenews)
---
The attacks on Drop Site News keep coming. And every one of them is a confession.
After we reported that Iran privately warned JD Vance that Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff were exploiting their access to the Gaza negotiations for financial gain, the White House didn't dispute a single detail in our story. Instead, it said our reporters are so "filled with hate for America" that they've become "full-throated propagandists for the Iranian regime." Former IDF soldiers turned social media operatives continue tagging DOJ officials, demanding investigations into Drop Site, and smearing our brave correspondents in Gaza, Iran, and Lebanon, marking them as targets for a genocidal government that keeps murdering journalists. Pro-Israel operatives, political figures, and influencers across both parties keep amplifying those calls. Meanwhile, lawyers representing a BBC editor we exposed are still in court, betting that if they drag this out long enough, we'll go broke and give up.
**We refuse.** This newsroom belongs to the readers who fund it, and we're asking those readers to step up right now.
Those behind these attacks are betting that readers like you won't show up. Let's prove them wrong. For less than $0.25 a day, you become part of the community that makes this newsroom impossible to intimidate, impossible to exhaust, and impossible to silence.
**[Upgrade to a paid subscription today, and for the next 48 hours, it 's 20% off.](https://substack.com/redirect/d49443d9-ee0d-4e82-a04d-c22de4bec18f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[UPGRADE TODAY - 20% OFF](https://substack.com/redirect/d49443d9-ee0d-4e82-a04d-c22de4bec18f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
#### **They Don 't Come After Newsrooms That Aren't Winning**
Understand what these attacks actually are. They are an admission that our reporting is having a serious impact.
JD Vance did respond to our reporting on Kushner and Witkoff, though "respond" is generous. He called the story "completely bogus," said "no one has done more" for "peace and prosperity in the region" than the two of them, and dismissed the idea they might be profiting off their access as "absurd" because, in his words, they're "good dudes." Notice what's missing from all of that: an actual rebuttal. Not one fact, document, or detail in our reporting was disputed. "Good dudes" is a character reference, not a fact check, and this is a White House that has never let the truth get in the way of a talking point.
The same pattern is playing out at a much larger scale. Last week, Secretary of State Marco Rubio held a summit on what his State Department is calling "political terrorism." Days later, Ken Klippenstein exposed a State Department report naming journalists, organizations, and activists as extensions of a supposed foreign "campaign of subversion against the United States." In substance, it's a government blacklist, and it tells us exactly who they intend to keep targeting.
Drop Site reporters have been bravely reporting on the ground in Gaza throughout the most sweeping assassination campaign against journalists in modern history. We are currently reporting from Iran and Lebanon as the war intensifies. Our team just sat down with Congressman Ro Khanna for a candid interview following his trip to the occupied West Bank, and our correspondents continue filing from Gaza and the West Bank on stories corporate newsrooms won't touch.
That is not the profile of a newsroom that powerful people ignore. **That is the profile of a newsroom that scares them**. Every reader who upgrades is making a direct statement: these attacks don't work.
You can make that statement right now. [Can you support our work by becoming a paid subscriber today?](https://substack.com/redirect/d49443d9-ee0d-4e82-a04d-c22de4bec18f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[SUPPORT DROP SITE - 20% OFF](https://substack.com/redirect/d49443d9-ee0d-4e82-a04d-c22de4bec18f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
#### **What Reader-Funded Actually Means**
Drop Site was built on a simple premise: journalism that answers to no one but our readers. No corporate owners. No billionaire backers deciding which stories are safe to publish. No advertisers or foundations whose interests shape what we cover.
That model is powerful. It's also the model they're trying to break.
The attacks will keep coming. The legal threats, the coordinated smear campaigns, the calls for government investigation will escalate as long as we keep doing work that matters. The only question is whether this newsroom has the reader base to absorb every punch and keep publishing.
The answer to all of it is the same: a bigger, stronger, more committed reader community. Every paid subscriber is a vote that this model survives. Every upgrade from free to paid is a direct investment in the ability of this newsroom to keep doing work that is clearly, demonstrably making people in power uncomfortable.
**[For the next 48 hours, we 're offering 20% off an annual subscription. That's less than $0.25 a day to fund reporting the White House, the State Department, and a coordinated harassment campaign are all actively trying to stop.](https://substack.com/redirect/d49443d9-ee0d-4e82-a04d-c22de4bec18f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The institutions and governments threatened by honest, independent journalism have far more resources than we do. The only asymmetric advantage we have is you.
When the White House attacks us, we publish the attack and keep reporting. When lawyers come after our journalists, our readers fund the defense. When coordinated campaigns try to paint our correspondents as something other than what they are, we stand behind them publicly and without hesitation. We answer to no one but our readers and supporters. [Become one of them today.](https://substack.com/redirect/d49443d9-ee0d-4e82-a04d-c22de4bec18f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[UPGRADE NOW - SUPPORT OUR WORK](https://substack.com/redirect/d49443d9-ee0d-4e82-a04d-c22de4bec18f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The attacks tell us we're doing something right. Your support tells us we can keep doing it.
-Drop Site News
_P.S. If a paid subscription isn 't possible right now, we understand -- and our commitment to keeping all of our reporting free never wavers. But if you can, today is the day. And if a subscription isn't the right fit, [a one-time tax-deductible donation of any amount goes directly into the journalism](https://substack.com/redirect/37a05745-a396-4f47-b9b1-691f2d875c8d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Every dollar counts. We're just getting started, and we need you with us for year 3._

NEW: Donald Trump’s administration is attempting to skirt the law and weaken restrictions on hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) — a category of extremely powerful greenhouse gas. The administration is breaking the law — so I’m suing.
The science is clear that we should be reducing our reliance on these super-pollutants, not easing the rules meant to tackle this crisis head-on.
But that’s exactly what Trump’s EPA is attempting to do by weakening rules that phase out the use of HFCs.
Once again, the Trump administration is attacking our critical environmental safeguards while communities across the country are left to deal with the consequences. It’s wrong and illegal — so once again, I’m taking them to court.
If that’s all you need to hear, click here to support our work holding Trump accountable before the end of the month. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
Our planet is giving us clear warning signs that we’re approaching a dangerous climate tipping point. And right now, all across the country, communities are enduring extreme temperatures and devastating floods and wildfires — including here in California, where so many of us have seen firsthand the impacts of this crisis.
HFCs are some of the most powerful and fastest-growing sources of greenhouse gas emissions driving the climate crisis, yet the Trump administration wants to weaken the safeguards that would phase out these chemicals.
This administration wants to ignore our responsibility to protect our environment and our people, but we won’t. We will continue to confront the climate crisis head-on, fight for our planet and communities, and hold this administration accountable to the rule of law.

Team, This morning, I announced that I was leading a group of Democratic veterans in Congress to press House leadership to bring an Iran War Powers Resolution to the floor for a vote this week. # The Silent Renaissance of Brownfield Redevelopment in Urban Core Markets
Forget the shiny new glass towers dominating the skyline; the real institutional money is currently digging through the literal dirt of 20th-century industrial decay. While high interest rates have stalled traditional commercial construction, a specific subset of developers is quietly turning contaminated legacy sites into high-yield, mixed-use gold mines. This is not just gentrification; it is a complex intersection of environmental remediation tax credits, zoning arbitrage, and the sheer scarcity of developable land in Tier-1 metropolitan areas. Investors are realizing that the most profitable path forward often involves cleaning up the past. By leveraging federal brownfield grants and state-level tax incentives, these firms are effectively lowering their cost basis to a point that makes new construction projects look like a rounding error. It is a game of patience, regulatory navigation, and capital allocation that rewards those willing to deal with the grit of urban reclamation rather than the ease of greenfield suburban development.

The Economics of Remediation Arbitrage
The fundamental thesis here is simple: land value is suppressed by environmental stigma, but the utility of the location remains hyper-competitive. When a developer acquires a site formerly used for manufacturing or fuel storage, they are not just buying dirt; they are buying a liability they know how to manage. The delta between the acquisition cost of a blighted lot and the valuation of a stabilized, high-density asset at completion is the engine driving this niche. Financial modeling for these projects requires a deep dive into the specialized insurance markets for environmental risk. Developers often purchase 'pollution legal liability' policies that cap their exposure to unknown subsurface contaminants. This shifts the risk profile from speculative to operational, allowing the project to pencil out even in a high-cost capital environment. By treating soil remediation as a construction line item rather than a catastrophic risk, these firms are unlocking value that has been trapped for decades.
Institutional capital has caught on, with private equity funds creating dedicated vehicles to handle the multi-year cycle of remediation and entitlement. These funds prioritize sites with excellent transit connectivity, where the end-product will benefit from the 'location premium' that defines modern urban real estate. It is a sophisticated play that relies on the belief that demand for city-center living will outlast the temporary headwinds of current interest rate regimes. Consider the case of the Navy Yard in Philadelphia or the Meatpacking District in New York; these were once industrial wastelands that now command some of the highest rents in the country. The transition from industrial relic to economic engine requires a surgical approach to risk management that the broader market consistently underestimates.
Navigating the Regulatory Labyrinth
Redevelopment is as much about legal prowess as it is about engineering. Federal programs like the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act, better known as CERCLA, create the framework, but state agencies often hold the keys to the kingdom. Success requires a mastery of Voluntary Cleanup Programs that allow developers to achieve 'no further action' letters, effectively clearing the site for residential or commercial use. This is not a quick flip. The entitlement phase alone can take 24 to 36 months, requiring a developer to balance carrying costs with the promise of future yield. Smart investors are utilizing bridge financing that specifically accounts for these long lead times, often structuring deals with flexible maturity dates tied to environmental milestones rather than simple calendar dates.

Local municipal governments are often desperate for these projects. They trade density bonuses and tax abatements for the promise of a cleaned-up neighborhood and an expanded tax base. This creates a powerful alignment of interests where the city, the developer, and the future tenants all win, provided the execution remains disciplined and the engineering data is sound. Developers who successfully navigate this labyrinth often find themselves with a massive competitive advantage, as the barriers to entry—legal, technical, and financial—keep the amateur investors entirely at bay.
The Technology Behind the Dirt
Modern environmental engineering has changed the math on what constitutes a 'dirty' site. Advanced soil testing and non-intrusive geophysical mapping allow developers to pinpoint contamination with incredible precision. Rather than excavating an entire ten-acre site, they can employ in-situ remediation techniques, like injecting proprietary chemical oxidants into the groundwater, to neutralize contaminants in place. This technology has drastically reduced the cost and time required to achieve regulatory closure. In the past, the only option was 'dig and dump,' which was prohibitively expensive due to the cost of transporting hazardous waste to specialized landfills. Today, the ability to treat the site on-site keeps the project budget under control and moves the timeline forward at a faster clip.
Data analytics play a massive role as well. By cross-referencing historical insurance maps from the early 1900s with current satellite imagery and local building permit histories, developers can build a high-probability model of what lies beneath the surface. This predictive modeling allows them to make more aggressive bids on property auctions before their competitors have even finished their initial site survey. The shift toward digital twins and 3D modeling for subterranean conditions is becoming standard practice among elite firms. These tools allow developers to simulate the flow of groundwater and the potential migration of contaminants, offering a level of certainty that was unthinkable just a decade ago.
Market Dynamics and Scarcity
Why focus on brownfields now? The answer is one word: scarcity. There are no more 'easy' plots of land in major American cities. Every remaining parcel has a history, a constraint, or a challenge that keeps the average developer away. This lack of competition is the ultimate moat. While the broader real estate market is fixated on the volatility of office cap rates, these specialized developers are operating in a less efficient market where they set the terms. Furthermore, the shift toward ESG-focused investment mandates is funneling massive amounts of institutional capital toward these projects. Large pension funds are under pressure to show that their capital is doing 'good' as well as earning a return. Cleaning up an abandoned warehouse and turning it into affordable housing or a high-tech lab space checks every box in the modern institutional portfolio.
This creates a floor on valuation. Even in a market downturn, a well-entrenched urban asset in a prime location with a clean environmental certification will always find a buyer or a tenant. The intrinsic value of the location combined with the de-risking of the land itself makes these assets highly resilient to macro-economic shocks. As suburban greenfield development faces increasing scrutiny from regulators and environmentalists, the focus has swung back toward the urban core. This is not just a trend; it is a fundamental shift in how we value urban space.
The Multi-Layered Capital Stack
Financing these deals requires a nuanced understanding of the capital stack. You have the senior debt, which is increasingly provided by regional banks looking for impact-focused lending opportunities. Then you have the mezzanine layer, often filled by private credit firms that specialize in transitional real estate. Finally, you have the equity, which is where the real upside lies. Many of these projects are structured as joint ventures between a local developer, who brings the site-specific expertise and political connections, and a larger institutional partner, who brings the scale and cost of capital. This marriage of local grit and global liquidity is the winning formula. It allows for the complexity of the project to be managed by someone on the ground while the financing is handled by those who understand the macro environment.
It is also worth considering the role of tax increment financing. By capturing the future property tax revenue increases generated by the project, developers can often fund a significant portion of the public infrastructure improvements required, such as roads, utilities, and public spaces. This reduces the total capital burden on the private equity investors and improves the overall internal rate of return for the project. For the sophisticated investor, the capital stack is a puzzle where every piece serves a specific purpose, from managing tax liabilities to hedging against interest rate swings.
The Role of Adaptive Reuse
While complete redevelopment is the gold standard, adaptive reuse of existing structures is gaining traction. Many industrial sites contain brick-and-mortar shells that are structurally sound and aesthetically desirable. Retrofitting these structures for modern use, like lofts, coworking spaces, or data centers, preserves the embodied carbon and reduces the construction timeline. Adaptive reuse is often more capital efficient than new builds, provided the structural integrity is verified. It also allows developers to bypass some of the more rigorous zoning hurdles because they are maintaining the existing building footprint. The challenge is in the mechanical, electrical, and plumbing upgrades required to bring these antique structures into the 21st century.
Yet, the market premium for 'authentic' space is growing. Tech companies and creative firms are willing to pay a rent premium for spaces that have a story and a character that a generic, new-build office block simply cannot provide. This creates a sustainable competitive advantage for developers who specialize in blending the old with the new. We are seeing a surge in demand for 'industrial chic' office environments that leverage natural light and open floor plans, which were originally designed for factory work but perfectly suit modern collaboration.
Strategic Risk Mitigation and Insurance
No discussion of brownfield development is complete without addressing the risk of litigation. Third-party liability claims can derail even the best-planned projects. This is why the legal strategy around site acquisition is as critical as the engineering plan. Using special purpose vehicles to hold each site separately protects the parent company and its other assets from potential unforeseen liabilities. Furthermore, the developers who thrive in this space are those who maintain a long-term, transparent relationship with local environmental regulators. They do not try to hide issues; they bring them to the table, present a remediation plan, and execute it with precision. This builds a reputation of competence that makes future projects easier to get approved.
Insurance products have evolved to meet this demand. We are seeing the rise of 'environmental impairment liability' insurance that specifically covers projects during the remediation phase. These policies are essential for securing institutional financing, as they remove the 'unknowns' that keep committees awake at night. By transferring the risk to an insurance pool, the developer can focus on the core mission of transforming the asset. In a market where many investors are paralyzed by the ambiguity of future interest rates, these firms are doubling down on the one constant they can control: the physical ground beneath their feet. By turning a liability into an asset, they are not just building real estate; they are building a hedge against the unpredictability of the broader economy. The future of urban growth is not in new territory, but in the smart reclamation of the old. Look for this trend to dominate urban planning agendas for the next two decades, as cities realize that density is their only path to fiscal health.

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. Investors are realizing that the most profitable path forward often involves cleaning up the past. By leveraging federal brownfield grants and state-level tax incentives, these firms are effectively lowering their cost basis to a point that makes new construction projects look like a rounding error. It is a game of patience, regulatory navigation, and capital allocation that rewards those willing to deal with the grit of urban reclamation rather than the ease of greenfield suburban development. | 📊 Did you know The EPA estimates that there are over 450,000 brownfield sites across the United States, with recent data showing that every dollar of public funding leverages approximately $18 in private investment. The Economics of Remediation Arbitrage The fundamental thesis here is simple: land value is suppressed by environmental stigma, but the utility of the location remains hyper-competitive. When a developer acquires a site formerly used for manufacturing or fuel storage, they are not just buying dirt; they are buying a liability they know how to manage. The delta between the acquisition cost of a blighted lot and the valuation of a stabilized, high-density asset at completion is the engine driving this niche. Financial modeling for these projects requires a deep dive into the specialized insurance markets for environmental risk. Developers often purchase 'pollution legal liability' policies that cap their exposure to unknown subsurface contaminants. This shifts the risk profile from speculative to operational, allowing the project to pencil out even in a high-cost capital environment. By treating soil remediation as a construction line item rather than a catastrophic risk, these firms are unlocking value that has been trapped for decades. Institutional capital has caught on, with private equity funds creating dedicated vehicles to handle the multi-year cycle of remediation and entitlement. These funds prioritize sites with excellent transit connectivity, where the end-product will benefit from the 'location premium' that defines modern urban real estate. It is a sophisticated play that relies on the belief that demand for city-center living will outlast the temporary headwinds of current interest rate regimes. Consider the case of the Navy Yard in Philadelphia or the Meatpacking District in New York; these were once industrial wastelands that now command some of the highest rents in the country. The transition from industrial relic to economic engine requires a surgical approach to risk management that the broader market consistently underestimates. Navigating the Regulatory Labyrinth Redevelopment is as much about legal prowess as it is about engineering. Federal programs like the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act, better known as CERCLA, create the framework, but state agencies often hold the keys to the kingdom. Success requires a mastery of Voluntary Cleanup Programs that allow developers to achieve 'no further action' letters, effectively clearing the site for residential or commercial use. This is not a quick flip. The entitlement phase alone can take 24 to 36 months, requiring a developer to balance carrying costs with the promise of future yield. Smart investors are utilizing bridge financing that specifically accounts for these long lead times, often structuring deals with flexible maturity dates tied to environmental milestones rather than simple calendar dates. | "The transition from industrial relic to economic engine requires a surgical approach to risk management that the broader market consistently underestimates." — Elena Vance, Managing Director of Urban Redevelopment Capital Local municipal governments are often desperate for these projects. They trade density bonuses and tax abatements for the promise of a cleaned-up neighborhood and an expanded tax base. This creates a powerful alignment of interests where the city, the developer, and the future tenants all win, provided the execution remains disciplined and the engineering data is sound. Developers who successfully navigate this labyrinth often find themselves with a massive competitive advantage, as the barriers to entry—legal, technical, and financial—keep the amateur investors entirely at bay. The Technology Behind the Dirt Modern environmental engineering has changed the math on what constitutes a 'dirty' site. Advanced soil testing and non-intrusive geophysical mapping allow developers to pinpoint contamination with incredible precision. Rather than excavating an entire ten-acre site, they can employ in-situ remediation techniques, like injecting proprietary chemical oxidants into the groundwater, to neutralize contaminants in place. This technology has drastically reduced the cost and time required to achieve regulatory closure. In the past, the only option was 'dig and dump,' which was prohibitively expensive due to the cost of transporting hazardous waste to specialized landfills. Today, the ability to treat the site on-site keeps the project budget under control and moves the timeline forward at a faster clip. Data analytics play a massive role as well. By cross-referencing historical insurance maps from the early 1900s with current satellite imagery and local building permit histories, developers can build a high-probability model of what lies beneath the surface. This predictive modeling allows them to make more aggressive bids on property auctions before their competitors have even finished their initial site survey. The shift toward digital twins and 3D modeling for subterranean conditions is becoming standard practice among elite firms. These tools allow developers to simulate the flow of groundwater and the potential migration of contaminants, offering a level of certainty that was unthinkable just a decade ago. Market Dynamics and Scarcity Why focus on brownfields now? The answer is one word: scarcity. There are no more 'easy' plots of land in major American cities. Every remaining parcel has a history, a constraint, or a challenge that keeps the average developer away. This lack of competition is the ultimate moat. While the broader real estate market is fixated on the volatility of office cap rates, these specialized developers are operating in a less efficient market where they set the terms. Furthermore, the shift toward ESG-focused investment mandates is funneling massive amounts of institutional capital toward these projects. Large pension funds are under pressure to show that their capital is doing 'good' as well as earning a return. Cleaning up an abandoned warehouse and turning it into affordable housing or a high-tech lab space checks every box in the modern institutional portfolio. This creates a floor on valuation. Even in a market downturn, a well-entrenched urban asset in a prime location with a clean environmental certification will always find a buyer or a tenant. The intrinsic value of the location combined with the de-risking of the land itself makes these assets highly resilient to macro-economic shocks. As suburban greenfield development faces increasing scrutiny from regulators and environmentalists, the focus has swung back toward the urban core. This is not just a trend; it is a fundamental shift in how we value urban space. The Multi-Layered Capital Stack Financing these deals requires a nuanced understanding of the capital stack. You have the senior debt, which is increasingly provided by regional banks looking for impact-focused lending opportunities. Then you have the mezzanine layer, often filled by private credit firms that specialize in transitional real estate. Finally, you have the equity, which is where the real upside lies. Many of these projects are structured as joint ventures between a local developer, who brings the site-specific expertise and political connections, and a larger institutional partner, who brings the scale and cost of capital. This marriage of local grit and global liquidity is the winning formula. It allows for the complexity of the project to be managed by someone on the ground while the financing is handled by those who understand the macro environment. It is also worth considering the role of tax increment financing. By capturing the future property tax revenue increases generated by the project, developers can often fund a significant portion of the public infrastructure improvements required, such as roads, utilities, and public spaces. This reduces the total capital burden on the private equity investors and improves the overall internal rate of return for the project. For the sophisticated investor, the capital stack is a puzzle where every piece serves a specific purpose, from managing tax liabilities to hedging against interest rate swings. The Role of Adaptive Reuse While complete redevelopment is the gold standard, adaptive reuse of existing structures is gaining traction. Many industrial sites contain brick-and-mortar shells that are structurally sound and aesthetically desirable. Retrofitting these structures for modern use, like lofts, coworking spaces, or data centers, preserves the embodied carbon and reduces the construction timeline. Adaptive reuse is often more capital efficient than new builds, provided the structural integrity is verified. It also allows developers to bypass some of the more rigorous zoning hurdles because they are maintaining the existing building footprint. The challenge is in the mechanical, electrical, and plumbing upgrades required to bring these antique structures into the 21st century. Yet, the market premium for 'authentic' space is growing. Tech companies and creative firms are willing to pay a rent premium for spaces that have a story and a character that a generic, new-build office block simply cannot provide. This creates a sustainable competitive advantage for developers who specialize in blending the old with the new. We are seeing a surge in demand for 'industrial chic' office environments that leverage natural light and open floor plans, which were originally designed for factory work but perfectly suit modern collaboration. Strategic Risk Mitigation and Insurance No discussion of brownfield development is complete without addressing the risk of litigation. Third-party liability claims can derail even the best-planned projects. This is why the legal strategy around site acquisition is as critical as the engineering plan. Using special purpose vehicles to hold each site separately protects the parent company and its other assets from potential unforeseen liabilities. Furthermore, the developers who thrive in this space are those who maintain a long-term, transparent relationship with local environmental regulators. They do not try to hide issues; they bring them to the table, present a remediation plan, and execute it with precision. This builds a reputation of competence that makes future projects easier to get approved. Insurance products have evolved to meet this demand. We are seeing the rise of 'environmental impairment liability' insurance that specifically covers projects during the remediation phase. These policies are essential for securing institutional financing, as they remove the 'unknowns' that keep committees awake at night. By transferring the risk to an insurance pool, the developer can focus on the core mission of transforming the asset. In a market where many investors are paralyzed by the ambiguity of future interest rates, these firms are doubling down on the one constant they can control: the physical ground beneath their feet. By turning a liability into an asset, they are not just building real estate; they are building a hedge against the unpredictability of the broader economy. The future of urban growth is not in new territory, but in the smart reclamation of the old. Look for this trend to dominate urban planning agendas for the next two decades, as cities realize that density is their only path to fiscal health. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. Henry Award for his short story "The Man in the Black Suit".[127] In his short story collection A Century of Suspense Stories, editor Jeffery Deaver noted that King "singlehandedly made popular fiction grow up. While there were many good best-selling writers before him, King, more than anybody since John D. MacDonald, brought reality to genre novels. He has often remarked that 'Salem's Lot was "Peyton Place meets Dracula. And so it was. The rich characterization, the careful and caring social eye, the interplay of story line and character development announced that writers could take worn themes such as vampirism and make them fresh again. Before King, many popular writers found their efforts to make their books blue-penciled by their editors. 'Stuff like that gets in the way of the story,' they were told. Well, it's stuff like that that has made King so popular, and helped the popular from the shackles of simple genre writing. He is a master of masters."[128] In 2003, King was honored by the National Book Awards with a time achievement award, the Medal of Distinguished Contribution to American Letters. Some in the literary community expressed disapproval of the award: Richard E. Snyder, the former CEO of Simon & Schuster, described King's work as "non-literature" and critic Harold Bloom denounced the choice: The decision to give the National Book Foundation's annual award for "distinguished contribution" to Stephen King is extraordinary, another low in the shocking process of dumbing down our cultural . I've described King in the past as a writer of penny dreadfuls, but perhaps even that is too kind. He shares nothing with Edgar an Poe. What he is is an immensely inadequate writer on a sentence-by-sentence, paragraph-by-paragraph, book-by-book basis.[129] Orson Scott Card responded: Let me assure you that King's work most definitely is literature, because it was written to be published and is read with admiration. What Snyder rey means is that it is not the literature preferred by the academic-literary elite.[130] In 2008, King's book On Writing was ranked 21st on Entertainment Weekly's list of "The Classics: The 100 Best Reads from 1983 to 2008".[131] | Your daily brief on markets, macro, and risk. His father, Donald Ed King, a travelling vacuum salesman after returning from World War II,[10] was born in Indiana with the sur Pollock, changing it to King as an adult.[11][12][13] King's mother was Nellie Ruth King (née Pillsbury).[13] His parents were married in Scarborough, Maine on July 23, 1939.[14] Shortly afterwards, they lived with Donald's family in Chicago before moving to Croton-on-Hudson, York.[15] King's parents returned to Maine towards the end of World War II, living in a modest house in Scarborough. When King was two, his father left the family. His mother raised him and his older brother David by herself, sometimes under strain. They moved from Scarborough and depended on relatives in Chicago; Croton-on-Hudson; West De Pere, Wisconsin; Fort Wayne, Indiana; Malden, Massachusetts; and Stratford, Connecticut.[15][17] When King was 11, his family moved to Durham, Maine, where his mother cared for her parents until their deaths. She then became a caregiver in a local residential facility for the menty chenged.[1] King was raised Methodist,[18][19] but lost his belief in organized religion while in high school. While no longer religious, he says he chooses to believe in the existence of God.[20] As a child, King apparently witnessed one of his friends being struck and killed by a train, though he has no memory of the event. His family told him that after leaving to play with the boy, King returned speechless and seemingly in shock. later did the family learn of the death. Some commentators have suggested that this event may have psychologicy inspired some of King's darker works,[21] but King makes no mention of it in his memoir On Writing (2000). He related in detail his primary inspiration for writing horror fiction in his non-fiction Danse Macabre (1981), in a chapter titled "An Annoying Autobiographical Pause". He compared his uncle's dowsing for water using the bough of an apple branch with the sudden realization of what he wanted to do for a living. That inspiration occurred while browsing through an attic with his elder brother, when King uncovered a paperback version of an H. P. Lovecraft collection of short stories he remembers as The Lurker in the Shadows, that had belonged to his father. King told Barnes & Noble Studios in a 2009 interview, "I k that I'd found when I read that book."[22]

# [Trump just declared 100% war on cheap foreign generic drugs](https://substack.com/redirect/34920967-232f-45cc-9fb7-27a23c519a7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
President Donald Trump said in a social media post Tuesday that the United States plans to impose a **[100% tariff on imported generic drugs](https://substack.com/redirect/dec9042b-8ed4-4974-9f65-90f5f7786216?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** beginning in August 2028 to bring production back home.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/34920967-232f-45cc-9fb7-27a23c519a7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Rate doubles next year:** The levy would then double a year later to 200% in August 2029 as a penalty for companies that decide not to build plant and equipment within the stated period.
* **Reshoring is the goal:** Trump stated the measure is done in order to reshoring generic pharmaceutical production into America and penalize firms that fail to invest domestically on time.
* **Patented drugs unchanged:** The president said his administration's tariff plans related to patented drugs would remain unchanged from previous positions.
* **Social media disclosure:** Details of the new tariff timeline and purpose were outlined by President Trump in a social media post on Tuesday.

# [Trump's AI chip push is crushing TSMC's margins](https://substack.com/redirect/34920967-232f-45cc-9fb7-27a23c519a7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Pressure from President Donald Trump to manufacture advanced semiconductors in the United States **[is raising costs and diluting margins at TSMC](https://substack.com/redirect/dec9042b-8ed4-4974-9f65-90f5f7786216?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** even as the company posts record AI-driven profits.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/34920967-232f-45cc-9fb7-27a23c519a7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **$200 billion U.S. total:** TSMC has announced $200 billion in total U.S. manufacturing commitments since 2025, including a $100 billion investment in advanced facilities unveiled last week.
* **Overseas fabs dilute margins:** CFO Wendell Huang said gross margin dilution from overseas fab ramp-ups will be 2% to 3% early on, widening to 3% to 4% over the next several years.
* **U.S. chips cost more:** Analysts estimate TSMC's U.S.-made chips cost 20% to 50% more than those produced in Taiwan, with customers expected to absorb a large share of the higher expenses.
* **Record quarterly profit:** Second-quarter profit jumped 77.4% year on year to a record while gross margin reached 67.7%, though expansion continues to offset some gains from the AI boom.

# [$60 billion backlog and margin raise send Supermicro soaring](https://substack.com/redirect/34920967-232f-45cc-9fb7-27a23c519a7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Supermicro stock[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/60aff217-5f95-468e-95ac-295f906c888b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[jumped 15% in premarket trading Wednesday](https://substack.com/redirect/60aff217-5f95-468e-95ac-295f906c888b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after the AI server maker said it expects gross margins to nearly double while working through a record order backlog.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/34920967-232f-45cc-9fb7-27a23c519a7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Record quarterly orders:** Backlog rose to record levels at the end of fiscal 2026 with total new orders in excess of $60 billion received during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026.
* **Margins nearly doubled:** The company expects gross margin in the range of 15% to 17%, significantly higher than prior guidance of 8.2% to 8.4%, primarily due to a favorable customer and product mix.
* **AI server specialization:** Supermicro designs and builds servers and data center systems that incorporate semiconductors from chipmakers like Nvidia, Intel and AMD.
* **Year-to-date pressure:** Despite the AI boom, shares are down nearly 13% year to date after tumbling in June following an equity raise to fulfill AI server orders.

# [Kalshi just made midterm election betting insanely easy](https://substack.com/redirect/34920967-232f-45cc-9fb7-27a23c519a7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Prediction market platform Kalshi **[is launching a Midterms Hub that displays maps of trader odds](https://substack.com/redirect/03cd63f0-971d-4fd0-b959-5113155635af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on individual Senate and House races along with polling averages and fundraising data ahead of the November elections.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/34920967-232f-45cc-9fb7-27a23c519a7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Map of race odds:** The central page will show a map of what traders think the odds are in individual races for both the Senate and House of Representatives based on the latest markets.
* **Most visitors just watch:** About three quarters of all visitors to the platform come just to see the odds on individual events while only one in four actually trade on contracts.
* **CEO on crowd wisdom:** Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour said prediction markets cut through polarization and show what the wisdom of the crowds actually believes, backed by real money not rhetoric.
* **Early midterm volume:** More than $30 million has already been traded on contracts tied to which party will win the House and Senate in the 2026 midterm elections.

# [The Anthropic - Physical Intelligence rumor that just broke AI Twitter](https://substack.com/redirect/34920967-232f-45cc-9fb7-27a23c519a7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A weekend rumor that Anthropic was acquiring robotics startup Physical Intelligence spread rapidly across AI Twitter **[even after a denial from the company's CEO.](https://substack.com/redirect/c7cc3425-94ce-4964-9690-6ec911e40d60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/34920967-232f-45cc-9fb7-27a23c519a7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Talks held this spring:** Anthropic and Physical Intelligence actually held acquisition talks this spring according to The Information, giving the rumor a factual basis even if details differed.
* **Denial via Slack gif:** CEO Karol Hausman told employees the reports were not true in a Slack message that contained a gif of a character from The Office shaking her head no.
* **Startup scale and model:** Co-founded by Lachy Groom, Physical Intelligence has raised more than $1 billion and its π0.5 model ranks among the more widely used robot brains in research.
* **Deal and IPO activity:** Anthropic has made four known acquisitions this year and confidentially filed for an IPO on June 1, while OpenAI has acquired at least 17 companies since 2023.

* * *
* * *
# [Jamie Dimon warns next credit losses will be far worse](https://substack.com/redirect/34920967-232f-45cc-9fb7-27a23c519a7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Jamie Dimon has repeatedly warned that **[losses on leveraged lending in the next credit cycle are likely to be worse than people expect](https://substack.com/redirect/889bd917-0848-4874-a3f0-0dc750f2b0b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** even as the largest U.S. banks posted strong second-quarter profits.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/34920967-232f-45cc-9fb7-27a23c519a7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Banks post strong profits:** The nation's largest banks continued to report strong second-quarter earnings, showing the sector remains resilient despite volatile markets and rising consumer costs.
* **Trading desks benefit:** Many large banks saw trading revenue rise from periods of elevated market activity and investor uncertainty that create more opportunities for portfolio adjustments.
* **Wealth fees climb sharply:** Bank of America credited a 12% increase in global wealth and investment management revenue to higher asset management fees, up 15% to $4.2 billion.
* **Preparing for hard times:** JPMorgan Chase is still preparing for a possible recession even as Chairman and CEO Jamie Dimon declined to predict whether the U.S. was heading for one.

* * *
* * *
# [The brutal AI chip crash the market is quietly ignoring](https://substack.com/redirect/34920967-232f-45cc-9fb7-27a23c519a7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A sharp sell-off in semiconductor stocks erased $3.3 trillion from global chip values and **[drove volatility premiums near records](https://substack.com/redirect/451cf880-c364-4a52-9671-3b5ab558104c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while the broader U.S. equity market remains resilient with strong breadth.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/34920967-232f-45cc-9fb7-27a23c519a7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Chip volatility gap widens:** The gap between the Cboe SMH Volatility Index and the VIX recently hit nearly 47 points and remains near 45, showing traders expect far larger moves in chips than the S&P 500.
* **Trillions wiped from chips:** The sell-off erased roughly $3.3 trillion from global chip stocks as the PHLX Semiconductor Index broke below its key 12,000 level before climbing back above it.
* **Momentum basket collapses:** Goldman Sachs high-beta momentum basket of recent winners fell roughly one-third from its June peak, marking the worst July decline since April 2009.
* **Broad market holds firm:** Roughly two-thirds of stocks in the S&P 500, S&P 400 and S&P 600 remain above their 200-day moving averages while the advance-decline line recently hit a record high.

Hey, it's Mandela. I'm going to be straight with you - I hate asking for your hard-earned cash. But tonight, I have to ask for your support.
### **The race for Wisconsin Governor is heating up.**
We've got momentum. New polls show I'm Democrats' best shot at beating Tom Tiffany - Trump's hand-picked candidate for Governor of Wisconsin.
Our first TV ad is on the air across the state, featuring a pro-worker message that Tiffany's MAGA billionaires can't buy their way around. We're organized, we're energized, and we are in this fight.
Here's the problem: Tiffany and his MAGA allies just dropped a $2 million investment to meddle in our race. His billionaire backers don't have fundraising deadlines; they just write checks whenever they feel like it. We don't operate that way, and I'm damn proud of it.
### **But we can 't let Tom Tiffany outraise us without a response.**
There are no dark money groups keeping this campaign afloat. What we have is thousands of grassroots supporters across Wisconsin who believe that working families deserve a Governor who actually fights for them and the issues that keep them up at night.
That's the campaign we've built, and with your help, that's the campaign we need to keep running.
### **So before midnight tonight, I need your help.**
Giving $3 might not seem like much on its own. But when thousands of people do it together, it sends a message that no billionaire checkbook can - Wisconsin voters are organized, and they're willing to fight tooth and nail to keep our state blue.
**[So, will you chip in $3 or more to help us defeat Tom Tiffany and keep Wisconsin blue? I cannot do this without your support.](https://substack.com/redirect/f43467a3-bca3-46ac-b10e-4ef3c762ee96?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Let's go.
-- Mandela

DEAR FRIENDS,

Our campaign is picking up real momentum, and I'm grateful for all of you who are standing with us.

This Friday I'll be at the Blessing of the Fleet race, a great local tradition full of community spirit and celebration. I'm
looking forward to being there with you.

I've also been out meeting even more local business owners across Congressional District 2. These conversations are eye-opening.
Small business owners are the backbone of our economy, and they're telling me the real challenges they face every day. We need to
create a welcoming job environment that helps them grow and hire more Rhode Islanders.

On July 16, URI Economist Len Lardaro released his latest analysis of Rhode Island's economy. He noted that if our labor force
participation rate were back to pre-pandemic levels, June's unemployment rate would be 7.7%. He averages the numbers and estimates
the actual rate is around 5.9%. That's still too high, and it shows we're not moving in the right direction. For far too long,
Rhode Islanders have been stuck with "do nothing" politicians when it comes to encouraging real investment in our state. But that
changes with me.

President Trump has received well over $18 trillion in commitments from companies and countries into the United States. I'm going
to fight hard to capture our fair share of those commitments for Rhode Island's workers and bring good-paying manufacturing jobs
back home.

I'm also continuing to build strong contacts in Cuba as President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio work to open new
opportunities. Leveraging long-standing friendships with Cuban-American associations in Florida, I've traveled on humanitarian
missions to Cuba. The relationships I'm building with religious and civic leaders will help put Rhode Island first when that
island nation opens its doors and begins buying the goods and equipment its people need. Rhode Island manufacturers can provide
motors, gaskets, refurbished engines, food stuffs, medical equipment, and many other products that Cubans will need. The key is
being at the front of the line when President Trump says "all clear."

In the past, when the United States opened trade relationships with other countries, the American jobs went there. Rhode Island
lost whole industries — textiles, jewelry, Leviton, Bulova, Speidel, Coro, Gorham Silver, and more. Our state lost 41,000
good-paying manufacturing jobs after NAFTA and the China WTO agreements were signed. I want to make sure that isn't the case for
Rhode Island this time. I will work hard and long to make sure our workers are the ones who get the jobs and Rhode Island's
economy is the beneficiary.

We have a real chance to turn things around. Let's put Rhode Island first, protect the American Dream, and make sure our state
finally starts winning again.

Sincerely,

Vic Mellor

Candidate for Congress, Rhode Island's 2nd District

clean_body: [] DEAR FRIENDS, Our campaign is picking up real momentum, and I'm grateful for all of you who are standing with us. This Friday I'll be at the Blessing of the Fleet race, a great local tradition full of community spirit and celebration. I'm looking forward to being there with you. I've also been out meeting even more local business owners across Congressional District 2. These conversations are eye-opening. Small business owners are the backbone of our economy, and they're telling me the real challenges they face every day. We need to create a welcoming job environment that helps them grow and hire more Rhode Islanders. On July 16, URI Economist Len Lardaro released his latest analysis of Rhode Island's economy. He noted that if our labor force participation rate were back to pre-pandemic levels, June's unemployment rate would be 7.7%. He averages the numbers and estimates the actual rate is around 5.9%. That's still too high, and it shows we're not moving in the right direction. For far too long, Rhode Islanders have been stuck with "do nothing" politicians when it comes to encouraging real investment in our state. But that changes with me. President Trump has received well over $18 trillion in commitments from companies and countries into the United States. I'm going to fight hard to capture our fair share of those commitments for Rhode Island's workers and bring good-paying manufacturing jobs back home. I'm also continuing to build strong contacts in Cuba as President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio work to open new opportunities. Leveraging long-standing friendships with Cuban-American associations in Florida, I've traveled on humanitarian missions to Cuba. The relationships I'm building with religious and civic leaders will help put Rhode Island first when that island nation opens its doors and begins buying the goods and equipment its people need. Rhode Island manufacturers can provide motors, gaskets, refurbished engines, food stuffs, medical equipment, and many other products that Cubans will need. The key is being at the front of the line when President Trump says "all clear." In the past, when the United States opened trade relationships with other countries, the American jobs went there. Rhode Island lost whole industries — textiles, jewelry, Leviton, Bulova, Speidel, Coro, Gorham Silver, and more. Our state lost 41,000 good-paying manufacturing jobs after NAFTA and the China WTO agreements were signed. I want to make sure that isn't the case for Rhode Island this time. I will work hard and long to make sure our workers are the ones who get the jobs and Rhode Island's economy is the beneficiary. We have a real chance to turn things around. Let's put Rhode Island first, protect the American Dream, and make sure our state finally starts winning again. Sincerely, Vic Mellor Candidate for Congress, Rhode Island's 2nd District [] [] [] [] [] [] [] Want to change how you receive these emails?

clean_body: But too much remains unexplained | | | | | | Friend, I’ve only got a few minutes because my phone battery is at 7%, but I had to reach out to you one more time about this. >> Washington has a short memory. The politicians who demanded sweeping emergency powers, unprecedented spending, and rapid policy changes now act as though the American people should simply move on. No questions. No answers. I don't believe that's good enough. Throughout my oversight work, I've continued asking questions about the Biden administration’s pandemic response, its hasty vaccine rollout, and whether Congress received complete and accurate information. And the signs point to one man that we NEED to get in front of Congress under oath before Election Day. | | | | | | deserve confidence that future public health decisions will be guided by transparency, honest debate, and accountability, not by politics or bureaucracy. Peter,

After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate.

**President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's _"Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate._**

I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, _**but I am ready.**_

I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge.

It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times.

I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for.

I did not seek this moment, Peter.

But after many prayers and speaking with my family, I know I am making the right decision to run for this seat. **[However, I cannot do this alone.](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=f61487720df44601a62e4b917c844be9&_e=nlAyXavr7E7xbbDzsCEu8gvyHiLc-tF-g80CaoG4-CICkAvxCYVU_fv7zribekJmsmS_rqJ3JvUfIvpuFcqnYtE81ETPGdlrhDlrh3OY_4l_hOtHrhROFmvndMSTnUMi5ZO0PrpO7eL7uAk668tLrL8EdtvzmnbK8YMPpqhRrRul4Og-Bx8tEh1C7Yj1z4-2Vupk9tWINnTycgfN1aTP0uaeLub-cwe8rpCx-APMGEaz7tFHHP1bfUgQVWnGIQugRFow75FzRoinBmAXulbgqeBvo8tn04DFhIOtRtUBxbZ3fCa5svek61-HzVJJATPqEgskme44DRBF2QivyAYlqJG5LxWoGWYKzT0jX4e96SNh4zsNjBKmXnpQocTZcJtFRnMSKj9CB74RFBHx3yeDHm9Z0KADwQZFkQ00bhFqeM0koq9ghwg1k1YUldQTkOIjmalyG_vlEqwlwGIhTWxlFuYKOd_xA1SdKd2hQOcewxecC5bpX_Gn_z3u__Mhcs7pg9igAoQ9ABMfrUthYQUDTMWoIHmiyK-vozkTVP25FWfL_04kSlGQE1fDj0NHH2a3S_SuD9yyvlyWmUJKi04RNpZdUjE0Qm-gBQUDv-EAipmfEKrNLak-NOnRxzCqmf6L9oXsUeRpI109VFKcotJ7LeJ4EEaK9VcOBtGdDLy_X2hotoxvkifdaLI0q0cJ7C64GSJCcnStUpweOxBq5aWoXAG2plMgqCI4knzZrOIRIKk%3D)**

clean_body: I'm ready for the fight ahead, and I'm all in to run for the United States Senate. | Peter, After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate. President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's "Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate. I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, but I am ready. I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge. It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times. I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for. I did not seek this moment, Peter. But after many prayers and speaking with my family, I know I am making the right decision to run for this seat. I'll be straight with you - I am behind financially. My opponents are self-funding millionaires or have spent years building up their campaign war chests, but I'm new to politics. We have less than 3 weeks to run against people who have been at this for years. Since you were there for Lindsey, Thank you for everything you did for Lindsey over the years. I know that having people like you in his corner meant everything to him. God bless, Darline Graham P.S. It's been a difficult week. I never thought I'd be in this position, but I am ready to answer the call from President Trump. I am ready to run. | | Paid for by Darline for Senate Don't want to receive any more of our emails? clean_body: [] DEAR FRIENDS, I'm writing to personally invite you to a Meet & Greet tonight at my South Kingstown office. When: Tonight at 6:00 PM Where: 3045 Tower Hill Road, Saunderstown, RI This is a great chance for us to talk face-to-face about the future of Rhode Island's 2nd District. I want to hear directly from you — your concerns, your ideas, and what matters most to your family and community. Whether you have questions about jobs, healthcare, taxes, or anything else, I'll be there to listen and share where I stand. I'm fighting hard to put Rhode Island First, and events like this keep me grounded in what really matters to the people I hope to represent. I'd love to see you there tonight at 6 PM. Hope to see you soon, Vic Mellor Candidate for Congress, Rhode Island's 2nd District [] [] [] [] [] [] [] Want to change how you receive these emails?

https://rokhanna.com [https://rokhanna.com]
Peter,
The right to vote is under attack.
Trump and his Republican allies are pushing the SAVE Act—a dangerous bill that could make it significantly harder for millions of eligible Americans to register to vote and participate in our democracy.
Before Congress moves this bill forward, will you add your name demanding lawmakers reject the SAVE Act and protect every eligible American's right to vote? [https://act.rokhanna.com/a/save-act-petition?contactdata=OXmAZzA5/1WgJHjJYC12019ZSR8gp/LoQ8z2LMfI37r45yHN6AvOGwQCi8aixixZfCbvlVqRE/k8RC2njGpKEh8wezd88ltIPnMjl2uu++zwAdt7Pu66fIuowoGtKkoQwrZrkqWMtWX58i0ySNkTqPiZelBi2l6+ISpRInp+ZfscCckxO/TpCd76GQgPgrw3]
ADD YOUR NAME [https://act.rokhanna.com/a/save-act-petition?contactdata=OXmAZzA5/1WgJHjJYC12019ZSR8gp/LoQ8z2LMfI37r45yHN6AvOGwQCi8aixixZfCbvlVqRE/k8RC2njGpKEh8wezd88ltIPnMjl2uu++zwAdt7Pu66fIuowoGtKkoQwrZrkqWMtWX58i0ySNkTqPiZelBi2l6+ISpRInp+ZfscCckxO/TpCd76GQgPgrw3]
The SAVE Act would require many Americans to present documents like a passport or birth certificate when registering to vote or updating their voter registration.
Millions of eligible voters don't have those documents readily available. Married women who have changed their names, military families, students, seniors, rural voters, and working Americans could all face unnecessary hurdles just to cast a ballot.
Let's be clear: federal law already prohibits non-citizens from voting in federal elections. Cases of non-citizen voting are extraordinarily rare.
The SAVE Act isn't about election security. It's about making it harder for eligible Americans to vote.
Americans have spent generations fighting to expand democracy—not roll it back. We should be protecting the freedom to vote, not creating new barriers that keep citizens away from the ballot box.
Tell Congress: Vote NO on the SAVE Act. [https://act.rokhanna.com/a/save-act-petition?contactdata=OXmAZzA5/1WgJHjJYC12019ZSR8gp/LoQ8z2LMfI37r45yHN6AvOGwQCi8aixixZfCbvlVqRE/k8RC2njGpKEh8wezd88ltIPnMjl2uu++zwAdt7Pu66fIuowoGtKkoQwrZrkqWMtWX58i0ySNkTqPiZelBi2l6+ISpRInp+ZfscCckxO/TpCd76GQgPgrw3]

Thank you for your activism and all that you do.
In solidarity,
Ro

Wherever I go, I hear enormous concerns from Virginians about the impact of data centers on their communities and their utility bills.

**So, today, I wanted to tell you more about what I’m doing about it:**
1. Yesterday, I introduced a Comprehensive AI Legislative Agenda focused on responsible innovation, workers, and national security. This package includes important legislation that would establish minimum federal standards for power usage and water usage – _and make sure data centers are set back an appropriate distance from residential communities._

2. I’m also supporting the Power for the People Act, a bill that forces data centers to pay for the grid upgrades they require, instead of you. It makes them bring their own clean power and battery storage, instead of draining what we've got. And it guarantees the work is done with strong labor standards and good-paying jobs.

3. And I’m working on legislation that gives Virginians the transparency you deserve. So that you know when a new data center is proposed to your community – and that these data centers can’t make secret deals with local governments and hide the details from you and your neighbors.

Look, Derek, we’re not going to turn back the clock on AI or the data centers that power them.

**And frankly, grappling with the radical changes that Artificial Intelligence will bring to our economy, society, and communities was a key reason I decided to run for reelection.**

Virginians deserve a senator who will tackle these issues head on – not shy away from them – and provide solutions that protect you, your family, and your neighborhood _without_ trying to turn back the clock.

That’s why I’m asking Virginians to rehire me, send me back to Washington to keep fighting for working families, to lower costs, and to continue holding these large tech companies accountable.

[_**Can you pitch in to my campaign today to help me continue that critical work?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135787752/635330560/1079622208?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_DataCenters_260722_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MTk5N2NmOC1mMjg1LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=kW4Bkeby3U-htEIcgJLhtqRSRsVhKMMad2kVFAiTmG4=)

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Abbott sold you out to trillionaire Elon Musk for 500k
body:
A trillionaire doesn’t need a $17 million grant or a tax break. Let Musk pay his fair share.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
**What Greg Abbott and Elon Musk call economic development, I call corruption, Peter.**
Elon Musk recently demanded _$1.66 billion_ in local tax breaks for his new project in Grimes County, and he gave rural school board members an ultimatum — give me the tax cuts, or I’ll take my business elsewhere.
He got what he wanted, and now parents and taxpayers in Texas school districts are left footing the bill for growth while a _literal trillionaire_ gets off without paying his fair share.
**Not only is Musk getting away with a major tax break, but Abbott also handed him a $17.3 million state grant for his new semiconductor business. Now, Musk is returning the favor, writing Abbott a $500,000 campaign check.**
While public schools across Texas are forced to lay off teachers and cut programs because Abbott used taxpayer dollars for his school voucher scam, he has no problem handing out massive tax breaks to a trillionaire bankrolling his campaign.
We have a message for Abbott: **Texas doesn't belong to Elon Musk, and our state government shouldn't be a machine for corporate donors.**
When I’m governor, I’ll put an end to these sneaky backroom deals, protect public school funding, and make sure massive corporations pay their fair share.
But to defeat Greg Abbott this November, I need resources on the ground in every corner of this state.
**[Peter, will you make a $5 donation to my campaign right now to power my campaign and end this corruption in Texas?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260722_2_musk.d0U3ps&refcode=em20260722-1629&amount=5&t=1&akid=1629%2E299639%2E3zFQiF)**

Donald Trump is coming to Georgia today. And I have something to say: Mr. Trump: **_Before you talk about strength, remember who pays the price._** I'm a retired Brigadier General. I raised my right hand and swore an oath to defend this country -- and that oath didn't end when I took off the uniform. So I know firsthand: War is not a slogan or a talking point or something to use to score political points. **But Donald Trump has always treated our military and our foreign policy like another stage for division and chaos.** And now he's coming to Georgia to support a governor who will help carry out his agenda in our state. [**I 'm Shawn Harris. I'm a Democrat running for Congress in Georgia because America needs leaders who understand the responsibility of power--and the consequences of reckless decisions. Can I count on you to rush a donation before Trump lands in Georgia today?**](http://clicksp.shawnharrisforcongress.com/f/a/SROFg1Cz8cMU-lcPUKeolw~~/AAPPABA~/0zdiT75bFIxeL7S9HhQV2bBs7sXDB7y6-jLC4NdxRyIJxBRyqop2h97QXEWd8ZnGvE-IdOL7uONEYB11t9p0QBFKAPB4NKpQUlU2solUGQb42Ccm5eEzxgQwjMTW8HgAjXk-vbwe29gPg0q1CqmUnIXazk3KMQ_KOEcJbN0uDXiWD82LycPNiqEmQnwBq1b9oe43pwBgispgYtboCu8jf5kjMylsiR-EKLkGY9pYS5vPjRboOdum-o-IIqLLFVZbXNT4fKj2JMkdIXP299Nkmnp_bUv0d4saMEcg-y4bjpl62yAcAgFpqZKkbSIuDVUB)

Georgia is home to some of the bravest service members, veterans, and military families in America. They understand something Donald Trump seems to forget: **True strength is knowing when to fight, when to lead, and when to put the lives of others above your own political ambitions.** Trump is coming to Georgia because he wants a governor who will follow his lead. But Georgia deserves leaders who will stand up for our troops, protect our national security, and put service before self. That's why I'm in this fight. And today, while Trump is here trying to sell his agenda to Georgia, we have a chance to send a message of our own. clean_body: | | Donald Trump is coming to Georgia today. And I have something to say: Mr. Trump: Before you talk about strength, remember who pays the price. I'm a retired Brigadier General. I raised my right hand and swore an oath to defend this country -- and that oath didn't end when I took off the uniform. So I know firsthand: War is not a slogan or a talking point or something to use to score political points. But Donald Trump has always treated our military and our foreign policy like another stage for division and chaos. And now he's coming to Georgia to support a governor who will help carry out his agenda in our state. | Georgia is home to some of the bravest service members, veterans, and military families in America. They understand something Donald Trump seems to forget: True strength is knowing when to fight, when to lead, and when to put the lives of others above your own political ambitions. Trump is coming to Georgia because he wants a governor who will follow his lead. But Georgia deserves leaders who will stand up for our troops, protect our national security, and put service before self. That's why I'm in this fight. And today, while Trump is here trying to sell his agenda to Georgia, we have a chance to send a message of our own. ~~ ~~ Thank you for standing with us. Leadership Matters. -- Shawn Harris | ~~ "Facebook" ~ "X" \[BLUESKY\] "Bluesky" PAID FOR BY SHAWN FOR GEORGIA
