name: Veronica Escobar
subject: Sometimes all it takes is a spark of curiosity
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Veronica Escobar for Congress
body:
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135789241/635335405/-1405467182?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNDk0MTgyOC1mNzg1LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=MmeYMhWYeqKMYQdcAo4S4Xzggdqwfi3Cb_sdzdnqSPc=&emci=6fb7777d-dd85-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=c4941828-f785-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=14565883)
---

| | Growing up, I was always interested in politics, but never imagined I would actually be in politics. I always loved writing, and my plan included being an academic after earning a PhD in literature or being a journalist. After graduating from NYU with a master's degree, I came back home to save a bit of money before applying to PhD programs; I had fallen in love with Chicano literature and was committed to continuing my education. Little did I know that this time being back home would radically change my plans and my life. During my time home, there were some shocking events unfolding. The Border Patrol was stopping students, coaches, and staff at Bowie High School under the flimsy justification that they needed to verify the citizenship of students. It all reached a boiling point when one of the coaches was giving his students a ride home before he was pulled over at gunpoint. **It became impossible for me not to notice the struggle my community was facing, and I wanted to do something about it.** Very soon after moving back to El Paso, I began teaching at El Paso Community College and the University of Texas at El Paso, and connected with a group of activists who were working to push back on the constitutional and civil rights violations occurring in our community. I joined the Border Rights Coalition, where we fought for places like churches, schools, and clinics to be designated as safe zones free from intrusive immigration enforcement; we connected people to ESL classes and taught people to know their rights. At that same time, I also began volunteering for political campaigns. The trajectory of my career would change when I volunteered for Raymond Caballero's campaign for mayor of El Paso. At the time, it was the most impactful race I've ever experienced — because he spoke to the same issues I cared deeply about. Caballero called on the community to invest in itself; he believed that we had to save ourselves because no one was coming to do it for us. He inspired me so much that I committed to doing whatever I could to get him elected, even bringing my kids to the campaign office to see firsthand what real, grassroots work for our collective betterment looked like. **After Mayor Caballero won his election, my connection to community-centered politics deepened, and he offered me the opportunity to serve as his communications director.** It felt wild to leave my teaching position — a stable job I loved — but when you believe in something deeply, you have no choice but to embrace it and see it through. This faith in progress, rooted in community, is what started my journey — and is largely the reason I'm running for re-election today. In my heart of hearts, I will always be committed to fighting for your needs. Though our political landscape looks very different today, we all have the capacity to change our community; sometimes it takes being motivated by injustice. clean_body: | | | | Growing up, I was always interested in politics, but never imagined I would actually be in politics. I always loved writing, and my plan included being an academic after earning a PhD in literature or being a journalist. After graduating from NYU with a master's degree, I came back home to save a bit of money before applying to PhD programs; I had fallen in love with Chicano literature and was committed to continuing my education. Little did I know that this time being back home would radically change my plans and my life. During my time home, there were some shocking events unfolding. The Border Patrol was stopping students, coaches, and staff at Bowie High School under the flimsy justification that they needed to verify the citizenship of students. It all reached a boiling point when one of the coaches was giving his students a ride home before he was pulled over at gunpoint. It became impossible for me not to notice the struggle my community was facing, and I wanted to do something about it. Very soon after moving back to El Paso, I began teaching at El Paso Community College and the University of Texas at El Paso, and connected with a group of activists who were working to push back on the constitutional and civil rights violations occurring in our community. I joined the Border Rights Coalition, where we fought for places like churches, schools, and clinics to be designated as safe zones free from intrusive immigration enforcement; we connected people to ESL classes and taught people to know their rights. At that same time, I also began volunteering for political campaigns. The trajectory of my career would change when I volunteered for Raymond Caballero's campaign for mayor of El Paso. At the time, it was the most impactful race I've ever experienced — because he spoke to the same issues I cared deeply about. Caballero called on the community to invest in itself; he believed that we had to save ourselves because no one was coming to do it for us. He inspired me so much that I committed to doing whatever I could to get him elected, even bringing my kids to the campaign office to see firsthand what real, grassroots work for our collective betterment looked like. After Mayor Caballero won his election, my connection to community-centered politics deepened, and he offered me the opportunity to serve as his communications director. It felt wild to leave my teaching position — a stable job I loved — but when you believe in something deeply, you have no choice but to embrace it and see it through. This faith in progress, rooted in community, is what started my journey — and is largely the reason I'm running for re-election today. In my heart of hearts, I will always be committed to fighting for your needs. Though our political landscape looks very different today, we all have the capacity to change our community; sometimes it takes being motivated by injustice. I encourage you to find your spark and fan its flames. With gratitude, Veronica | Donate Today If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution to Veronica Escobar instantly: | = | = | = | = ---|---|---|--- | | | Paid for by Veronica Escobar for Congress. |

I am ready to continue his legacy. | Fellow Patriot, After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate. President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's "Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate. I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, but I am ready. I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge. It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times. I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for. I did not seek this moment, Fellow Patriot. But after many prayers and speaking with my family, I know I am making the right decision to run for this seat. I'll be straight with you - I am behind financially. | | **_Meet Rob:_** Born and raised in Kingston, PA, Rob Bresnahan is currently serving his first term as PA-08’s homegrown Congressman. He’s a fifth-generation Northeastern Pennsylvanian, and the only representative in Congress who is part of the National Electrical Contractors Association. A product of the American Dream, Rob learned the true meaning of hard work by getting his hands dirty early and often. He wired junction boxes, ran heavy equipment, drove trucks, and learned the value of an honest day’s work in the process. His family instilled the values of hard work, discipline, and perseverance in him at a young age – and Rob has stayed true to these foundational values all his life. At just 19 years old, Rob joined his family’s business as the CFO for Kuharchik Construction. He became the CEO of the company in 2013. Rob spent over a decade working and connecting with blue-collar Americans across the country before running for Congress in 2024. He was outspent 2:1 in his race against a 12-year Democrat that year, but the people of Northeastern Pennsylvania demanded change when they sent Rob to be their fighter in Washington. Through his experience as an electrical contractor, Rob saw the real world struggles facing America’s blue-collar workers first hand. Wages are not keeping up with the skyrocketing cost of living, and Americans who wake up every day and pay their dues are being left out to dry by their elected officials. But Rob’s voting record in Congress tells a different story. He’s stood up for hardworking Americans at every opportunity, regardless of partisan politics. Simply put, Rob Bresnahan brings both insight and candid concern for blue-collar America to Congress that your run-of-the-mill representatives don’t. Every day that he steps foot on Capitol Hill, Rob is 100% devoted to restoring America’s energy independence, deregulating the economy, and bringing well-paying jobs back to the great commonwealth of Pennsylvania. While he’s still serving his freshman term in Congress, Rob has already introduced key legislation to re-invest in American trades and pave avenues to success for young people who forgo a traditional college education. Now running for re-election in one of the most pivotal battleground races in the country, Rob is stepping up to the plate once again to deliver for the people of PA-08 and preserve our Republican House majority for the remainder of President Trump’s second term.

body:
Latino voters have the power to flip these seats.
#
Peter,
Arizona’s primary results are in, and the battle lines for November are officially set.
**We have a _massive_ opportunity to flip two of the most competitive seats in the nation, Arizona’s 2nd and 6th Congressional Districts**, defeat two extreme Republicans, and win a Democratic House majority.
[**With less than 15 weeks until Election Day, will you rush a contribution of $3 right now to help Voto Latino register, mobilize, and turn out Latino voters across Arizona’s key battlegrounds?**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260722-1.f9feC5&amount=3&refcode=em20260722-406&t=1&akid=406%2E1366028%2EhBYest)
**In AZ-06** , where Latinos make up 27% of voters, incumbent Republican Juan Ciscomani claims to stand for working families, but his record shows the complete opposite. **Ciscomani voted to allow healthcare credits to expire** , stripping 15,000 of his constituents of affordable coverage.
He also signed a letter opposing Medicaid cuts, then turned around and **voted for $880 billion in cuts** to Medicaid that threaten 130,000 people in his own district. He even posed at a local food bank for a photo-op after voting for**massive cuts to food assistance.**
**In AZ-02** , Congressman Eli Crane is choosing far-right extremism over working families, Tribal Nations, and the 20% of Latinos he represents in his district.
Crane has**openly defended tariffs** that cost local families an extra $1,000 last year, calling the financial strain **"necessary pain,”** and has even **voted against bipartisan housing relief** for rural and Tribal communities struggling with sky-high costs.
**Peter, it’s clear that Latino voters have the power to hold both incumbents accountable and flip these seats — but only if we organize on the ground right now.**
**[If you’re ready to flip these two vulnerable Republican seats, will you chip in $3 today to fuel Voto Latino’s voter registration and mobilization efforts in Arizona before November?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260722-1.f9feC5&amount=3&refcode=em20260722-406&t=2&akid=406%2E1366028%2EhBYest)**

Thank you,
Voto Latino

Paul LePage (ME-02): A two-time elected Governor of Maine whose American Dream story began sleeping in horse stables after becoming homeless at 11, Paul will end wasteful Democrat spending and bring back American jobs. Laurie Buckhout (NC-01): A retired Army Colonel and decorated combat commander from a long line of combat veterans, Laurie will fight to support our Veterans and make sure they receive the care they deserve when their mission is complete. Mike LiPetri (NY-03): A Conservative former New York State Assemblyman and champion of law enforcement, Mike will fight the pro-crime Democrats and help dismantle gangs trafficking fentanyl into our communities. Peter Oberacker (NY-19): A successful businessman from the Hudson Valley, Peter will fight to win this critical swing district and focus on bringing down the costs of groceries, utilities, and gas. Tano Tijerina (TX-28): A born and raised South Texan, Tano learned the importance of faith, family, and hard work. As a county judge, Tano locked away hardened criminals and will continue to fight to support law enforcement and the American Dream. Eric Flores (TX-34): A US Army Veteran, Eric will be a champion for our veterans, fight to keep the border secure, and put a stop to migrant crime in our communities. Greg Cunningham (NM-02): A Marine Veteran and law enforcement officer, Greg will fight for law enforcement, bring down the costs of energy, and keep the Southern border secure. John Braun (WA-03): A retired Navy Captain and job-creating manufacturer, John will fight to create more American jobs. Eric Conroy (OH-01): An Air Force Captain Veteran who answered the call when the Twin Towers fell on 9/11, Eric will fight for working families and revitalize Main Street America. Jim Desmond (CA-48): A Navy Veteran and commercial pilot, Jim will fight to lower costs and deliver safer communities. Brinker Harding (NE-02): An Omaha business leader, Brinker will rein in wasteful spending in Washington and work to reduce the National debt. Marty O'Donnell (NV-03): An award-winning composer for television shows, movies, and video games, Marty will fight to keep our border secure and invest in American technology. Carrie Buck (NV-01): A Nevada State Senator and education leader, Carrie will protect parents' rights, defend no tax on tips, and fully fund law enforcement. Aaron Flint (MT-01): A decorated combat veteran and fifth-generation Montanan and radio host, Aaron will fight to bring back American manufacturing and make the American Dream affordable again. These 17 candidates urgently need resources - not tomorrow, not closer to the election... Right here and right now. Some of their opponents have been in office for DECADES. The polling is on our side, the story is on our side, but NONE OF THAT matters if we can't tell voters about it. . We set a goal of raising $50,000 for each of them. We're not counting on you to cut a huge check, but we are hoping you can help chip away at that. We're BEGGING our grassroots team to dig deep and save President Trump's House Majority. I want to show you exactly what corruption looks like — and then I want to ask you to do something about it.
But, if you already agree that Washington corruption needs to stop, chip in to Equal Opportunity Now today. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email?refcode=260722_eon_frisco&amount=25]
CHIP IN TO STOP MAGA CORRUPTION » [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email?refcode=260722_eon_frisco&amount=25]
In his first year back in office, Donald Trump personally raked in more than $2 billion while working families struggle to keep up with rising prices.
More than $1.4 billion of it came from a crypto memecoin he launched days before his inauguration, and a venture called World Liberty Financial run by his own sons. He turned the office of the President of the United States into a personal ATM, and he didn't even try to hide it.
And it gets worse.
Just weeks ago, we learned that Trump and his Commerce Secretary negotiated a deal handing an American company access to one of the largest untapped tungsten reserves on earth — in Kazakhstan. The administration approved as much as $1.6 billion in federal financing to make it happen. Your tax dollars.
And then? Within weeks of the negotiations, a firm partly owned by Don Jr. and Eric Trump took a 20% stake in a company tied to that very same project.
Let me put that plainly: the President used your money to enrich his own sons. While more than 2 million Americans lost their health coverage. While hospitals and nursing homes were being defunded. While working families were told there just wasn't enough to go around.
There was plenty to go around. It just went to the Trumps.
This is the most corrupt administration in American history. It is not close.
And here's what makes me angriest of all: Corruption like this isn't just theft. It's the theft of opportunity itself. Because there is no equal opportunity if the game is rigged. When the powerful write the rules for themselves, working families don't get a fair shot — they get whatever scraps are left over after the well-connected have taken theirs.
That's exactly what Equal Opportunity Now was built to fight.
We know how to win. We've helped elect fighters who take on corruption, who champion honest government, who believe that public service means serving the public — not your own bank account. And we're building the bench of leaders who will do it up and down the ballot, in every corner of this country.
But we can't do it without you.

name: Peggy Flanagan
subject: Abdul asked me to reach out
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
[](https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260722-2-ak.fj_gs-&amount=10&refcode=em20260722-2688&t=2&akid=2693%2E251025%2E2NvHXX)
Peter,
I'm Peggy Flanagan, Lieutenant Governor of Minnesota, and I'm running for U.S. Senate. Abdul asked me to reach out to you directly, because our two races — different states, same fight — are more connected than you might think.
Before I dive in, I have to ask: [**Can you split $10 or any amount to support our campaigns? Both of our primary elections are coming up next month, and we need every bit of support to reach undecided voters and win.**](https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260722-2-ak.fj_gs-&amount=10&refcode=em20260722-2688&t=3&akid=2693%2E251025%2E2NvHXX)
**[Donate $10 ››](https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260722-2-ak.fj_gs-&amount=10&refcode=em20260722-2688&t=22&akid=2693%2E251025%2E2NvHXX)**
Peter, neither Abdul nor I take a dime of corporate PAC money. We’re the only candidates running in our respective races who can say that.
In my race, the outside spending has been relentless — dark money ads, AI deepfakes, you name it. And in Michigan, the same forces are lining up against Abdul to the tune of _$50+ million._
**Despite the millions of dollars being spent to stop us, I feel nothing but hope for both of our campaigns.**
I grew up on SNAP and Medicaid. My mom paid the rent with a Section 8 housing voucher. I know what it means to stretch 20 bucks until the end of the month. We need a government that shows up for working people, not corporate PACs and billionaires.
Abdul spent his career doing exactly that — as a doctor, as a health director, he built programs that will cancel up to $700 million in medical debt and got kids glasses instead of waiting for permission from the people who'd rather he didn't.
_That's why we both wrote the same non-negotiables into our campaigns:_
* Medicare for All, so no one has to choose between rent and a doctor's visit
* Dismantling ICE, so families don't live in fear of being torn apart.
* And getting corporate money out of politics altogether, so it's not even a question who a senator answers to.

**We can't out-raise the people trying to stop us. But together, we can out-organize them — if enough people like you decide both of these races matter.**
[**So today, I'm asking you to split a donation between my campaign and Abdul's. Whatever you can give, split evenly, helps us both go toe-to-toe with the money lined up against us — in Minnesota and in Michigan, on the same day, for the same reason.**](https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260722-2-ak.fj_gs-&amount=10&refcode=em20260722-2688&t=23&akid=2693%2E251025%2E2NvHXX)
**[Donate $10 ››](https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260722-2-ak.fj_gs-&amount=10&refcode=em20260722-2688&t=42&akid=2693%2E251025%2E2NvHXX)**
I don't think it's a coincidence that the same interests are spending against both of us. I think it means we're doing something right. Let's prove it.
Chi miigwech (that’s Ojibwe for big thank you)
💚 Peggy
* * *
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Emails like this help us stay connected with grassroots supporters like you, so thank you for taking the time to read this message. To contribute via check, please address it to Abdul for U.S. Senate, PO Box 126, St. Clair Shores, MI 48080.

John Sununu wants to send me back to “bussing tables.” He said it at the
Republican Senate debate as an insult — as if working in a restaurant is
something to be ashamed of.

It isn’t. It’s something to be proud of.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260722_2.Q5QYTI&refcode=em20260722-2&t=1003&akid=7877%2E582294%2ErXWnGL ]Puritan Restaurant menu

My family has run the Puritan for over 100 years. I know what a 65-hour
work week looks like, and I’ve spent my time in Congress fighting for the
people who work them.

When Sununu was in Washington, he voted for the Wall Street bailout and
championed corporate tax breaks — all while voting against expanded
workers’ rights. He left the Senate and spent the next 17 years cashing in
on corporate boards and working with Big Oil, Big Pharma, and Wall Street.

That’s who John Sununu is fighting for. It’s not you. [ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260722_2.Q5QYTI&refcode=em20260722-2&t=1004&akid=7877%2E582294%2ErXWnGL ]And if you’re
tired of politicians who only show up for the people cutting them checks,
I hope you’ll make a donation to our campaign today.

In Congress I’ve introduced legislation to protect jobs, fight for lower
costs for working families, and deliver real results for veterans and
small businesses across New Hampshire.

John Sununu is running to go back to Washington and protect the same
people who made him rich. [ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260722_2.Q5QYTI&refcode=em20260722-2&t=1005&akid=7877%2E582294%2ErXWnGL ]I’m running to fight for you and your family
— and I need you in my corner. Can you make a $5
contribution to my campaign today?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260722_2.Q5QYTI&amount=5&refcode=em20260722-2&t=1024&akid=7877%2E582294%2ErXWnGL ]Donate $5 »

With appreciation for all you do,

Chris Pappas

Peter,

While my Republican opponent is fueled by dark-money super PACs and special interests, I’m building a grassroots movement powered by folks like you: _your_ interests, concerns and hopes for the future.
**Now that we’re just over 100 days away from the election, this race is about to heat up – and I need to hear from you directly. body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-conrad [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-conrad]
Speaker Johnson says he’s a Christian. I say he’s the Antichrist.
Senator Rafael Warnock called out Mike Johnson for his hypocrisy out loud. He said he couldn’t understand why the Speaker could read the bible, say a prayer, and then cut a trillion dollars out of Medicaid — calling it waste, fraud, and abuse.
My grandmother taught me in Sunday school that we are supposed to treat every single person that we meet with dignity.
Speaker Mike Johnson? He wants to take healthcare away from millions of Americans. There’s nothing Christian about him.
Mike Johnson thinks that he can hide behind his faith — but I know the truth.
He’s voted to cut Social Security. He tried to overturn the election in 2020. He has an extreme record on LGBTQ+ issues and bodily autonomy. And he’s used his Christian faith to explain his actions every step of the way.

We’ve all had a front-row seat to this administration’s blatant corruption for the last year and a half, and it’s not getting any easier to stomach as time goes on.
So let’s take a minute to talk about all this money that Donald Trump has made for himself since returning to the office. Take a look at these two recent headlines, because they paint quite the picture:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25]

This is actually bananas.
Donald Trump has made at least $2 billion since returning to office. Of that huge sum of money, $1.4 billion came from his corrupt crypto ventures.
Here’s how this happened, and why it’s problematic: just a few days before Trump was inaugurated, an investment firm tied to the United Arab Emirates bought a 49% stake in his family’s crypto company, creating a massive financial tie between Trump and a foreign government, and a serious conflict of interest when it comes to foreign policy.
Plus, as President, Trump now directly oversees the regulation of this industry that he’s personally and directly benefiting from, and he has dramatically rolled back guardrails around crypto.
This is corruption plain and simple. And Trump’s huge profits are apparently without precedent, as the New York Times points out:
“Mr. Trump’s profits are a haul once unimaginable for any leader of a liberal democracy, particularly a sitting American president. No modern Western leader has ever publicly disclosed such big windfalls while in office.”
More than just breaking norms (and laws), Donald Trump’s greed and corruption is showing the world a new standard of acceptable behavior from leaders of a liberal democracy.
Here’s the real kicker to all of this: Congress has the power to stop it, but Republicans have repeatedly refused to join Democrats to do anything about it.
It’s clear that as long as Republicans control Congress, Trump will keep abusing the power of the presidency to enrich himself and his family and shield himself from accountability.
Flipping the House this November will give us real subpoena power, real oversight, and the ability to demand answers from an administration that has spent two years trying to make itself untouchable. Because no one — not even Donald Trump — is above the law.

By California law, vote-by-mail ballots are considered late if they do not arrive within seven days of election day, even if they are postmarked on or ahead of election day. What does this mean? Hey folks,
It's good to be back.
[Don Lemon](https://open.substack.com/users/143409218-don-lemon?utm_source=mentions) and I covered a lot of ground in this one--and somehow it all connects. We talked about the chaos surrounding Mitch McConnell, the way conspiracy theories thrive when institutions lose public trust, the media ecosystem that rewards outrage over facts, and what it actually feels like to build an audience in this new digital world. We even got surprisingly personal by the end.
**Here 's what we got into:**
* [**00:01:07**] We dive straight into the questions surrounding Mitch McConnell's health, the political stakes in Kentucky, and why transparency matters.
* [**00:06:14**] We unpack the Nolan Wells case, public distrust in institutions, and how social media incentives push people toward the most extreme conclusions.
* [**00:08:00**] Jeffrey Epstein, suspicious headlines, and why Americans increasingly question official narratives--even when there may not be a conspiracy.
* [**00:16:15**] Don and I talk about the collapse of traditional media gatekeepers, the rise of streaming, and why influence looks completely different today.
* [**00:23:13**] We wrap things up with some unexpected laughs, personal stories about identity, and a reminder that authentic conversations still matter.

This episode is about much more than the day's headlines. It's about trust, media, politics, and how we navigate a world where everyone is competing for your attention. If you care about staying grounded while everything around us feels louder and more chaotic, this conversation is for you. If you value honest conversations like this, help me keep them going.

| Running a campaign means making lots of tough decisions, Peter.

**Now, the tough decision my team and I have to make is how much airtime we can buy to keep our TV ad running across the district over the next 13 days before the primary election.**

name: Rep. Vikki Goodwin
subject: Access to clean water shouldn't be a partisan issue.
disclaimer_text: paid for by the Vikki Goodwin Campaign, Allen Biehl, Treasurer
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/Goodwin-email?refcode=20260722_em_fr_b1_VG_engaged [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/Goodwin-email?refcode=20260722_em_fr_b1_VG_engaged]
Peter, days ago, I called for a special legislative session to address the data center crisis in Texas.
I’ve been on the road since then, talking about water and data centers (and many other things) because Texans deserve answers and leaders who show up.
Across our state, communities are wondering if we will have enough water, if families will be forced to compete with billion-dollar corporations for resources that belong to all Texans. I've pledged to put Texans first.
As Lt. Governor, I will prioritize bills that regulate data centers and protect our water, land, health, and access to electricity.
Access to clean, reliable water shouldn't be a partisan issue. It should be common sense.
Unfortunately, Dan Patrick has spent years making other things his top priorities.
While communities worry about water shortages, he's focused on gerrymandered maps, banning THC products, putting the Ten Commandments in public school classrooms, doing nothing to solve the challenges Texans are actually facing.
I am running to change that, but I need your help.
Peter, it's time Texas has a Lieutenant Governor who's willing to fight for our water and our communities. Will you chip in today to help me defeat Dan Patrick this November? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/Goodwin-email?refcode=20260722_em_fr_b1_VG_engaged]
SUPPORT VIKKI TODAY [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/Goodwin-email?refcode=20260722_em_fr_b1_VG_engaged]
Thank you,
Rep. Vikki Goodwin
Vikki Goodwin is a true Texan. Raised in Dallas, she graduated from UT and the LBJ School of Public Affairs. She’s currently serving her fourth term in the Texas Legislature.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/Goodwin-email?refcode=20260722_em_fr_b1_VG_engaged [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/Goodwin-email?refcode=20260722_em_fr_b1_VG_engaged]
Throughout her life, Vikki has strived to build a better Texas for her family, her clients and her constituents. Now, she has her sights set on returning sanity to Texas government and restoring a collaborative and cooperative spirit, putting aside things that divide us, with a focus on real issues, not distractions.
Representative Vikki Goodwin is serving her fourth term in the Texas Legislature, representing parts of Austin and the Lake Travis area, and she is currently running for Lt. Governor of Texas. She is a passionate supporter of Texas public schools, has steadfastly voted against vouchers, and will continue to do so.
As a member of the Appropriations Article III Subcommittee overseeing education funding, she champions educational equity and access at all levels. Her priorities are to increase funding to public schools, housing affordability, water infrastructure, and access to healthcare.
Now, she's running for Lt. Governor against Dan Patrick to build a collaborative and cooperative spirit, putting aside things that divide us and focusing on real issues that impact real Texans.

Colorado turns the first Trump DOJ’s own words against its Second Amendment lawsuits
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hey friends,
Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** Colorado is fighting DOJ lawsuits over its magazine ban and Denver's assault-weapons ordinance, [citing Sessions-era memos against federal overreach](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). An Aurora church is under review after a [$24 million Medicaid scheme](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) exploiting the homeless, and 98 people linked to Tren de Aragua were [indicted for an ATM-hacking scheme](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) spanning 26 states, including Colorado. [Four ICE protesters were detained](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in Centennial amid ongoing demonstrations, and a Montezuma County judge agreed to a [90-day suspension for misconduct](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), with his fate ultimately left to voters in 2028.
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** The State Department released a 99-page report accusing communist Cuba of a nearly [seven-decade subversion campaign against the U.S.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), alleging it infiltrated the government and cultivated left-wing activism; Rubio said the report exposes "the full history of Cuban espionage."
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** Nash Herman asks why [Colorado health care keeps getting pricier](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) despite subsidies, when scale should lower costs. Cory Gaines argues Colorado's "majority renewables" milestone reflects [coal retirements shrinking the denominator](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), not real renewable growth, masking rising power imports. And Russ Minary lists what he calls [Trump administration accomplishments](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) across immigration, energy and deregulation, urging conservatives to vote in November.
This is your Mountain Minute for Wednesday, July 22, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Colorado turns the first Trump DOJ’s own words against its Second Amendment lawsuits](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
When the Justice Department sued Colorado in May over its large-capacity magazine ban, the state went looking for ammunition of its own. It found it inside DOJ’s filing cabinets.
In its federal court filing on June 30, Colorado submitted a motion to dismiss that leverages two memos from Jeff Sessions, the first attorney general in Trump’s first term. The state utilizes these documents to contend that the DOJ is attempting to assert an authority that its own former leadership said it should not exercise.
The 2017 memo told department heads that “it is not the responsibility of the federal government to manage non-federal law enforcement agencies.” The 2018 memo warned that long-term federal court supervision of state and local governments “can deprive the elected representatives of the people of the affected jurisdiction of control of their government.”
Those memos are now exhibits in a case where the current Trump DOJ is suing Colorado for enforcing its own gun laws.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Has Trump kept his promises? You decide.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY RUSS MINARY, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_A conservative columnist makes the case that the Trump administration's second-term record — from border security to the economy — speaks for itself._
* **56-item accomplishment list:** Guest columnist Russ Minary compiles a lengthy list of what he calls Trump 2.0 achievements, spanning immigration enforcement, crime reduction, economic growth, deregulation, and foreign policy wins, sourced from Jeff Childers' Coffee&Covid blog.
* **Not blind loyalty, just results:** Minary stresses he's "not a Trump fanboy" but a conservative focused on facts, acknowledging ongoing challenges like gas price fluctuations, inflation, and housing affordability while crediting the administration for tackling them.
* **A call to show up in November:** He warns that disillusioned conservative and unaffiliated voters sitting out primaries let further-left candidates win, urging readers to vote in the upcoming election to avoid a "very dark" outcome.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

**[The Hidden Trust Weapon: Olly, Olly, Oxen Free!](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | JULY 19** _“Olly, olly, oxen free!” If you’re smiling right now, you’re probably remembering the same thing I am. Long before smartphones, video games, and streaming television, neighborhood kids had an amazing ability to entertain themselves. We’d ride our bikes until the streetlights came on, play baseball in empty lots, build forts out of scrap lumber, and, when the evening shadows grew just a little longer, someone would shout, “Let’s play hide-and-seek!”_ __
**[Xcel says it has no affordability crisis. Its customers and regulatory filings tell another story.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | JULY 17** _Every week, Carlos H. sits down with his bills and works out what his family can go without. Some weeks it is dinner. “I just opt out to say, hey, okay, maybe won’t be cooking up something tonight, so we can just make ends meet,” the Denver father said. Some weeks it is gas—a quarter tank instead of a full one, and the math of whether that gets him to the next payday._ __
**[The rise of DSA, and a platform to rewrite the Constitution.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY SHAINA COLE | NATIONAL | JULY 16**
_Six thousand people started the Democratic Socialists of America in 1982. The number didn’t move much for thirty years. Then, around 2016, it did. By July 4, 2026, DSA had 120,000 members, more than the Socialist Party of America ever had under Eugene Debs, whose dues-paying membership peaked back in 1912._ __

body:
https://secure.ngpvan.com/pHjIfjOHuUuKCNiE1dEHTw2?contactdata=uy/zDuhYSCrOOlSVGrH8vhq3/X2wk/umta0/yJCJ4NGBauX0VWwBwkNWXbJPJpVbr4M/bq8TOJTAXh1sOhRNhZ0hrNNQKTsPOmun3gAsitLwN/v1kO6O53r25/NKf6yX [https://secure.ngpvan.com/pHjIfjOHuUuKCNiE1dEHTw2?contactdata=uy/zDuhYSCrOOlSVGrH8vhq3/X2wk/umta0/yJCJ4NGBauX0VWwBwkNWXbJPJpVbr4M/bq8TOJTAXh1sOhRNhZ0hrNNQKTsPOmun3gAsitLwN/v1kO6O53r25/NKf6yX]
Dear Peter,
The Trump administration is once again putting Oregon's public forests on the chopping block.
The U.S. Forest Service has released a draft plan that could triple logging across 5.5 million acres of eastern Oregon's national forests over the next decade, including the Malheur, Ochoco, Umatilla, and Wallowa-Whitman National Forests. The proposal would also weaken long-standing protections for large, mature trees and assumes the elimination of safeguards that have protected millions of acres of roadless forests.
These forests are some of Oregon's greatest natural treasures. They provide clean drinking water, store climate-polluting carbon, support wildlife like wolves, salmon, elk, and owls, and offer places for people to hike, hunt, fish, and recreate.
The Forest Service claims dramatically increasing logging will reduce wildfire risk, but many scientists and conservation advocates warn that removing mature forests and expanding logging could harm wildlife habitat, degrade water quality, and undermine the forests' natural resilience to climate change and wildfire.
We can't stand by and let this happen.
Take action [https://secure.ngpvan.com/pHjIfjOHuUuKCNiE1dEHTw2?contactdata=uy/zDuhYSCrOOlSVGrH8vhq3/X2wk/umta0/yJCJ4NGBauX0VWwBwkNWXbJPJpVbr4M/bq8TOJTAXh1sOhRNhZ0hrNNQKTsPOmun3gAsitLwN/v1kO6O53r25/NKf6yX]
Right now, the Forest Service is accepting public comments [https://secure.ngpvan.com/pHjIfjOHuUuKCNiE1dEHTw2] , and they need to hear from Oregonians who believe our public forests should be managed for clean water, wildlife, climate resilience, and future generations, not increased industrial logging.
Tell the Forest Service:
* Protect mature and old-growth forests that store carbon and provide critical wildlife habitat.
* Keep safeguards in place for large trees and roadless areas.
* Base forest management decisions on the best available science, not political pressure.
* Prioritize truly climate-smart wildfire solutions that protect communities without sacrificing our public lands.
Our public forests belong to all of us, not the logging industry. Submit your comment today and help defend the forests that make Oregon extraordinary! [https://secure.ngpvan.com/pHjIfjOHuUuKCNiE1dEHTw2]
Sincerely,

The U.S. Forest Service has released a draft plan that could triple logging across 5.5 million acres of eastern Oregon's national forests over the next decade, including the Malheur, Ochoco, Umatilla, and Wallowa-Whitman National Forests. The proposal would also weaken long-standing protections for large, mature trees and assumes the elimination of safeguards that have protected millions of acres of roadless forests. These forests are some of Oregon's greatest natural treasures. They provide clean drinking water, store climate-polluting carbon, support wildlife like wolves, salmon, elk, and owls, and offer places for people to hike, hunt, fish, and recreate. The Forest Service claims dramatically increasing logging will reduce wildfire risk, but many scientists and conservation advocates warn that removing mature forests and expanding logging could harm wildlife habitat, degrade water quality, and undermine the forests' natural resilience to climate change and wildfire. We can't stand by and let this happen. Take action [] Right now, the Forest Service is accepting public comments [] , and they need to hear from Oregonians who believe our public forests should be managed for clean water, wildlife, climate resilience, and future generations, not increased industrial logging. Tell the Forest Service: Protect mature and old-growth forests that store carbon and provide critical wildlife habitat. Keep safeguards in place for large trees and roadless areas. Base forest management decisions on the best available science, not political pressure. Prioritize truly climate-smart wildfire solutions that protect communities without sacrificing our public lands. Our public forests belong to all of us, not the logging industry. Submit your comment today and help defend the forests that make Oregon extraordinary! body:
The Village Idiot is Going to Get the World Blown Up

| | | **[Don’t Let Trump Help Saudi Arabia Get a Nuclear Bomb](https://default.salsalabs.org/T021ad931-dbb3-4d7d-8762-5d08c873ceb4/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)** [](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tefb73181-9cc0-4c6f-9589-6e3b36d24b24/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) With the Middle East already in the midst of about 37 different wars, what they clearly need is lots of nukes. And Donald Trump is on it! Always eager to prove that he is an even bigger idiot than you thought, Trump is will give the Saudi’s a brand new nuclear cooperation agreement— complete with that “new plutonium smell”, and without critical safeguards to keep them from building their own nuclear bombs. The proposed agreement would not prohibit Saudi Arabia from enriching uranium or reprocessing spent nuclear fuel, both of which are critical pathways to building nuclear weapons. It would also omit inspections to so they can build these weapons in privacy. _(Pause for a moment, and consider just how big an idiot Trump is)_

Oh, also, just a reminder that the de facto leader of Saudi Arabia is **Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman — the same guy **[whom U.S. intelligence concluded approved an operation to “capture or kill” Jamal Khashoggi](https://default.salsalabs.org/T12f5bf1f-de66-45e3-937a-6e9519e3ce98/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9), a U.S. resident and Washington Post columnist who was brutally murdered by Saudi agents inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul. Saudi Arabia may have legitimate energy needs. But no nuclear agreement should give its authoritarian government the ability to enrich uranium while denying international inspectors the access needed to ensure that its nuclear program remains peaceful. Congress will have approximately 90 legislative days to object once the agreement is submitted. It must act. **[Add your name and demand that Congress reject any nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia that opens a path to a nuclear weapon.](https://default.salsalabs.org/T3d5747ad-b80c-47bb-be74-428d6d7e3727/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)**

The fight over it has brought Congress to a standstill -- other legislation blocked outright to force the Senate's hand. The House is going again before the August recess. That is the window. If it does not become law, the 2026 election runs under the same rules we have right now. That is the whole fight. -- The 2026 Victory Team P.S. The Senate stalled it once already. Fellow Patriot,

After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate.

**President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's _"Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate._**

I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, _**but I am ready.**_

I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge.

It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times.

I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for.

I did not seek this moment, Fellow Patriot.

But after many prayers and speaking with my family, I know I am making the right decision to run for this seat. **[However, I cannot do this alone.](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=c835ac84e1724fbfb49eb90cbdb424e0&_e=fB-0oAdBAF67D-iomu8zrKUSeH8rxQs5Y3Y_t9lDflWIZed7THQNZvS1KXMD1peOKDiZWNugufhHDulcpVK6jHOpA_yCD7YIYbTaA88q6z7gYRiCGvanQBrCOdXnzpO4psq2MKH7VfmqIKpP-gvfz7PXwLpG46Wu-th-23lodTtcZ_ikmaw1JmBijF2xoV1uOQsM2YRWJWPD0Xuy2Wz0auygop2qwb5w6adv1viLtCMjxvVtiUD-9A_-1zBC4JPqdUkAntrV__itS-Yx8worPmBTt1xYrREgqMTYCHJbWeRJjiNe1LN6cf3RJgJ_oeJ_5McjFAwFNKf4sTLGKB62nsKEQd7cL14-0bxvwrTqLgxP1P210aUGcPE6V7zIuAGPt8H8YNbY3cEe6IwpBy8h7WUfqter66MP92ifyhbrQv-ynUq_e9joJQNCIvRMHMJmeHygT1he9ckFmRNcQFRNc8oQCxTyvqooqLG5qA57keFSk9dkYJlVzrqgcgRFImypc4DVmzrPDi4SFcTGI6vu0sGxRgi8KB-6kYzEWai_8vdREVPPp23ECfQHGJyoV4SWj9OeQa_VdCtJa9GLbhnkSG0sUG8Jequ0XKO8vlz21pGAMVNr2yWBZYIYAo_Dwe4Zk4OPzB3y0aIkg4fdSnZ9y-N1niOg5XN0vzurhfS0S01Ipvn_uIfWM_1MeMBEaz24WfWW0cYhHsVR5NbxZ5JgKEcdktMsTjzCwJxFuA9GkmM%3D)**

We have less than 3 weeks to run against people who have been at this for years. **[Would you please give $5, $10, or even $50 to help us build our grassroots campaign before the August 11th Special Election Primary?](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=c835ac84e1724fbfb49eb90cbdb424e0&_e=fB-0oAdBAF67D-iomu8zrKUSeH8rxQs5Y3Y_t9lDflWIZed7THQNZvS1KXMD1peOKDiZWNugufhHDulcpVK6jHOpA_yCD7YIYbTaA88q6z7gYRiCGvanQBrCOdXnzpO4psq2MKH7VfmqIKpP-gvfz7PXwLpG46Wu-th-23lodTtcZ_ikmaw1JmBijF2xoV1uOQsM2YRWJWPD0Xuy2Wz0auygop2qwb5w6adv1viLtCMjxvVtiUD-9A_-1zBC4JPqytWUXA5QSECyDLsJbJBLchRR5UECMka-jU6PgeJGFIr-jfdIXGW7q2o1iL-zTIYc9hk6KeqSU8F_UBWcQ1W8TAfCl1QkjbIv6uhewRABaLkGImGLDe9YzLZXUPonRmd1OExZHJKehoH-K7D_UUUGLy1XARPXk6n9XpqKnXV7zyqN9xE5UEyrEuRSWbc4ZQ5an0k64WsQtC7uYkuk6hWy3xCYbIGxzG_BTfkDy3iv_cASbh0eWyAF94K5-1Y_jpR3y5o7p4ZjmjekIN-M2s_SGEIuY4m3VdO2nnPpCHrlRx0keah7top9JGqzLXmaFwgeBjzmPOSrU-haurpuHO84Ka5SvEPp3mRGQNhslvyGXu0WWWfIiv9GuI5VLIOoojDOh4jgkmPVTAfni6MXQ6_B64s2_BklsTzJ-K3H48E-0AFYDlvH76PAVotz4gb7hVCrJOaoijlcq64XDWLgXeEJJGHi2AqALCl1YpcUg2MMt5A%3D)**

God bless,

clean_body: Lindsey worked so hard, for so long for this state. I am ready to continue his legacy. | Fellow Patriot, After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate. President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's "Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate. I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, but I am ready. I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge. It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times. I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for. I did not seek this moment, Fellow Patriot. But after many prayers and speaking with my family, I know I am making the right decision to run for this seat. I'll be straight with you - I am behind financially. My opponents are self-funding millionaires or have spent years building up their campaign war chests, but I'm new to politics. We have less than 3 weeks to run against people who have been at this for years. Since you were there for Lindsey, Thank you for everything you did for Lindsey over the years. I know that having people like you in his corner meant everything to him. God bless, Darline Graham P.S. It's been a difficult week. I feel this ruling in a way that's hard to put into words.

---
**The Supreme Court quietly handed down a ruling last month that deserves a lot more attention than it got.** | **Supreme Court Rejects Lawsuit Alleging Roundup Weedkiller Caused Cancer** _— The New York Times_
---
The case came down to a simple question: _can a company be held accountable for a cancer-causing product it sells without a warning?_
The Court sided with Bayer, the company that makes Roundup weedkiller, in a 7-to-2 decision. It threw out a verdict that a St. Louis gardener named John Durnell had won.
Mr. Durnell used Roundup for decades. He developed non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, _the same cancer I was diagnosed with in 2022,_ and a jury agreed that the company should have warned him about the risk.
The Supreme Court rejected the ruling, which essentially paves the way for thousands of lawsuits against Bayer to be dismissed.
Cancer taught me how fragile and precious life really is. And I was lucky. I had extraordinary care and treatments that saved my life. So many people never get that chance, and that painful truth stays with me.
Mr. Durnell did what any of us might do. He bought a product off a shelf. And now the highest court in the country has told him, and potentially thousands of others still waiting for their day in court, that there's nothing they can do.
**This is exactly why the work we do at JanePAC matters so much. Courts can be captured. Regulators can be pressured. But the people who write our laws and appoint the officials enforcing them are elected — and that means we still have a say.**
Electing leaders who believe that human health comes before corporate profit is how we build accountability that no single ruling can erase.
Surviving cancer changed me. It made me think hard about the time I have left and how I want to use it. I don't want to look back with regret. I want to know I did everything I could to fight for a world where corporations can't put people's health at risk and simply walk away.
This ruling doesn't change that resolve. It sharpens it.
In solidarity,
Jane Fonda

clean_body: I feel this ruling in a way that's hard to put into words. | The Supreme Court quietly handed down a ruling last month that deserves a lot more attention than it got. | Supreme Court Rejects Lawsuit Alleging Roundup Weedkiller Caused Cancer — The New York Times The case came down to a simple question: can a company be held accountable for a cancer-causing product it sells without a warning? The Court sided with Bayer, the company that makes Roundup weedkiller, in a 7-to-2 decision. It threw out a verdict that a St. Louis gardener named John Durnell had won. Mr. Durnell used Roundup for decades. He developed non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, the same cancer I was diagnosed with in 2022, and a jury agreed that the company should have warned him about the risk. The Supreme Court rejected the ruling, which essentially paves the way for thousands of lawsuits against Bayer to be dismissed. Cancer taught me how fragile and precious life really is. And I was lucky. I had extraordinary care and treatments that saved my life. So many people never get that chance, and that painful truth stays with me. Mr. Durnell did what any of us might do. He bought a product off a shelf. And now the highest court in the country has told him, and potentially thousands of others still waiting for their day in court, that there's nothing they can do. This is exactly why the work we do at JanePAC matters so much. Courts can be captured. Regulators can be pressured. But the people who write our laws and appoint the officials enforcing them are elected — and that means we still have a say. Electing leaders who believe that human health comes before corporate profit is how we build accountability that no single ruling can erase. Surviving cancer changed me. It made me think hard about the time I have left and how I want to use it. I don't want to look back with regret. I want to know I did everything I could to fight for a world where corporations can't put people's health at risk and simply walk away. This ruling doesn't change that resolve. It sharpens it. In solidarity, Jane Fonda = Before you scroll away, our candidates are up against the oil and gas lobby and the billionaires backing it, all hellbent on protecting a political system that rewards their bottom line. The Jane Fonda Climate PAC exists to disrupt that status quo by unseating politicians in the pocket of corporate polluters and replacing them with climate champions willing to fight like hell for our planet and the communities we call home. body:
Celebrate the momentum and find upcoming events, canvassing opportunities, and more ways to help.

| | | | | |
---
|
---
| | | | | |
# This Week with Team Berge
---
| | Hi Team Berge,
We have exciting news: Team Berge won the recent La Crosse straw poll!
This is a huge milestone for our campaign and a reminder of what is possible when people hear Emily’s community-rooted message. Every conversation, event, shared post, and volunteer shift helps us reach another voter.
This victory belongs to all of you. With the August 11 primary approaching, now is our chance to carry that momentum forward.
Thank you to every volunteer and supporter who helped make this possible. Let’s keep going.
---
|
---
| |
# Featured Event: Boogie with Berge!
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
Celebrate the Momentum With Team Berge!
Join us for a free evening of live music, community, and excitement as we work to get out the vote for Emily! Boogie for Berge is more than a night of music. It is an opportunity to bring people together, welcome new supporters, and build energy heading into the August 11 primary.
---
| [RSVP](https://us.list-manage.com/8ANNniQmyjQ?e=1362dd258a&c2id=d51b517ba2e5c823fe0a3e4f0e8330f1)
---
| |
# Ways to Volunteer This Week
---
| |
Every community event is an opportunity to listen, connect, and introduce more voters to Emily. Join Team Berge at one of the upcoming events below and help us continue building this campaign from the ground up.

**Saturday, July 25**(12:00pm-3:00pm) - Almond Tator Toot Parade**Sunday, July 26**(11:00am-1:00pm) - Richland Center Meet & Greet**Tuesday, July 28**(6:00pm-8:00pm) - Farmers Union Town Hall**Wednesday, July 29**(5:00pm-9:15pm) - Galesville Meet & Greet**Thursday, July 30**(5:00pm-8:00pm) - Boogie with Berge!
---
| | | | | | | | | | | [Sign Up to Volunteer](https://us.list-manage.com/13KgqUZJa1M?e=1362dd258a&c2id=d51b517ba2e5c823fe0a3e4f0e8330f1)
---
| |
# Help Us Reach Voters
---
| |

Some of the most important campaign moments happen one conversation at a time. Canvassing gives voters an opportunity to hear directly about Emily, ask questions, and learn what is at stake in this election.
No previous experience is needed. We will provide the training, materials, and support you need to feel comfortable getting started.
**Thursday, July 23**(12:00pm-2:00pm) - Knock doors in La Crosse**Saturday, July 25**(10:00am-12:00pm) - Knock doors in Stevens Point**Sunday, July 26**(12:00pm-1:00pm) - Knock doors in Eau Claire**Saturday, July 25**(11:00am-1:00pm) - Knock doors in La Crosse**Thursday, July 30**(12:00pm-2:00pm) - Knock doors in La Crosse**Saturday, August 1**(10:00am-11:00am) - Knock doors in Eau Claire**Saturday, August 8**(10:00am-11:00am) - Knock doors in Eau Claire
Want to canvass closer to home or help in another way? Complete our [Canvassing Form](https://us.list-manage.com/i8byqmlq1Wq?e=1362dd258a&c2id=d51b517ba2e5c823fe0a3e4f0e8330f1), and a member of Team Berge will help you find the right opportunity.
---
| [Join a Canvass Launch](https://us.list-manage.com/qPJ_oCglB3v?e=1362dd258a&c2id=d51b517ba2e5c823fe0a3e4f0e8330f1)
---
| |
# Support the Campaign from Anywhere
---
| |

Can’t attend an event this week? There are still several easy ways to help increase Emily’s visibility and reach more voters:
Request a Berge yard sign:[ Yard Sign Request Form](https://us.list-manage.com/uN6nM8DT9HI?e=1362dd258a&c2id=d51b517ba2e5c823fe0a3e4f0e8330f1)Order a Berge shirt and wear it to events, parades, and around town:[ Order Your Shirt Today](https://us.list-manage.com/3kDURDF1Ei_?e=1362dd258a&c2id=d51b517ba2e5c823fe0a3e4f0e8330f1)Submit a written testimonial about why you are supporting Emily:[ Submit a Story](https://us.list-manage.com/mwjiVKnuWrb?e=1362dd258a&c2id=d51b517ba2e5c823fe0a3e4f0e8330f1)Host a postcard writing party with friends, family, or neighbors. This is a great way to help reach voters while building community.Boost social media engagement by liking, commenting on, and sharing campaign posts. Follow Berge for Congress on Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Reddit, and Bluesky.Wear your Berge button around town. Volunteers have shared great stories about conversations started with neighbors, cashiers, servers, and community members just by wearing a button.**Have a question about an event or how to get involved? Just reply to this email and we will help get you connected!**
---
| |
# Thank you for being a part of Team Berge!
---
| |
Winning the La Crosse straw poll is worth celebrating, but the true strength of this campaign is the community building it every day.
Thank you for showing up, spreading the word, and believing in what we can accomplish together. Let’s keep building toward August 11.

body:
I saw this trend on TikTok and wanted to give it a shot

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135798503/635359659/-1080040549?refcode=email-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZThkNDUwMS0wYTg2LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=-R9fIZjEpUk_RvlT2SRVbz35Qavp2UjDoWeuxVmrQQI=) Hey, I saw this trend on TikTok and wanted to give it a shot, so here goes: **Here are five things that I believe are _actually_****worth your money:** [**1) A nice glass of Oregon pinot.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135798504/635359660/1480016760?refcode=email_072226_5things&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZThkNDUwMS0wYTg2LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=-R9fIZjEpUk_RvlT2SRVbz35Qavp2UjDoWeuxVmrQQI=) As one of the few members of Congress lucky enough to call Oregon’s wine country their home, there’s nothing I love more after a long week than enjoying what the Willamette Valley’s wineries have to offer. [**2) Shopping small.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135798505/635359661/1480016760?refcode=email_072226_5things&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZThkNDUwMS0wYTg2LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=-R9fIZjEpUk_RvlT2SRVbz35Qavp2UjDoWeuxVmrQQI=) The only way we grow as a community is if we support our local economy, and I always love seeing the heart and passion poured into small businesses all around Oregon’s 6th District. [**3) Treats for my dog, Cooper.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135798506/635359662/1480016760?refcode=email_072226_5things&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZThkNDUwMS0wYTg2LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=-R9fIZjEpUk_RvlT2SRVbz35Qavp2UjDoWeuxVmrQQI=) This one’s pretty self-explanatory. [**4) Quality time with my family.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135798507/635359663/1480016760?refcode=email_072226_5things&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZThkNDUwMS0wYTg2LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=-R9fIZjEpUk_RvlT2SRVbz35Qavp2UjDoWeuxVmrQQI=) After a long and frustrating week in Washington, going on a hike with my loved ones is my favorite way to unwind and enjoy the presence of the people that matter most to me. [**5) Helping Democrats flip the House blue.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135798508/635359664/1480016760?refcode=email_072226_5things&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZThkNDUwMS0wYTg2LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=-R9fIZjEpUk_RvlT2SRVbz35Qavp2UjDoWeuxVmrQQI=) The only way we can put a check on Trump’s authoritarian regime and put our country back on the right track is if we can take back the House majority. And if you agree, then I have to ask: **[We can’t take back the House without defending this seat. So, if you think delivering results for working families is worth the money, then will you pitch in to help me protect OR-06 and put Democrats on the path to the majority this November?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135798509/635359665/1480016760?refcode=email_072226_5things&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZThkNDUwMS0wYTg2LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=-R9fIZjEpUk_RvlT2SRVbz35Qavp2UjDoWeuxVmrQQI=)** _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | | [Donate $5 →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135798510/635359666/1480016760?express_lane=true&amounts=5,15,25,50,100,250,500&amount=5&refcode=email_072226_5things&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZThkNDUwMS0wYTg2LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=-R9fIZjEpUk_RvlT2SRVbz35Qavp2UjDoWeuxVmrQQI=)

[](https://act.adamschiff.com/signup/aschiff_email_072226_warpowers?t=6&amount=10&refcode=aschiff_email_072226_warpowers&akid=10009%2E5257348%2EBaREOE)
Derek, We are, in real time, seeing the problems that come with embarking on a war of choice. A war that the president got this country involved in — not because we were attacked or because there was an imminent threat of attack, but because he chose to do so. Endless hostilities. Soaring gas prices at home. Eighteen American families who have already buried a son or daughter. All of this without a single vote of approval from the U.S. Senate. **Congress has _never_ authorized this conflict: not when the bombing began, not at the 60-day mark this spring, and not when the ceasefire collapsed and the strikes resumed. Only Congress can declare war, and it has not.** _Since this war started, I’ve worked to force vote after vote on it._ The Senate has voted nearly a dozen times on war powers resolutions to end this conflict, and each time the record moves further in our direction. On June 23 it finally passed such a resolution — 50 to 48, four Republicans joining us — directing the president to withdraw our troops. That is the strongest bipartisan vote yet on Iran. So I’m filing a new War Powers Resolution — and I need your help to draw attention to it. The louder our voices, the harder we are to ignore. **[Derek, add your name in support of my latest War Powers Resolution →](https://act.adamschiff.com/signup/aschiff_email_072226_warpowers?t=10&amount=10&refcode=aschiff_email_072226_warpowers&akid=10009%2E5257348%2EBaREOE)** | | [ADD YOUR NAME→](https://act.adamschiff.com/signup/aschiff_email_072226_warpowers?t=11&amount=10&refcode=aschiff_email_072226_warpowers&akid=10009%2E5257348%2EBaREOE)

This has to be the moment we stand up. This has to be the moment we say: enough.
Thank you,
Adam

Friend, Rent is up almost 50% since 2019 and home prices are at an all-time high. Chronic homelessness in my city of Detroit rose 33% last year. Other costs of living keep increasing — from groceries to healthcare, utilities, and insurance payments. **I’m working in Congress to make life better and more affordable for you, including lowering these costs of living, ensuring the human right to safe and affordable housing, and increasing financial stability.** **My**** _Housing Our Communities Act_****officially became law this month** , as part of a bipartisan housing bill. It directs the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to establish a grant program to **increase the supply of affordable housing in our neighborhood****s**. A reliable and safe roof over one’s head can be a matter of life and death. **I’m also spearheading the****Economic Dignity for All Agenda****to provide regular cash assistance directly to individuals and families nationwide.** Most American families live paycheck to paycheck, but these transformative policies can help alleviate financial stress, save lives, and build economic security for all, by:
* sending every family a monthly payment of $458 for every child they are caring for
* providing $250 per month to adults aged 19 to 67 years old
* support newborns and cover new expenses by providing every family with $2,000 upon the birth of their child

[**Will you join me in calling on Congress to help families get through the affordability crisis and end poverty by sending universal payments to Americans, including passing the bills in my****Economic Dignity For All Agenda****?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38h9nrsCCiMen3CGd5zila9jzJnep0tjRIZRggydvVqTMlW2P8xMczdT67OrReJtwwTGgivIrbvUw3aFvxj8uBcPrXvbdYaokpZYNEGq5uKnNmSykDS3xSDQbjeRjZLSsOzm8R0tgLkAu5GhD4SxaeXNwjrTPpH803SquptY0deVXYFbIOkBU_rFVznAACXFNnwrh6GQsk6kmXexgCQID6eMk0G4Ma7t7AEi6ogWpQrGy6tKu8UHetv1ZONaiwLYSbifYQyv1GYBlCtdljxoBj4Lk0B4b6w-GinraLD6aY5wy5rdASraxpNOoTqqy5cim5mIeh1wlFo6JszVIggORbELZuSyKKPFk9vG0KcKQu3HTWzbS9pkXsOsOlNybHWmx0kqwhntG5RqzXJPrcAud_b/4sj/51GlSVrxQTWQs_aTllKzpw/h1/h001.LYYaQkGWGj4kFREIzqo3_PgtbSYxeZWX7nYzDU73PM8) | [DEMAND DIGNITY FOR ALL](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38h9nrsCCiMen3CGd5zila9jzJnep0tjRIZRggydvVqTMlW2P8xMczdT67OrReJtwwTGgivIrbvUw3aFvxj8uBcPrXvbdYaokpZYNEGq5uKnN1kIwMir9_cegQtBhg1oENCJ124fEmfRt5gQ8Z_p8gZleBy3P64D48oin9CDybtiowRBdI_qmwGCr-pymZ26U2v7oxJxaXCjaY5tNJaDIUlQxFJ4Q-9gWtqHiLmSdhhnm2V3sMIf7mSWxrCT9RJlu97ilNjd8utYCuej6khqpDQItjFYns6ghKRRs6qv-l1dhVcMHrL1UoUuqccERkuohfVQYK6wSy-0U2qWtJd3MYU_DETXFm7kaXCELwRSVv0NGumXstt8_qWG9eM2_KWk4hPg8PJe3l8B3-kqPmdgL3O/4sj/51GlSVrxQTWQs_aTllKzpw/h2/h001.4biTjge4hpGonRda7I06TAHA1nWd2ufRkbSm8xYWFPU)

Families in Michigan and across the country are in dire need of urgent relief to survive and pay their bills.
It’s a policy choice to keep people struggling in poverty. Congress can vote on and pass policies to break the cycle of poverty and provide urgently needed financial stability.
For example, over 160 successful pilot programs across the country have shown that sending cash directly to people saves lives, dramatically reduces poverty, and stimulates local economies.
The ongoing payments laid out in my Economic Dignity for All package of bills would all be administered by the Social Security Administration, which already sends out monthly checks to 50 million seniors.
**This legislation would cut poverty in the U.S. by 45%, cut child poverty by two-thirds, and nearly eliminate deep child poverty.**
As the People’s Policy Project wrote, this “would lift millions of Americans above the poverty line, expanding economic security on a scale not seen since the New Deal and Great Society eras.”
[**Please add your name to demand Congress pass policies that help ensure that every family and child has the resources they need to not only survive, but flourish.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38h9nrsCCiMen3CGd5zila9jzJnep0tjRIZRggydvVqTMlW2P8xMczdT67OrReJtwwTGgivIrbvUw3aFvxj8uBcPrXvbdYaokpZYNEGq5uKnP_cUv47kChCihZfJx47DSgJ7SbGMZmSp0Lpsc4eXoY5PN0EnBvWyfK3jrWsqHfNnEc9dT1x5ZDlP-IpacDg1FPtPSovO8jNNqSH4zQI8AEcQjrDKEaGzLD2Zr7VqJn4IWBWH_8Q7Iy4gIiLb7WYGhiCGQFeewIZBaVbLiccd9UJ1cgHRbQytmOBRPRhXwcFEecxKuPWbKp1ucfrbXWO1fS1klXXyGL_RoIXBUlVvwMpk8f_7AV_6qcxxvPBSb66Bq_IcoIoy4T1PNQnLiqHyGfzWdnM7H1s6X63a8eMTLvs/4sj/51GlSVrxQTWQs_aTllKzpw/h3/h001.2XnG88op3oLtVyQTjCCEWwO3B4Geigoljc_nVyrSNgQ)

Thank you for taking action. I promise I’ll never stop fighting for you in Congress.
I’ve brought **$68 million in federal funding for over 55 community projects in my district, from home repairs to healthcare clinics.** My team has resolved 13,000 constituents’ cases, returning **$12.6 million back to district residents** by securing payments for tax returns and programs such as Social Security.
I’m leading additional legislation to expand our social safety net and get closer to economic justice for all, including policies to:
* stop grocery stores’ price gouging
* cancel medical and utility debt
* end unjust wealth disparities
* get big money out of politics
* keep families in their homes
* stop modern-day redlining in auto insurance
* end the subminimum tipped wage (which is just $2.13 an hour)
* lower the cost of prescription drugs
* establish the first-ever permanent, federal low-income water affordability program to stop water shutoffs and help families pay their water bills
* correct credit history for victims of predatory lending, fraud, and economic abuse — and people with medically necessary debt

**I’ve also stopped evictions and water shutoffs** , and I’m fighting back against Trump’s attacks on our rights to housing, including his attempts to gut HUD and undermine the enforcement of our fair housing laws.
When we build power together, our vision for a better world is possible.
Always serving you and fighting for better,
Rashida

Chronic homelessness in my city of Detroit rose 33% last year. Other costs of living keep increasing — from groceries to healthcare, utilities, and insurance payments. I’m working in Congress to make life better and more affordable for you, including lowering these costs of living, ensuring the human right to safe and affordable housing, and increasing financial stability. My Housing Our Communities Actofficially became law this month , as part of a bipartisan housing bill. It directs the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to establish a grant program to increase the supply of affordable housing in our neighborhoods. A reliable and safe roof over one’s head can be a matter of life and death. I’m also spearheading theEconomic Dignity for All Agendato provide regular cash assistance directly to individuals and families nationwide. Most American families live paycheck to paycheck, but these transformative policies can help alleviate financial stress, save lives, and build economic security for all, by: sending every family a monthly payment of $458 for every child they are caring for providing $250 per month to adults aged 19 to 67 years old support newborns and cover new expenses by providing every family with $2,000 upon the birth of their child | Families in Michigan and across the country are in dire need of urgent relief to survive and pay their bills. It’s a policy choice to keep people struggling in poverty. Congress can vote on and pass policies to break the cycle of poverty and provide urgently needed financial stability. For example, over 160 successful pilot programs across the country have shown that sending cash directly to people saves lives, dramatically reduces poverty, and stimulates local economies. The ongoing payments laid out in my Economic Dignity for All package of bills would all be administered by the Social Security Administration, which already sends out monthly checks to 50 million seniors. This legislation would cut poverty in the U.S. by 45%, cut child poverty by two-thirds, and nearly eliminate deep child poverty. As the People’s Policy Project wrote, this “would lift millions of Americans above the poverty line, expanding economic security on a scale not seen since the New Deal and Great Society eras.” Thank you for taking action. Trump is trying to take away your right to vote. Here’s how you can hold him accountable. | |

Peter, Trump went on prime-time TV to give a rambling, lie-filled speech about our elections. _Even David Ellison’s CBS News had to cut away._ The next day, his DHS Secretary announced that he would unilaterally **withhold federal funding from states that refuse to bend their voting laws to Trump’s whims.** _Now Congress is getting in on the scheme to take away your voting rights._ MAGA Republicans are trying to attach the _SAVE Act_ to unrelated, must-pass legislation to keep the government funded and our troops paid. **They know this attack cannot stand on its own, so they are trying to jam it through by holding everything else hostage.** 🚨 **Let’s be very clear: This is Trump’s election takeover.** And it is part of the same dark money project that captured the Supreme Court. Wealthy donors spent _decades_ building a Court that would deliver for them. Now Trump is trying to rig the elections before voters can elect a Congress with the power to expose their corruption, investigate the captured Court, and rein them in. [**Send a message to Congress right now. That is a wannabe dictator trying to change the rules before the people can stop him.** Trump knows his party will lose a fair election. He knows a Democratic Congress would expose his corruption, the corruption around the captured Supreme Court, and the billionaire donors and power players keeping this rigged system in place. **So they are spending big and breaking the rules to keep Trump Republicans in power.** And when they restrict the right to vote, they limit power to fight for everything else: housing, groceries, prescription drugs, fair wages, clean air, safe communities, and a government that answers to working people. Fellow Conservative,

Last week, President Trump addressed the nation in a primetime speech on election security.

**ABC and NBC refused to air it.**

Not because it was dangerous. Not because it was illegal. Because they didn't want the American people to hear the TRUTH about voter fraud in our country.

Think about that, Fellow Conservative. The President of the United States requested airtime to speak to the American people — and two of the biggest networks in the country said no. _They decided for you what you should and shouldn't see._

President Trump called it exactly what it is: censorship. He said the networks are "a part" of the fraud — that they want to "keep it going" and "protect the radical left." He's right.

**This is not a free press. This is a propaganda machine.**
