The Al-Masri family home in Gaza City after it was bombed by the Israeli military, killing a couple and their four children as they slept on July 21, 2026. Gaza City. Screenshot of video by Abdel Qader Sabbah.
_Story by Abdel Qader Sabbah, Mohamed Ahmed, Sharif Abdel Kouddous, and Jawa Ahmad_
GAZA CITY--The charred shell of the Al-Masri family home in the Sabra neighborhood of Gaza City was still smoldering on Tuesday afternoon, hours after the Israel military bombed it, killing Firas and Salsabeel al-Masri and their four children--Faryal, Salma, Amira and Naim--as they slept.
The airstrike came without warning in the middle of the night, destroying the upper floor of the simple two-story structure and setting it ablaze. "We were asleep in the middle of the night, at around 2 a.m. or so, when we heard a huge explosion," Abu Youssef Al-Masri, the children's grandfather, told Drop Site as he stood in front of the partially collapsed home. "We realized the house had been struck. The house collapsed and caught fire."
The fire spared nothing inside, family belongings burnt to ash lay among broken cinder blocks, the walls that remained standing blackened with soot.
"The house burned completely. It was my brother's home--he, his wife, and their four children. Burned until it was charred. My brother's entire family has been erased," Mohammed Al-Masri, the brother of Firas, said. "They burned before our eyes and we couldn't do anything." He spoke standing at the graveyard where the family of six were buried on Tuesday afternoon.
The bodies were carried by relatives wrapped in white shrouds through the rubble-strewn cemetery to be laid to rest. Abu Youssef stood in the middle of the shallow graves and placed the small body of his granddaughter, Amira, next to her mother as Israeli drones buzzed incessantly overhead. "The whole world is watching us," Mohammed said. "There is no ceasefire in effect, the war hasn't stopped, and no one cares about us."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/bc7c3602-9f2d-4100-9cd2-63e10fd83ef3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
###### Relatives bury Firas and Salsabeel al-Masri and their four children after they were killed in an Israeli airstrike on their home in Gaza City on July 21, 2026. Video by Abdel Qader Sabbah.
The attack on Tuesday came amid a particularly brutal and escalated Israeli assault across Gaza over the past several days as the world's attention has been distracted by the renewed U.S. war with Iran. Daily airstrikes, shelling, quadcopter attacks, and shootings have targeted residential buildings, tent encampments, civilian vehicles, a funeral procession, a police station, and a hospital-turned-shelter, killing dozens of Palestinians across the enclave over the past week alone. At the same time, Israeli ground troops have been pushing further into Gaza, steadily extending the "yellow line" westward, taking more land, and driving the Palestinian population onto an ever-shrinking territory.
"It's not simply that the resumption of the war in Iran provides cover, it's also the fact that the war has largely been a failure from an Israeli perspective, and the Israeli state will look to compensate for this failure elsewhere before a new regional balance takes shape," Nasser Abourahme, a professor of Middle Eastern and North African Studies at Bowdoin College, told Drop Site. "It's most important to remember that the genocide itself has both stalled and never stopped. For all the horrific and unprecedented destruction and death, Israel hasn't yet achieved any of its core aims: the ethnic cleansing of the Strip, the disarming of the resistance factions, or the resettlement of the Strip."
The latest killing spree has brought the Palestinian death toll in Gaza since a so-called ceasefire went into effect in October 2025 to 1,180--including over 250 children--with 127 being killed in the first three weeks of July. Over 3,800 have been injured. The total recorded death toll since Israel launched its genocidal assault in October 2023 is now over 73,300 killed, with nearly 174,000 injured, according to Gaza's health ministry.
On Monday, an Israeli airstrike slammed into the Al-Yemen Al-Saeed Hospital building in the Jabaliya refugee camp, [killing](https://substack.com/redirect/d4eb0e06-a06f-40bb-993e-824ed993ae26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least four people and wounding several more. Like many hospitals in Gaza, the facility entirely ceased functioning during the war and is instead being used primarily as a shelter for displaced Palestinians.
"I went out to visit my friend near Al-Yemen Al-Saeed and suddenly there was a very large explosion, two consecutive explosions," Youssef Akasha, an eyewitness who was just meters away from the attack, told Drop Site as he stood outside Shifa Hospital in Gaza City where the dead and wounded were being brought. Bloodied children were carried out of ambulances while bodies wrapped in blankets were put on gurneys. "The children were having fun, playing football, and suddenly they started screaming. We went directly to Al-Yemen Al-Saeed...we found the place destroyed and children were lying on the ground, women screaming, and men running to rescue the wounded."
One of the worst attacks came on Friday, when Israel [bombed](https://substack.com/redirect/1577f98a-68ff-418a-ac59-115971d27d83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a funeral procession outside the Ahmed Yassin Mosque in the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, killing at least eight mourners as they gathered to bury a man killed just hours earlier. Bodies lay strewn on the blood-soaked ground. One man was blown in half, his legs torn off his body as crowds of people screaming on the street tried to rescue the wounded. At Al-Awda hospital, injured children lay wide-eyed and silent on hospital beds as doctors rushed to treat them. One man knelt and embraced a bloodied corpse lying on a gurney, unable to let go.
"It was a very big attack and there was a large number of martyrs," Medhat Saleh, an eyewitness who was wounded in his right arm, told Drop Site. "We couldn't have imagined they would bomb a funeral of this size. Many children, women, and men...A massacre in every sense of the word. The people were piled on top of each other, torn apart." He continued, "It's gotten much, much worse. In recent days, this has become a daily occurrence."
The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Thameen Al-Kheetan, made note of the escalated Israel assault in a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/ff15a5d8-c8f4-4092-9bcb-5bc560822f0d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday. "The Israeli military has intensified its attacks in Gaza in recent days, killing and injuring dozens of Palestinians--children, women and men...Nine months after the announcement of a ceasefire, still, nowhere is safe for Palestinians in Gaza," Kheetan said, noting that the UN had documented 57 Palestinians killed between July 13 and July 20 alone. "Meanwhile, the Palestinian population in Gaza remains trapped in an ever-shrinking area, with the 'yellow line' constantly being moved westwards by the Israeli occupying power, presenting a continuous threat to life as the Israeli military appears to routinely fire on Palestinians for mere presence in the vicinity of that line...The violations, the suffering and the misery that continue to be imposed on the Palestinians in Gaza cannot be ignored."
As part of the October 2025 agreement, Israeli troops withdrew to the "yellow line," a boundary running roughly parallel to the coastline and cutting off large swathes of north and south Gaza, that gave Israel control of 53% of the enclave. The move was supposed to mark the beginning of an eventual phased withdrawal back to a "buffer zone" at the border with Israel. Yet over the past nine months, the Israeli military has instead steadily pushed further westward in areas along the yellow line, taking more Palestinian land and placing yellow concrete blocks in some places to indicate their new line of control, which is now estimated to encompass closer to 70% of Gaza, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/b3be4754-2296-49d6-a80e-340950fd83ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Israeli military officials.
"The escalation of the killing, the expansion of the so-called yellow line in new land grabs, and the agitation of politicians and the settler movement for renewed Jewish settlement in Gaza all point to the fact that Israel's endgame remains the ethnic cleansing of Gaza and its full conquest one way or another," Abourahme said. "At the end of the day, the so-called ceasefire didn't stop the genocide, it only modulated its tempo and intensity."
For the past several days, Israeli ground troops have launched a sustained attack on areas near the Zeitoun neighborhood in Gaza City, including aerial bombing, shooting, and shelling attacks, razing land with bulldozers, and issuing displacement orders to force residents to flee their homes and shelters and drive them eastward.
"Today, they moved the yellow line here. The day before, they bombed the area, so we left. We spent one more night at home, then we had to leave," Umm Salem Dawla, a resident displaced from the area, told Drop Site. "We gathered our belongings and left them at the camp. I keep saying I'll go and sit by the cemetery. What can I tell you? What kind of life is this?"
On Wednesday, the troops pulled back and residents in the area found yellow concrete blocks placed at the Dawlah junction on Salah al-Din street--the main north-south thoroughfare running the length of the enclave.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/592c612f-49e7-48f1-9540-ee672f79d755?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
###### The Israeli military forced residents to flee from the Zeitoun neighborhood in Gaza City and placed yellow blocks on Salah al-Din street on July 22, 2026. Video by Abdel Qader Sabbah.
"The Israelis started shelling the area, tanks started firing at us and at our home so we fled because the situation was extremely difficult...the tanks are always visible in the street, firing at our homes, and the quadcopters are constantly overhead. They don't leave us alone. Twenty four hours a day there is shelling and gunfire," Assem Dawla, another displaced resident of Zeitoun, said. "As you can see, we're now taking out our belongings and leaving because the occupation has advanced the yellow line to Salah al-Din street. There is no longer any possibility of life here. Life in Zeitoun has been wiped out. There is no hope left and no way to live here anymore."
The Israeli military's encroachment to the Dawlah junction in effect prevents Palestinians in this area of Gaza City from accessing Salah al-Din road and the rest of the enclave further south.
"My fear is that all of Gaza will end up inside the occupation's new boundaries. Netanyahu is now talking about taking 67% to 70% of the Gaza Strip, but I believe he wants to control all of it. There won't be anywhere left for us. We'll all be living under the control and domination of the Israeli army," Dawla said. "The war is not over. We're still living in a state of fear, greater even than when the war was ongoing."

The attack on Tuesday came amid a particularly brutal and escalated Israeli assault across Gaza over the past several days as the world's attention has been distracted by the renewed U.S. war with Iran. Daily airstrikes, shelling, quadcopter attacks, and shootings have targeted residential buildings, tent encampments, civilian vehicles, a funeral procession, a police station, and a hospital-turned-shelter, killing dozens of Palestinians across the enclave over the past week alone. At the same time, Israeli ground troops have been pushing further into Gaza, steadily extending the "yellow line" westward, taking more land, and driving the Palestinian population onto an ever-shrinking territory. "It's not simply that the resumption of the war in Iran provides cover, it's also the fact that the war has largely been a failure from an Israeli perspective, and the Israeli state will look to compensate for this failure elsewhere before a new regional balance takes shape," Nasser Abourahme, a professor of Middle Eastern and North African Studies at Bowdoin College, told Drop Site. "It's most important to remember that the genocide itself has both stalled and never stopped. For all the horrific and unprecedented destruction and death, Israel hasn't yet achieved any of its core aims: the ethnic cleansing of the Strip, the disarming of the resistance factions, or the resettlement of the Strip." One of the worst attacks came on Friday, when Israel a funeral procession outside the Ahmed Yassin Mosque in the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, killing at least eight mourners as they gathered to bury a man killed just hours earlier. Bodies lay strewn on the blood-soaked ground. One man was blown in half, his legs torn off his body as crowds of people screaming on the street tried to rescue the wounded. body:
New Marquette Law School Poll
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260722-3068)
Peter,
Well, folks, today has been a day of polls. Along with the long-awaited Marquette Law School Poll, we also saw internal polls released from two of our opponents.
While the Marquette Law School Poll was completed before the field shifted last week, the other two polls went out early this week.
The good news? We’re leading in all three.
[__](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260722.aOxfa7&refcode=em20260722-3068&t=1&akid=3068%2E105371%2E2fMrDg)_We love to see it!_
Marquette has Fran at 26%, 11 percentage points ahead of her nearest opponent. A newer poll commissioned by the Barnes campaign has her at 39%, leading Barnes by 13 percentage points.
And a poll commissioned by the Crowley campaign has Fran at 35%, 20 percentage points ahead of Barnes and 21 percentage points ahead of Crowley. In other words: Every poll released today, including two paid for by our opponents, shows Fran with a double-digit lead.
Like we always say, a poll is only a snapshot, but three snapshots from three different pollsters definitely leaves us feeling optimistic that our message is resonating with voters across the state.
This is extremely exciting news, but it's also going to spur opposition from corporations and special interests to pile money into this race. Fran stands up to the AI data center lobby and the charter school lobby, and fights for working people even when it’s not easy (and as we can see people are responding!)

If everyone was able to give $47, our average donation, we would reach our goal before the day ended.

Francesca

I’ve never campaigned like the establishment says you’re supposed to.
I don’t like doing “call time” asking wealthy people to write big checks, and I don’t attend fancy cocktail-party fundraisers.
We’ve created a new way to do politics — one rooted in community organizing and in building a movement of working-class voices that have gone unheard for far too long.
My husband and I run an independent auto repair shop. Every day, we meet people trying to keep an aging car on the road because replacing it isn’t an option. We see what an unexpected repair bill means for a family balancing groceries, rent, childcare, and everything else life throws their way. Those conversations shape every vote I take in Congress.

subject: The final chapter of this race just began
body:
[1]LeftNet

[ https://act.leftnet.org/go/21450?c0=leftnet_em20260722_partner_ms_kh_em_leftnet.ofXWiM&refcode=em20260722-1686&amount=5&t=1001&akid=1686%2E2118727%2E1rtrLD ][IMG]

I will officially face off against MAGA extremist Andy Biggs in the
general election this November.

[ https://act.leftnet.org/go/21450?c0=leftnet_em20260722_partner_ms_kh_em_leftnet.ofXWiM&refcode=em20260722-1686&amount=5&t=1002&akid=1686%2E2118727%2E1rtrLD ]Rush a donation of $5 to kickstart my re-election
campaign as we enter the final chapter of this toss-up race.

If you don’t know who Biggs is, he is nearly identical to my 2022
opponent, Kari Lake, who we narrowly defeated by less than 1 percent of
the vote.

He’s denied the 2020 election results and pushed bogus conspiracy
theories, he’s attacked our reproductive rights, and he’s loyally
supported every part of the MAGA agenda that’s actively hurting Arizona’s
working families.

We’re not surprised Biggs won this primary — he was hand-picked by Donald
Trump and backed by far-right groups like Turning Point USA long before he
became the official Republican nominee for governor.

Now, the full force of the Republican machine will rapidly pour their
resources from millionaires, billionaires, and super PACs into this race

| | **_Meet Rob:_** Born and raised in Kingston, PA, Rob Bresnahan is currently serving his first term as PA-08’s homegrown Congressman. He’s a fifth-generation Northeastern Pennsylvanian, and the only representative in Congress who is part of the National Electrical Contractors Association. A product of the American Dream, Rob learned the true meaning of hard work by getting his hands dirty early and often. He wired junction boxes, ran heavy equipment, drove trucks, and learned the value of an honest day’s work in the process. His family instilled the values of hard work, discipline, and perseverance in him at a young age – and Rob has stayed true to these foundational values all his life. At just 19 years old, Rob joined his family’s business as the CFO for Kuharchik Construction. He became the CEO of the company in 2013. Rob spent over a decade working and connecting with blue-collar Americans across the country before running for Congress in 2024. He was outspent 2:1 in his race against a 12-year Democrat that year, but the people of Northeastern Pennsylvania demanded change when they sent Rob to be their fighter in Washington. Through his experience as an electrical contractor, Rob saw the real world struggles facing America’s blue-collar workers first hand. Wages are not keeping up with the skyrocketing cost of living, and Americans who wake up every day and pay their dues are being left out to dry by their elected officials. But Rob’s voting record in Congress tells a different story. He’s stood up for hardworking Americans at every opportunity, regardless of partisan politics. Simply put, Rob Bresnahan brings both insight and candid concern for blue-collar America to Congress that your run-of-the-mill representatives don’t. Every day that he steps foot on Capitol Hill, Rob is 100% devoted to restoring America’s energy independence, deregulating the economy, and bringing well-paying jobs back to the great commonwealth of Pennsylvania. Fellow Patriot,

After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate.

**President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's _"Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate._**

I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, _**but I am ready.**_

I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge.

It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times.

I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for.

I did not seek this moment, Fellow Patriot.

clean_body: I'm ready for the fight ahead, and I'm all in to run for the United States Senate. | Fellow Patriot, After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate. President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's "Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate. I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, but I am ready. I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge. It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times. I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for. I did not seek this moment, Fellow Patriot. But after many prayers and speaking with my family, I know I am making the right decision to run for this seat. I'll be straight with you - I am behind financially. My opponents are self-funding millionaires or have spent years building up their campaign war chests, but I'm new to politics. We have less than 3 weeks to run against people who have been at this for years. Since you were there for Lindsey, Thank you for everything you did for Lindsey over the years. I know that having people like you in his corner meant everything to him. God bless, Darline Graham P.S. It's been a difficult week. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

And that’s why I’ll always fight for you

| |

Peter, I've spent my life traveling this commonwealth, and no matter where I go, I meet people who work hard.

People raising families. Running small businesses. Working long shifts. Looking after their neighbors. Doing everything they can to build a good life.

Unlike some politicians, I've never believed the problem is that Kentuckians aren't working hard enough. The real problem is that it's gotten harder and harder for that hard work to pay off. The system is not holding up its end of the deal.

That's one of the reasons I'm running for governor.

I believe no one should ever have to leave their corner of Kentucky in order to build a better life. And I believe government ought to be helping people do exactly that instead of making it harder to stay.

subject: We want to make sure you saw Paul Eaton’s email
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTEVETS, VOTEVETS
body:
#
Peter,
Paul Eaton reached out yesterday about stopping the Arc de Trump.
If you missed it, check it out below:
* * *
Peter, I need to tell you where the fight to stop Trump’s arch stands, because it’s getting worse.
Two weeks ago, a federal commission packed with Trump appointees voted 8 to 1 to advance the Arc de Trump — 250 feet tall, sitting on Memorial Circle, at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery.
They heard nearly three hours of public opposition first. Veterans. Families. People who understand what that place means to this country. The commission listened, then voted to advance the arch anyway.
This isn't final. But it's closer than it's ever been.
The sightline between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington was designed on purpose — a quiet symbol of a reunited country — and Trump wants to put a monument to himself in the middle of it.
I've spent enough of my life on the grounds of Arlington National Cemetery to know its gravity. My father, killed in action during the Vietnam War, is buried there. Men who I trained, who served under me, are buried there. It is not the backdrop for some draft-dodging coward’s vanity.
So we're asking for $5. That's it.
$5 because Trump’s commission could force this through before most people even hear what’s happened.
$5 because we're up against a President who's made this one of the top priorities of his administration.
But really, $5 or anything you can afford. Because whatever you can give, right now, matters more than the amount itself.
[**Can we count on you? Chip in that $5 and help VoteVets raise enough hell that they can't force the Arc de Trump through in secret. Enough to stop this, once and for all.**](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-jul26.EhtcQh&refcode=em260722-1-120&t=1&akid=35378%2E3013755%2Ea2CPgr)

---
****
We've stopped Trump before.
With your help, we’ll stop this, too.
Very respectfully,
Paul Eaton
Major General, U.S. Army, Retired
Senior Advisor, VoteVets

subject: Why JD Vance’s story meant so much to Charlie Kirk
body:
| | | |
---
| | | Fellow Patriot,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Fellow Patriot, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith.

clean_body: | | | | | | | Fellow Patriot, Faith is essential to the survival and success of America. Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth. He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him. He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country. That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt. That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith. Fellow Patriot, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story... It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now. So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together. Young people face that pressure every single day. They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is. JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion. He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back. That's what Communion is about... And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now. That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith. Your support does far more than just send you a book... It helps Turning Point USA reach young people in the very places where faith is under attack. Because of supporters like you, students on more than 5,000 campuses are hearing something they may not hear anywhere else: a serious defense of faith, truth, and a life rooted in God. For many of them, that's the first time anyone has challenged the lies they have been fed. And for many of them, that's where their minds begin to change -- and so do their lives. Charlie believed the next generation was worth fighting for. He believed young people were not beyond reach -- they needed someone willing to meet them where this battle is being fought and tell them the truth clearly and directly. That's why your support matters. It helps Turning Point USA keep showing up. And it helps carry forward the mission Charlie gave his life to build. | | | Now's the time to act. Now's the time to restore faith in God and faith in America before another generation drifts even farther from both. And with you, Charlie's mission will reach further -- and touch more young lives -- than ever before. For Charlie, The Turning Point USA Team P.S. Fellow Patriot, many young people leave home with a foundation of faith, only to have the culture chip away at it, piece by piece. JD Vance knows what that struggle looks like. So do countless young Americans who Turning Point USA is reaching right now. 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044

name: KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION
subject: The time is now...
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION * 6709 West 119th Street * Ste
body:
Make your voice heard, get out to Early Vote!

| | | | | |
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Friends,The time is now.Early voting began Saturday, and turnout so far has been lower than expected. That means every single vote matters.This election will determine the fiscal future and direction of Johnson County for years to come.Over the past several years, families have watched their property taxes skyrocket while county spending has nearly doubled. Residents have been speaking up, but too often their concerns have been dismissed. The current message from Mike Kelly is that we need "steady leadership" because everything is working.**I respectfully disagree.** History teaches us that organizations rarely fail because no one saw the warning signs. They fail because leaders choose not to listen.Whether it was the Titanic sailing toward an iceberg, Kodak ignoring digital photography, or Blockbuster dismissing streaming, the warning signs were there. The problem wasn't that they were invisible. The problem was that they were ignored.Johnson County is not beyond saving, but we cannot continue down the same path and expect a different result. If we don't bring discipline back to county spending, protect taxpayers, and restore accountability, today's challenges will become tomorrow's crisis.That is why I am running for County Commission Chair.My entire career has been about facing difficult problems head-on, making responsible financial decisions, and building organizations that serve people well. I won't ignore the warning signs, and I won't ignore the voices of the people who elected me.Please make your voting plan today, whether you vote early or on Election Day. Your vote truly matters.[**EARLY VOTING INFORMATION**](https://us.list-manage.com/cNo44vDlGaB?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)[**ELECTION DAY POLLING LOCATION – AUGUST 4**](https://us.list-manage.com/CjeBNvVA3ND?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494) I would be honored to earn your vote and the opportunity to serve as your Johnson County Commission Chair.Working hard on your behalf,Karen

Residents have been speaking up, but too often their concerns have been dismissed. The current message from Mike Kelly is that we need "steady leadership" because everything is working.I respectfully disagree. History teaches us that organizations rarely fail because no one saw the warning signs. They fail because leaders choose not to listen.Whether it was the Titanic sailing toward an iceberg, Kodak ignoring digital photography, or Blockbuster dismissing streaming, the warning signs were there. The problem wasn't that they were invisible. The problem was that they were ignored.Johnson County is not beyond saving, but we cannot continue down the same path and expect a different result. If we don't bring discipline back to county spending, protect taxpayers, and restore accountability, today's challenges will become tomorrow's crisis.That is why I am running for County Commission Chair.My entire career has been about facing difficult problems head-on, making responsible financial decisions, and building organizations that serve people well. I won't ignore the warning signs, and I won't ignore the voices of the people who elected me.Please make your voting plan today, whether you vote early or on Election Day. Your vote truly matters. I would be honored to earn your vote and the opportunity to serve as your Johnson County Commission Chair.Working hard on your behalf,Karen | | | | | | | | | PAID FOR BY KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION 6709 West 119th Street Ste. 224 Overland Park, KS 66209 USA or |

name: Ryan Helfert
subject: THANK YOU - Upcoming Event with Congressman Ryan Mackenzie
body:
[cid:a99ea7ff-b936-42dd-a249-11b3c6967784]

Team Mackenzie,
I wanted to take a moment to personally thank everyone for the incredible work you're doing. I truly can't say enough about this team. Your dedication, enthusiasm, and commitment to talking with voters have been nothing short of amazing. Our grassroots effort is growing because of volunteers like you.
UPCOMING EVENT:
This Sunday, July 26, we officially kick off the final 100 days until VICTORY!
Please join Congressman Mackenzie for our 100 Days to Victory Launch:
Northampton County Republican Office
2523 Willow Park Rd.
Bethlehem, PA
TIME: 1:30 P.M.
DATE: Sunday, July 26th
We'll be hitting the doors, making phone calls, and building the momentum that will carry us through Election Day. Bring your friends, family, neighbors; everyone is welcome to join the team. Light refreshments will be provided.
It is truly humbling to be surrounded by so many people who are willing to give their time and energy to make a difference. Your support means more than you know, and this campaign would not be possible without you.
Let's make these next 100 days count. Let's Win and continue to Deliver for Our Community.
Thank you again for everything you do. I can't wait to see you on Sunday!

Thank you,

Ryan Helfert

Battlestation Director PA-07 | Team Mackenzie

(814) 490-4583 | rhelfert@nrcc.org<mailto:rhelfert@nrcc.org>

Something is happening across Pennsylvania.
Over the last several weeks, one thing has become impossible to ignore:
**The more Pennsylvanians hear from Josh Shapiro, the less impressed they become.**
The latest Quinnipiac poll shows that despite spending million of dollars on advertising, Josh Shapiro’s numbers are plummeting.
Pennsylvanians are asking tough questions.
They’re asking [**why energy costs continue to rise**](https://us.list-manage.com/_CNE3BkstNa?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd) in a state sitting on some of the largest natural gas reserves in the world.

And they’re looking for a Governor who will actually listen.
Stacy Garrity has spent years traveling to all 67 counties, meeting with families, small business owners, veterans, farmers, first responders, and workers across our Commonwealth.
**She isn’t running to build a political brand. She’s running to get Pennsylvania back on the right track.**

| | Peter - It’s Ciro, Lawler’s Campaign Manager. I just got off a call with our media team, and this needs to go to our grassroots supporters like you who are funding this race.
_**_Democrats are already spending real money attacking Mike, and attacking you._**_
They have already invested thousands of dollars and are currently running attack ads on streaming platforms across the Hudson Valley. Hulu. YouTube. Peacock. Roku. You name it! Every device in your living room is now serving the radical left’s dark money version of what happened in Congress this year, and Mike is not on the air to answer any of it.
Not because he does not want to be. Because we haven’t raised enough to air all of our ads yet. Here is what streaming ads actually do at this stage of a race:
* They plant the first impression with undecided voters before Labor Day
* They stack up unanswered, night after night, across every household in NY-17
* They cost real money to counter once they are already running

Today I had the opportunity to join Walker Wildmon on _At the Core_ on American Family Radio to discuss the rise of Flock cameras across our nation. During that conversation we kept circling one word -- surveillance -- and whether America is quietly becoming a surveillance state. That question stayed with me long after the microphones went off, because underneath it is a much older question: are we a nation built on safety, or a nation built on liberty?
[| | | Listen now * 51:05
---|---|---](https://substack.com/redirect/c3f0cd7f-828f-4adc-8d33-83e218d4555f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
_**Listen to[ At the Core with Walker Wildmon ](https://substack.com/redirect/1a2d6cb3-01a8-45f4-ac40-d836c354979f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)on American Family Radio**_
Somewhere along the way, many Americans came to believe that the first duty of government is to keep us safe. It might be comforting idea, but it is a false one. Our founders did not build this country to shield us from every danger -- they built it to shield us from the greatest danger of all, a government with too much power over its own people. So if you want to understand why cameras are quietly going up across Mississippi to photograph every car that passes, you first have to see that we have our own founding backward.
The men who built this country did not organize it around safety. They organized it around liberty. Read the Bill of Rights and you will notice something strange: it is almost entirely a list of things the government is forbidden to do -- even when doing them would make us safer. Police cannot search your home without a warrant, though warrantless searches would surely catch more criminals. You cannot be silenced, though some speech is dangerous. You cannot be jailed on an accusation you are never allowed to face. Every one of those protections is a deliberate trade. The founders accepted more risk in exchange for more freedom. A nation built on safety would never have written such rules.
They did this on purpose. They had just thrown off a government that justified every intrusion -- the general warrants, the standing armies, the soldiers in private homes -- in the sacred name of order. They concluded that concentrated power was a bigger threat than disorder ever was. Patrick Henry did not say give me safety or give me death.
This is not a small distinction. It decides what kind of country we are. In a nation built on liberty, the government must justify itself to you. In a nation built on safety, you must justify yourself to the government. In the first, the citizen watches the state. In the second, the state watches the citizen.
Which brings us to the cameras. Flock license-plate readers and the new AI systems coming to our highways operate on one simple premise: photograph everyone, because anyone might be a criminal. That sentence is unthinkable in a country built on liberty and perfectly natural in one built on safety. When innocent Americans are pulled over at gunpoint because a camera misread a plate, that is not the system failing. That is a safety-first machine doing exactly what it was designed to do -- sweep broadly and sort out the innocent later.
Here is the problem safety can never solve. It has no stopping point. There is always one more freedom to surrender for one more sliver of security, and then another after that. Liberty is the only principle that tells the government where it may not go, no matter how safe the alternative sounds.
Mississippi drew that line in 2009 when it banned automated traffic cameras. Seventeen years later, the state crossed its own line. Safety is the floor beneath a free people. It was never meant to be the ceiling above them.

clean_body: Today I had the opportunity to join Walker Wildmon on At the Core on American Family Radio to discuss the rise of Flock cameras across our nation. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? from the desk ofDana Criswell | | | Jul 22 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Today I had the opportunity to join Walker Wildmon on At the Core on American Family Radio to discuss the rise of Flock cameras across our nation. During that conversation we kept circling one word -- surveillance -- and whether America is quietly becoming a surveillance state. That question stayed with me long after the microphones went off, because underneath it is a much older question: are we a nation built on safety, or a nation built on liberty? Listen to American Family Radio Somewhere along the way, many Americans came to believe that the first duty of government is to keep us safe. It might be comforting idea, but it is a false one. Our founders did not build this country to shield us from every danger -- they built it to shield us from the greatest danger of all, a government with too much power over its own people. So if you want to understand why cameras are quietly going up across Mississippi to photograph every car that passes, you first have to see that we have our own founding backward. The men who built this country did not organize it around safety. They organized it around liberty. Read the Bill of Rights and you will notice something strange: it is almost entirely a list of things the government is forbidden to do -- even when doing them would make us safer. Police cannot search your home without a warrant, though warrantless searches would surely catch more criminals. You cannot be silenced, though some speech is dangerous. You cannot be jailed on an accusation you are never allowed to face. Every one of those protections is a deliberate trade. The founders accepted more risk in exchange for more freedom. A nation built on safety would never have written such rules. They did this on purpose. They had just thrown off a government that justified every intrusion -- the general warrants, the standing armies, the soldiers in private homes -- in the sacred name of order. They concluded that concentrated power was a bigger threat than disorder ever was. Patrick Henry did not say give me safety or give me death. This is not a small distinction. It decides what kind of country we are. In a nation built on liberty, the government must justify itself to you. In a nation built on safety, you must justify yourself to the government. In the first, the citizen watches the state. In the second, the state watches the citizen. Which brings us to the cameras. Flock license-plate readers and the new AI systems coming to our highways operate on one simple premise: photograph everyone, because anyone might be a criminal. That sentence is unthinkable in a country built on liberty and perfectly natural in one built on safety. When innocent Americans are pulled over at gunpoint because a camera misread a plate, that is not the system failing. That is a safety-first machine doing exactly what it was designed to do -- sweep broadly and sort out the innocent later. Here is the problem safety can never solve. It has no stopping point. There is always one more freedom to surrender for one more sliver of security, and then another after that. Liberty is the only principle that tells the government where it may not go, no matter how safe the alternative sounds. Mississippi drew that line in 2009 when it banned automated traffic cameras. Seventeen years later, the state crossed its own line. Safety is the floor beneath a free people. It was never meant to be the ceiling above them. Friends,
This is Zyon Khalifa , and I wanted to reach out to you directly to tell you why I'm running to bring a new generation of leadership to South Carolina, and show you how we are on the verge of pulling off the biggest upset of the election cycle . When we launched this campaign, national talking heads and out-of-state pundits immediately tried to write us off. But we just won a hard-fought primary runoff—not by playing the traditional political game, but by building a grassroots coalition of everyday folks who are tired of being overlooked by our leaders in Washington .

subject: Wesley Bell’s AIPAC trip
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter, have you
seen this?

Rep. Wesley Bell is trying to claim he “represents” MO-01, boasting about
bringing resources home while taking a swipe at Cori Bush for “seeing it
differently.”

What he failed to mention? While St. Louis' families are struggling, Bell
fled the country for a luxury, AIPAC-funded trip to Israel.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260722-2-cb.nnmMid&refcode=em20260722-38066&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1002&akid=38066%2E1203867%2EwxBYpw ]Tweet from @CoriBush: "You abandoned St. Louis and the country for a
lavish, MAGA-AIPAC funded trip to Israel. Maybe sit this one out, Wesley";
Cori's quote tweeting a post from @bell4mo that says: "To me, representing
#MO01 means bringing resources home to modernize Lambert Airport, help our
neighbors recover from last year's tornado damage, and keep our
communities safe from gun violence. But Cori Bush saw it differently."

Bell joined dozens of other Congress members on these lobbyist-funded
junkets — completely ignoring his own voter base’s unfavorable opinions of
Israel. To make matters worse, he just voted against cutting $3.3 billion
in U.S. weapons funding to Israel, all to appease the group bankrolling
his campaign.

These trips are a standard tool used to buy support for Israel on Capitol
Hill, and Bell fell right in line — choosing to fund bombing civilians
overseas with people’s hard-earned tax dollars while delivering only a
fraction of what Cori has for MO-01.

Because Bell was right about one thing: Cori does see it differently — and
it’s exactly the kind of leadership St. Louis deserves.

When she was in Congress, Cori led the charge by introducing the original
ceasefire legislation even when it wasn’t easy, and has never backed down
from the fight for ending military aid to Israel and its genocide of
Palestinian people.

That’s why AIPAC’s super PAC took her out in 2024, and why they’ve already
spent $2.2 million to stop her this time around.

With less than two weeks until Missouri’s primary, we have the chance to
replace one of AIPAC’s puppets with a real progressive champion who’s
accountable to her community. But we can only defeat the megadonors and
super PACs flooding the race in these final 13 days if this grassroots
team steps up right now.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260722-2-cb.nnmMid&refcode=em20260722-38066&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1003&akid=38066%2E1203867%2EwxBYpw ]Can you split a donation of $10 to Cori’s campaign and
Justice Democrats today to help us send Cori back to Congress and deliver
another loss to AIPAC on August 4th?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260722-2-cb.nnmMid&refcode=em20260722-38066&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1022&akid=38066%2E1203867%2EwxBYpw ]Contribute $10

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

subject: 14 days out: pods, ten texts, and a sneak peek

body:
Hi friends,
Fourteen days to the primary. Early voting runs through Saturday, August 1, and if you want a mail ballot, that request has to be in by this Friday, July 24 (request yours at [vote.elections.virginia.gov](https://www.google.com/url?q=https://vote.elections.virginia.gov&source=gmail&ust=1784859704769000&sa=E)). Here's what we need this week, and a few items we're particularly proud of.
In this one, in order: the neutrality fight you may have seen in the news, Jason's first Substack post, a chance to represent us tomorrow night in Richmond, your pod captain (who's about to call you), an ask that takes ten minutes, yard signs, our first ad, the voting deadlines, and, if you're the letter-writing type, everything you need to get printed in your local paper. Skim what you need. The one thing we'd beg you to read is the ten texts section.
**YOU MAY HAVE SEEN JASON IN THE NEWS**
Last week, Jason organized a letter asking the Democratic Party of Virginia to reaffirm its neutrality after the DCCC promoted one of our opponents while early voting was already underway. Yesterday, that effort escalated. Six of the seven campaigns in this race, led by Jason, sent a second letter pointing to FEC filings that show the state party joined a fundraising committee benefiting a single candidate in the middle of a contested primary.
This is the whole campaign in one story. Jason is running because the people who make the calls should answer to the people who pay the price. That includes party institutions. Voters should pick nominees. Not Washington. Full stop.
And the stakes are higher than they look. The Supreme Court just struck down the limits on coordinated party spending, and because disclosures come monthly, money spent right now won't be public until weeks after the primary is over. The only thing standing between voters and a nomination decided behind closed doors is a party that plays it straight. If we're the party of No Kings, that means no kingmakers either. Free and fair elections: that is all the candidates in this race are asking for and we are proud to lean into that fight because it's the right thing to do.
Full story here: [VA-01 Democrats escalate dispute with state party over primary neutrality - Virginia Mercury](https://www.google.com/url?q=https://virginiamercury.com/2026/07/21/va-01-democrats-escalate-dispute-with-state-party-over-primary-neutrality/&source=gmail&ust=1784859704769000&sa=E)
Also new this week: our first Substack post is up. [House Democrats Have the Resources: Seven Things Democrats Should Be Doing Right Now](https://www.google.com/url?q=https://substack.com/home/post/p-207821372&source=gmail&ust=1784859704769000&sa=E) The short version: the discharge petition that freed the Epstein files proved the minority's tools work. Jason lays out the machine that runs those tools at scale (shadow hearings, GAO requests, inspector general referrals, constituent casework dashboards) and what he'd do in his first 100 days to build it. ASK: If you have a Substack account, restacking it to your network would help us out a great deal.
Finally, I want to ensure folks saw the rebuttal to Rob Wittman's July 4th op-ed. It is paywalled, but you can find the full version here: [The ladder that lifted Rob Wittman is one he's voting to pull up | Guest column](https://www.google.com/url?q=https://jasonknappforcongress.com/the-ladder-that-lifted-rob-wittman-is-one-hes-voting-to-pull-up-guest-column/&source=gmail&ust=1784859704769000&sa=E)
**ASK: If this is the kind of leadership you want in Congress, forward this email to one person who hasn 't met Jason yet.**
**CAN YOU BE OUR PERSON IN RICHMOND TOMORROW NIGHT?**
We're bummed we cannot attend the Metro Richmond Area Young Democrats (MRAYD) General Body Meeting on Thursday, July 23 at 6:30 PM at Legend Brewing Co (321 W 7th St, Richmond, VA 23224). If someone is available to attend in our place, you would have our gratitude. Reach out to Jen Cash and we'll ensure you have everything you need: [jen@jasonknappforcongress.com](mailto:jen@jasonknappforcongress.com) or 202.696.3633.
**THE PODS ARE LIVE**
A note from Josh, our campaign manager: we've organized the district into eight neighborhood teams, or pods, each with a captain and a home turf. If you've signed up to volunteer, you're in one. Your captain is your person for canvasses, postcard parties, and phone banks close to home. No more driving an hour to help. The work is on your own street, with your own neighbors, and your captain will be reaching out this week if they haven't already. Not in a pod yet? Reply with your town and we'll match you.
**TEN TEXTS. THAT 'S THE WHOLE ASK.**
Here's the math that should make you optimistic. This is a seven-way primary, and turnout in an August primary is small. Around 9,000 votes across the whole district can win this thing. Not ninety thousand. Nine.
At that scale, the most powerful tool in politics isn't a TV ad. It's you texting people who already know you. A message from a friend gets read and gets acted on in a way no campaign text ever will.
ASK: This week, please text ten people you know who live in VA-01. Tell them you're supporting Jason Knapp, a retired Navy combat pilot who's refusing corporate PAC money and has pledged to limit his own time in office. Tell them early voting is open now. Then ask them when they plan to vote. That question, "when," is the one that turns a supporter into a voter.
Ten texts from each of you outnumbers anything money can buy in this race.
**YARD SIGNS: WANT ONE? CAN YOU DELIVER A FEW?**
Two asks, both easy.
First: if you're reading this and don't have a Knapp sign in your yard, we'd love to fix that. Reply and we'll get one to you.
Second: we need drivers. We've mapped 81 supporters around the district who are ready for a sign, and we need volunteers to run drop-off routes, a handful of addresses each, an hour or so of your time. Windows down, playlist on, democracy delivered. Reply with your town and we'll hand you a route.
**THE NEW AD**
Our first ad is up this week and we hope you will like it! Watch the new ad here: [Knapp full ad - YouTube](https://www.google.com/url?q=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v%3D4BLiZ1IPqyw&source=gmail&ust=1784859704770000&sa=E)
**DATES TO CIRCLE**
Mail ballot requests close this Friday, July 24. Request yours at [vote.elections.virginia.gov](https://www.google.com/url?q=https://vote.elections.virginia.gov&source=gmail&ust=1784859704770000&sa=E). Early voting runs through Saturday, August 1 (find your early voting location at the same site). Primary day is Tuesday, August 4, polls open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m.
**LETTERS TO THE EDITOR - Write a Letter, Reach Your Neighbors**
The letters page is the most-read page in most local papers, and editors print letters from local people. If you've been looking for a way to help before the August 4 primary, this is one of the most effective things you can do from your kitchen table.
How to get printed:
\- Watch the word limit for your paper (listed below). Shorter gets picked first.
\- Hook it to something the paper ran. "I read your story last week about rising power bills, and..." Editors publish letters that continue their own coverage.
\- Write about what you've seen firsthand, in your own words. Form letters get tossed, and so does anything you've already posted on social media. Original letters only.
\- Make one point, not five.
\- Sign with your full name, town, and a daytime phone number (papers call to verify but won't print it). If you volunteer with a campaign, say so in a line at the bottom.
\- One paper at a time, and most run one letter per writer per month, so make it count.
\- The weeklies close their pages early in the week. Deadlines below are firm.
Where to send yours:
**Chesterfield, Henrico, Hanover:** Richmond Times-Dispatch, online form at [richmond.com/forms/contact/letter_to_the_editor](https://www.google.com/url?q=https://www.richmond.com/forms/contact/letter_to_the_editor&source=gmail&ust=1784859704770000&sa=E) (300 word limit). Henrico readers can also write the Henrico Citizen: [tlappas@henricocitizen.com](mailto:tlappas@henricocitizen.com)
**Williamsburg, James City, York, Poquoson:** Virginia Gazette: [letters@vagazette.com](mailto:letters@vagazette.com). WYDaily: [news@wydaily.com](mailto:news@wydaily.com). Daily Press: online letters form [here](https://www.google.com/url?q=https://www.dailypress.com/opinion/letters/vp-letter-to-the-editor-form-20190814-xgzj66yisjappg3aro6dyazjj4-story.html&source=gmail&ust=1784859704770000&sa=E).
**Gloucester and Mathews:** Gazette-Journal, Charlie Koenig, editor: [ckoenig@gazettejournal.net](mailto:ckoenig@gazettejournal.net). 300 words, due Tuesdays by noon. This paper requires a signature, so sign a copy, scan or photograph it, and attach it to your email.
**Middlesex:** Southside Sentinel, Don Richeson, editor: [editor@ssentinel.com](mailto:editor@ssentinel.com). 400 words, letter can be in the email body, due Tuesdays by 10 AM.
**Lancaster (Northern Neck):** Rappahannock Record, Robert Mason, editor: [editor@rapprecord.com](mailto:editor@rapprecord.com). 300 words, due Tuesdays by noon. When print space runs out, letters may run on RRecord.com.
**Westmoreland, Northumberland, Richmond County:** Michelle Smith edits the Westmoreland News, Northumberland Echo, and Northern Neck News: [nnneditor@lcs.net](mailto:nnneditor@lcs.net). No word limit, due Fridays. Ask for your letter to run in all three papers.
**Essex and King & Queen:** Rappahannock Times, Chris Rose, editor: [rapptimes@gmail.com](mailto:rapptimes@gmail.com). 500 words, due Mondays by 10 AM. This paper wants your letter attached as a Word document.
**King William and New Kent:** Country Courier: [office@countrycouriernews.com](mailto:office@countrycouriernews.com). Submit five days before publication.
Questions? Reply to this email.
* * *
Paid for by Knapp for Congress
You're receiving this because you've connected with the campaign: donated, volunteered, signed up, or written to us. If you'd rather not get these updates, reply "remove" and we'll take you off the list.

Around 9,000 votes across the whole district can win this thing. Not ninety thousand. Nine. At that scale, the most powerful tool in politics isn't a TV ad. It's you texting people who already know you. A message from a friend gets read and gets acted on in a way no campaign text ever will. ASK: This week, please text ten people you know who live in VA-01. Tell them you're supporting Jason Knapp, a retired Navy combat pilot who's refusing corporate PAC money and has pledged to limit his own time in office. Tell them early voting is open now. Then ask them when they plan to vote. That question, "when," is the one that turns a supporter into a voter. Ten texts from each of you outnumbers anything money can buy in this race. YARD SIGNS: WANT ONE? CAN YOU DELIVER A FEW? Two asks, both easy. First: if you're reading this and don't have a Knapp sign in your yard, we'd love to fix that. Reply and we'll get one to you. Second: we need drivers. We've mapped 81 supporters around the district who are ready for a sign, and we need volunteers to run drop-off routes, a handful of addresses each, an hour or so of your time. Windows down, playlist on, democracy delivered. Reply with your town and we'll hand you a route. THE NEW AD Our first ad is up this week and we hope you will like it! Watch the new ad here: DATES TO CIRCLE Mail ballot requests close this Friday, July 24. Request yours at . Early voting runs through Saturday, August 1 (find your early voting location at the same site). Primary day is Tuesday, August 4, polls open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. LETTERS TO THE EDITOR - Write a Letter, Reach Your Neighbors The letters page is the most-read page in most local papers, and editors print letters from local people. If you've been looking for a way to help before the August 4 primary, this is one of the most effective things you can do from your kitchen table. How to get printed: \- Watch the word limit for your paper (listed below). Shorter gets picked first. \- Hook it to something the paper ran. "I read your story last week about rising power bills, and..." Editors publish letters that continue their own coverage. \- Write about what you've seen firsthand, in your own words. Form letters get tossed, and so does anything you've already posted on social media. Original letters only. \- Make one point, not five. \- Sign with your full name, town, and a daytime phone number (papers call to verify but won't print it). If you volunteer with a campaign, say so in a line at the bottom. \- One paper at a time, and most run one letter per writer per month, so make it count. \- The weeklies close their pages early in the week. Deadlines below are firm. Where to send yours: Chesterfield, Henrico, Hanover: Richmond Times-Dispatch, online form at (300 word limit). Henrico readers can also write the Henrico Citizen: mailto:tlappas@henricocitizen.com Williamsburg, James City, York, Poquoson: Virginia Gazette: mailto:letters@vagazette.com. WYDaily: mailto:news@wydaily.com. Daily Press: online letters form . Gloucester and Mathews: Gazette-Journal, Charlie Koenig, editor: mailto:ckoenig@gazettejournal.net. 300 words, due Tuesdays by noon. This paper requires a signature, so sign a copy, scan or photograph it, and attach it to your email. Middlesex: Southside Sentinel, Don Richeson, editor: mailto:editor@ssentinel.com. 400 words, letter can be in the email body, due Tuesdays by 10 AM. Lancaster (Northern Neck): Rappahannock Record, Robert Mason, editor: mailto:editor@rapprecord.com. 300 words, due Tuesdays by noon. When print space runs out, letters may run on RRecord.com. Westmoreland, Northumberland, Richmond County: Michelle Smith edits the Westmoreland News, Northumberland Echo, and Northern Neck News: mailto:nnneditor@lcs.net. No word limit, due Fridays. Ask for your letter to run in all three papers. Essex and King & Queen: Rappahannock Times, Chris Rose, editor: mailto:rapptimes@gmail.com. 500 words, due Mondays by 10 AM. This paper wants your letter attached as a Word document. King William and New Kent: Country Courier: mailto:office@countrycouriernews.com. Submit five days before publication. Questions? | | Fellow Conservative, If you haven’t heard about “See You at the Library Day” on Fox News or Newsmax or your other favorite news sources, _**[please let me tell you why it’s so critical.](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=8f3b60e7c5354e2da034b359691e5f90&_e=e0cmWelW42jRQcD6qUmjZ0NMOjx2UT72OamZ6hiIAA9LdDvwrO2_CSnKo2oq8XhfRHbzl9032J9hD24_h2B7vtgItQRav0xs7lkpJ1OBdONZFGIHw942S6IbxtBmxIShm1Yanbrt2rf0F-zj5eTAUKm5Si_fZSxnW1xhG1uygMzOU0NCE1c-rRtRPhEFOfjrzgZ5BKlxp4b19-G8RvGK1jDzjwocogWaJFY7hiTIUneUo9x9_7eZO-Hj0_KO1VyVNY5rENNlcL_OW1b28lK_TXzO3tf4b-DGRPlmTmvRb26e06eUhNlNKa5rJ8eqmiIoNCiAz_MWa_jrQeYlTJQKjNYIdWHvE_Z6ve3IvweMDi0eY_ZcVlYmoSxjr5Aq1hZIA5vVx8QWIeFQ6-zgehFQBa9Na4J6HSYS1zkflh1Qw2c7TkWA83PkP_dk9SP0ZGIrIutK2tAE-oqrsv5lJT987p-yOkQ6HgTKe2GG-H5YK36dfA6mwH1e9VkzdKLe4YNEKaLm5l-O8cVSxZTBBnwjzR9Cq4eAwuo0674k8EbxeNxJzPFxjsCl6_pJsmf2VlRf1n3f3Oe21H-dK85nBOfZXtL0jezHePakgRgFPoQd4KcCf9lBWfglnTNvqxytqWwsH5HzKy9FRWE5E4OgwfIZtTvlSbjyYAgoqUj2Ust1pfGtkgysxrxuwHGgf42OgsbDwKoQ9iwdxA6ckzGgf6X24A%3D%3D)**_ Back when you were growing up, you may remember lazy Saturdays at the library with a kind but stern librarian.She would fill your mind with classics like _Pat the Bunny_ and _The Little Engine That Could_. And eventually you got old enough to roam by yourself and discover adventures like the _Three Musketeers_ , _Treasure Island_ and _Charlotte’s Web_.But today, all that has changed. Instead of filling children with wholesome stories, the president of the American Library Association (ALA) says libraries should be used to address ‘systemic racism’ and elevate ‘BIPOC and GLBTQR+ writers and voices.’ Radical librarians call _Adventures of Huckleberry Finn_ and _To Kill a Mockingbird_ “racist.” They’ve stripped Laura Ingalls Wilder’s name from a prestigious book award because of her “problematic’ _Little House_ series.And they bring in men wearing full makeup, dresses, and high heels for “Drag Queen Story Hours” where books like these are read to children of all ages... _A is for Activist._ An _ABC_ _board_ _book_ for “families who want their kids to grow up in a space that is unapologetic about activism, environmental justice, civil rights, LGBTQ rights, and everything else that activists believe in and fight for.” _Woke Baby_. “For all the littlest progressives, waking up to seize a new day of justice and activism. Woke babies raise their fists in the air. Woke babies cry out for justice. Woke babies grow up to change the world.” _Prince and Knight._ The “premier queer-friendly fairy tale” about a prince who marries a knight instead of a princess. And _The Hips on the Drag Queens Go Swish, Swish, Swish._ A “family-friendly celebration of drag” that encourages children to “work it.”I wish I could tell you this was only happening in places like New York City and San Francisco...

The kit includes everything they need to bring your conservative values back into our public libraries: instructions for booking their library space and running their Story Hour, small American flags for little ones, fun stickers, wholesome books, Bible memory verse cards, and other specialty items. Your sponsorship gift is the only way we can fund our “Story Hours” for 250,000 children to counter the radical leftists who’ve taken control of our libraries.We don’t have the millions behind us like the giant taxpayer-funded ALA. Singlehandedly, you’ll be reaching 50 children with our wholesome, Godly, and patriotic message. Whatever you can give whether it’s $35, $125, or anything higher or lower please send in your sponsorship gift in the next 48 hours so we know how many libraries we have sponsored for this year’s “See You at the Library Day.” Thank you! God Bless You and God Bless America, Kirk Cameron | | | BRAVE For Good 100 I-45 N 260Conroe, TX 77301 | This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com

#
Is the answer to our problems to turn to the same playbook over and over again?
A playbook that says in order to win, Democrats must rely on the same dark money that backed election deniers who voted to overturn the 2020 election.
A playbook that says in order to win we need to show deference to Trump by thanking the ICE agency.
A playbook that says, in order to win, we must be defenders of the status quo.
**_Here’s what I believe:_ Good leadership swings for the fences.**
Good leadership gets big money out of our system. It takes on the corruption that blocks common sense solutions that would lift working people.
I believe that our elected officials should take on abuses of corporate greed everywhere they find it.
That is why I don’t — and never will — take money from industry lobbyists or corporations. Because **we deserve better.**

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9a8a8eba-d0bc-4b4f-a345-27dc41502ed0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Hi, it's Mandela. Since I've entered this race, I've made it clear I have two big goals: deliver for working-class families and protect Wisconsin from Donald Trump's handpicked candidate for Governor.
I've kept my foot on the gas and put in the work, traveling to and gaining the support of Wisconsinites from all 72 counties.
And now, I believe that work speaks for itself in today's new Marquette Law poll.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9a8a8eba-d0bc-4b4f-a345-27dc41502ed0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
### **I am beating Tom Tiffany by 4 points. Other Democratic candidates are polling 3 or more points BEHIND him.**
This poll shows that I am the only Democrat who has a case to beat Tom Tiffany that bears out in the numbers.
But, I know that polling isn't enough of a case to be the candidate. As I said before, I don't _just_ care about beating my MAGA opponent.
### **At the center of my campaign is fighting for and earning the trust of working-class families.**
And in a primary that should be about making the case to and earning the trust of Wisconsin families, outsiders are trying to meddle.
Now, Republicans are spending millions to promote the candidate they think they can beat. That's not Wisconsinites voicing their preferences; that's outside dollars trying to manipulate and divide us.
And establishment Democrats aren't innocent, either. Instead of letting the democratic process play out, political insiders worked behind closed doors to try to tip the scales in favor of another candidate.
Why? Frankly, I'm still trying to figure all of that out. But, here's what I do know for certain: I'm committed to fighting for working-class families and refuse to take a cent from corporate PACs to win this race. That's why I'm proud that so many folks are resonating with our campaign.
### **Look, I entered this race to fight - to fight to win and fight to deliver.**
I'm ready to stand strong in what this campaign has built, the grassroots movement we have cultivated, and I am confident that we can and will win.
But it's obvious that Republicans and establishment Democrats fear our campaign because we can win and because we can deliver.
### **So, it 's up to us.**
What are we going to do before August 11th to make sure Wisconsin's Democratic candidate for Governor represents the best of us?
What are we going to do to make sure that the Democratic candidate can defeat Trump's handpicked candidate on November 3rd?
**[I 've laid out the stakes, and if you're with me, I need you now more than ever. Will you chip in right now to fuel this campaign and ensure we have the resources to win and deliver? ](https://substack.com/redirect/9a8a8eba-d0bc-4b4f-a345-27dc41502ed0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)[->](https://substack.com/redirect/902a609e-a072-429e-889b-b82d01209c05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[CHIP IN NOW ->](https://substack.com/redirect/9a8a8eba-d0bc-4b4f-a345-27dc41502ed0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The writing is on the wall: we can win. Now, let's go do it.
\- Mandela Barnes

name: JB Pritzker
subject: Being blunt about New Hampshire
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/221?c0=em_ms_cp_20260722_3.XHc5u8&refcode=em20260722-3&t=1&akid=7880%2E582294%2E-Hq9N2)
Governor JB Pritzker here.
Let me be blunt: **_Everything we care about is on the line in 2026 — and New Hampshire could decide the outcome._**
We’ve already seen the damage Trump’s second term is inflicting on our country: His ICE agents are once again targeting families in broad daylight -- tearing apart communities, rounding up workers, and instilling fear across entire neighborhoods. He’s gutting environmental protections while utility rates spike, forcing working families to foot the bill so his billionaire donors can cash out.
He has no interest in bipartisanship, decency, or democracy. **And if Democrats don’t take back the Senate this November, there will be nothing stopping him.** That’s why we _must_ win in New Hampshire.
**[Chris Pappas is running in a tied race that could decide Senate control. Chip in $5 now to help him win.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260722_3.e7rM10&refcode=em20260722-3&t=2&akid=7880%2E582294%2E-Hq9N2)**
Trump and his MAGA allies are laser-focused on New Hampshire. They’ve recruited a big-name candidate, they’re lining up GOP billionaire donors, and they know if they win here, they’ll shut the door on a Democratic Senate majority.
We can’t let that happen.
Chris Pappas is a fighter. He’s taken on Big Pharma, defended reproductive freedom, and delivered for working families in one of the toughest districts in the country.
I want him in the Senate. But we’re all going to have to come together to get him there. He’s running in a true battleground. His race is tied. And the GOP machine, desperate to keep Democrats locked out of power, is ready to bury him in dark money and attack ads.
**[That’s why I’m asking-- urgently -- for your help: Can you chip in $5 to help Chris Pappas win in New Hampshire and give us a fighting chance to stop Trump?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260722_3.e7rM10&refcode=em20260722-3&t=3&akid=7880%2E582294%2E-Hq9N2)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260722_3.e7rM10&amount=5&refcode=em20260722-3&t=22&akid=7880%2E582294%2E-Hq9N2)**
The damage is real. The stakes are massive. And the time to act is right now.
Thank you for standing with Chris and for standing up to the madness.
JB Pritzker
Governor of Illinois
**New Hampshire is poised to be one of the closest Senate races in the country. Will you chip in today to help Chris stop the Republicans from flipping the Granite State red and expanding their Senate majority?**
**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_cp_footer?refcode=em20260722-3&t=23&refcode2=7880_582294_-Hq9N2&akid=7880%2E582294%2E-Hq9N2)**

body:
Derek, we just got out of our mid-week finance meeting — and things aren’t looking great.

In 2024, Elon Musk spent more money in NY-17 than in any other Congressional district. Billionaires and special interest groups were able to drag Mike Lawler across the finish line, even while Kamala won. So when I saw this headline, my alarm bells went off. [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqiBIysd_1t7dQL51NYrcys-m_vYbS_fSFWnMSCqgNUawdJvMcNP0-yw3SCe5KaEJQSRpyrUXOzswsWZONH5b8qtiKq88_1mw1pv7mNPmH9RxuKS-A1ksFLUXBEr4FMbM6f0TpKVW6V5q0MRwUA0-RxCa0MgiCIEt2NA8CNvLkqe117jPOGYUcsdAUqfPSFfK0pgjoAR03vlt4PCX_OLooplnv5Adz67Q9xtRuMPMzoLfz_swWEPgH1DBEPKQSvE-NYRpA4oR12YRie_TLeOvNNt4u4YWHfkXzJ9FCxrS8dg/4sj/U1TUCtzqRIC7JzLfT5G1jg/h0/h001.70h3bAnfrw3JzYLhIeilIk8gHNz-MNrR_R2v3nlIvps) **Trump’s MAGA Supreme Court has ripped off one of the last remaining campaign finance guardrails, giving the greenlight for dark money groups to funnel unlimited sums directly to candidates.** I’m not going to lie, it’s bad news. We’re going to see even more dark money in this race. It’s a loss for anyone who cares about making sure everyday Americans have a voice in government. I come from a blue-collar family. After attending West Point, I spent 16 years in the Army, did six tours overseas, and was Director for Counterterrorism at the White House. Asking for money doesn't come naturally to me. But I have to, if we’re going to have a chance against what the Supreme Court just unleashed. This is a grassroots campaign – last quarter, 90% of contributions were less than $100. So when you see me and my team out on the ground, fighting for votes, please know: We’re only able to do so because of the response to emails like this one. Our average donation to these emails is roughly $38. Some people give more, some people give less. $38 may not sound like a lot, compared to what Elon Musk has, but when hundreds of people chip in, it really gives us the ability to compete. [Please. If you can afford to do so, will you chip in $38, or whatever you can afford, to help us stand up to dark money and flip NY-17?
