clean_body: | | | | In 2024, Elon Musk spent more money in NY-17 than in any other Congressional district. Billionaires and special interest groups were able to drag Mike Lawler across the finish line, even while Kamala won. So when I saw this headline, my alarm bells went off. Trump’s MAGA Supreme Court has ripped off one of the last remaining campaign finance guardrails, giving the greenlight for dark money groups to funnel unlimited sums directly to candidates. I’m not going to lie, it’s bad news. We’re going to see even more dark money in this race. It’s a loss for anyone who cares about making sure everyday Americans have a voice in government. I come from a blue-collar family. After attending West Point, I spent 16 years in the Army, did six tours overseas, and was Director for Counterterrorism at the White House. Asking for money doesn't come naturally to me. But I have to, if we’re going to have a chance against what the Supreme Court just unleashed. This is a grassroots campaign – last quarter, 90% of contributions were less than $100. So when you see me and my team out on the ground, fighting for votes, please know: We’re only able to do so because of the response to emails like this one. Our average donation to these emails is roughly $38. subject: I had to fight harder to be heard.

body:
Now I’m fighting for you, Friend.
|

| | | | [](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)

---
| | Friend,
They said I’d never make it. That I should stay quiet, sit still, and stop trying.

But I’ve never been interested in playing by anybody’s rules but my own.

I’m Katie Britt. A Christian, a conservative, a mom of two, and the youngest Republican woman ever elected to the U.S. Senate. I didn’t run for office to win popularity points. I ran to fight for families like yours, Friend.
From day one, they saw me as just some small-town Alabama girl. Easy to ignore and _even easier to push aside_.

But what they didn’t count on is the kind of __backbone__ , __grit__ , and __fire__ women like me are made of.

The truth is, I’ve had to fight**twice as hard** to earn a seat at the table. And the moment I got there, the Left wasted no time trying to tear me down.

They didn’t expect a woman like me to show up and challenge _everything_ they stand for. They thought I’d sit down, smile, and play nice. **But that’s not who I am,_and it _never_ will be._**

I’ve had to prove myself in __every__ room I walk into. I’ve had to work longer hours, ask harder questions, and out-hustle the establishment just to be taken seriously. And still, every day, they try to undermine me, discredit me, and push me aside.

Why? Because I don’t play their games. I don’t fall in line. And I won’t apologize for my values, my faith, or my love for this country.

The Left is trying to undermine the values we hold dear, **and they’d love _nothing more_ than to see me back down.**

But here’s the thing: __I’m not going anywhere_._
I won’t apologize, I won’t play nice, and I won’t be backing down.

They are terrified of strong, unapologetic conservative women, and they _should_ be.

[**If you believe in fighting harder than anyone else just to be heard. If you believe in standing strong when the odds are against you, then I need you with me.**](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
This fight isn’t easy. It’s never been easy. But with your support, we’ll keep pushing forward, together. And we’ll prove that no one can ignore a woman with a backbone like mine.
---
[JOIN THE FIGHT >>>](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
Because if we don’t stand up today, the next generation will be forced to fight the same battles I have — fighting just to have their voices heard.
_**And I refuse to let that be their legacy, Friend.**_
\- Katie Britt

clean_body: Now I’m fighting for you, Friend. | | | | | | | | | | Friend, They said I’d never make it. That I should stay quiet, sit still, and stop trying. But I’ve never been interested in playing by anybody’s rules but my own. I’m Katie Britt. A Christian, a conservative, a mom of two, and the youngest Republican woman ever elected to the U.S. Senate. I didn’t run for office to win popularity points. I ran to fight for families like yours, Friend. From day one, they saw me as just some small-town Alabama girl. Easy to ignore and even easier to push aside. But what they didn’t count on is the kind of backbone , grit , and fire women like me are made of. The truth is, I’ve had to fighttwice as hard to earn a seat at the table. And the moment I got there, the Left wasted no time trying to tear me down. # [RFK Jr. cut food safety jobs. Now Michiganders are getting sick.](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=208086253&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA4MDg2MjUzLCJpYXQiOjE3ODQ3NjE0NTQsImV4cCI6MTc4NzM1MzQ1NCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.F-YKmrxVwWG0RMJj3MBEI0Myw3TkXpjAwVQ7Q60zEKs)
### This is what I was worried about when I filed articles of impeachment.
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Jul 22
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/rfk-jr-cut-food-safety-jobs-now-michiganders?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-restack-comment&action=restack-comment&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA4MDg2MjUzLCJpYXQiOjE3ODQ3NjE0NTQsImV4cCI6MTc4NzM1MzQ1NCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.F-YKmrxVwWG0RMJj3MBEI0Myw3TkXpjAwVQ7Q60zEKs&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/rfk-jr-cut-food-safety-jobs-now-michiganders?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Salads are giving people diarrhea.
I never thought I'd type that sentence in this newsletter. But I never thought RFK Jr. would be so bad at his job that I'd devote an entire Substack to warning people that their lettuce may contain a parasite that causes explosive diarrhea.
And I never thought I'd type the word "diarrhea" this many times in one post, but buckle up, that's the world right now.
More than 6,500 Michiganders have gotten sick. It's the worst year for this parasite in American history, and Michigan is the epicenter.
Behind every one of those numbers is somebody's kid missing summer camp, somebody's mom missing shifts she can't afford to miss, somebody's grandpa in an ER bed because of a Caesar salad.
So the question every Michigander deserves an answer to is: _How the heck did this happen?_
I've been yelling about this for a year. I wish I were wrong.
Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and the Trump administration took a chainsaw to our public health system. Thousands of food safety and public health jobs were cut, and career scientists were purged. And FoodNet, the CDC's early-warning system for foodborne illness, went from tracking eight pathogens down to two.
They kneecapped the system to watch out for foodborne illness. One year later, cyclospora showed up.
Former CDC Director Robert Redfield (who was appointed by Donald Trump, btw) said cutting this surveillance was contrary to the country's interest, **because surveillance is "the key to early identification."**
If you've been reading this newsletter or following politics a while, you know this isn't a new soapbox for me. Last September, I announced I was drafting articles of impeachment against RFK Jr. I formally introduced them because he'd fired the CDC director, purged the scientists, gutted the research, and misled the Senate under oath.
Now this outbreak happened. And now everyone knows RFK Jr.'s negligence is making us less safe.
This is what it looks like when the invisible system that quietly protects you goes away. It looks like 6,500 Michiganders glued to their toilets, signs on the Taco Bell counter, and a state government teaching us all to wash lettuce like it's 1826.
This is why a U.S. Senate that actually looks out for people is so critical. **RFK Jr. has this job because the Senate confirmed him.** The Senate is supposed to keep guys like RFK Jr. from, well ... this. When the Republican Senate is a rubber stamp for Trump, you get RFK Jr.
And when you get RFK Jr., you get explosive diarrhea spreading around the country.
This is what is at stake in November. MAGA Mike Rogers will do whatever Trump says. He's proved that again and again. This Senate seat in Michigan is the difference between a government that watches out for you and one that fires the watchers, calls it efficiency, and denies accountability.
I'm running because I give a damn about your family. I want your kids, parents, and friends to be safe and healthy. That used to be the bare minimum for the Senate. Now, it's all about the GOP kissing Trump's ring.
OK. Before I let you go, I'm going to do the thing RFK Jr.'s department should be doing louder: actual public health guidance, from one Michigander to another. Here's what the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services recommends right now:
* **Buy whole heads of lettuce** instead of bagged or premixed salad kits.
* **Throw away the outer two or three layers** of leaves and wash the rest under running water.
* **When you can cook it, cook it.** Heat kills this thing, but rewashing bagged greens doesn't.
* **If you have diarrhea that lasts more than a few days, call your doctor.** Ask about cyclosporiasis testing; it's very treatable with the right antibiotics.

And please, check on your neighbors, especially the older folks. If somebody is sick, bring them soup or offer to drive them to the doctor. It doesn't matter what political party they belong to; we gotta take care of each other. That's the Michigan way.
If this post made you mad, good. Take action. Share this post with somebody. Speak up. **[Support my campaign](https://substack.com/redirect/cfa4a3cf-d3cc-4078-9f03-feedb5de8b7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** or others who are speaking out against RFK Jr. This chaos simply must stop.
There's a lot going on in the world, and the people who did this are counting on it being too gross and too boring to talk about.
Let's hold them accountable.
And if RFK Jr. doesn't like me saying all of this. Well, go enjoy some unwashed lettuce, sir.
With grit,
Haley

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

Hey folks,
I sat down with **Destiny** for one of the most wide-ranging conversations we've had in a while--and we didn't hold back. We talked about the collapse of trust in American politics, the Democratic Party's future, Trump, conspiracy culture, AI, housing, campaign finance, and what it actually takes to govern instead of just going viral.
We agreed. We disagreed. We challenged each other. And honestly? That's exactly the kind of conversation we need more of right now.
**Here 's what we got into:**
* **00:01:07** -- We kick things off with the Mitch McConnell rumors, conspiracy theories, and why the collapse of public trust has made even basic facts feel impossible to believe.
* **00:10:06** -- Destiny and I dive into the fight over the Democratic Party, the rise of the DSA, primary politics, and whether Democrats have a compelling vision for the future.
* **00:23:50** -- We get into AI, crypto, economic populism, campaign finance reform, and what serious regulation should actually look like instead of empty slogans.
* **00:35:08** -- The conversation shifts to leadership, housing, long-term vision, and why America feels like it's been operating without a real mission for decades.
* **00:48:18** -- We close with a candid debate over what Democrats got wrong, why Republicans bear enormous responsibility for today's political climate, and what has to change before 2028.

This episode is about more than partisan talking points. It's about whether we're still capable of having honest conversations about governing, policy, and the future of the country. Even when we disagreed, the goal was understanding--not scoring points. If you're tired of the endless noise and want conversations that actually wrestle with the hard questions, this is one you shouldn't miss. And if you value honest conversations like this, help me keep them going.

name: Doug Jones
subject: My opponent wants to throw Obama in jail
disclaimer_text: Paid for by VPP
body:
| Folks,

My opponent, Tommy Tuberville, just went on national TV and said that President Barack Obama and Dr. Fauci should be thrown in jail. [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/120350?t=6&akid=26813%2E878179%2E8MBOrh) “He’s a crook. Obama is a crook. All these people broke the law. Let’s put them in jail.”

I suppose that’s what “Coach” has decided he wants to focus on.

Not the cost of groceries. Not rural hospitals across Alabama closing their doors. Not whether working people can find a good-paying job or make ends meet. He’d rather spend his time on television pushing baseless conspiracy theories and calling just about everybody he disagrees with a crook or a communist.

California loses roughly $867 million tied to [in-home services](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLHOnDAQhJ8GOp_MGuxLQZHmuj9tSrTYC7eSvUa2geTto0veIN0UM6NP38-v5Qs5suw_MNHsL15CDkslwUYrthZpL_mUUBvv70YLaLBKOwWwSFygD7MP1kBP8-Ceo7PjZKf-PfthWo2FCcAF9zTjOOhpIOP19m0b3Wh6nj9P2gGAmayeHk_jQti0W601m0HoRn0eARvVh89SqVzY-CIWyZ-U5eFz6uP8bu2onfnewauD133fjy3_Ero_s9TB68iRG_vawauVMx0KQ2JRB56VZVf5oqKGVSUK7JGDOvB3ImlVJRahmhsqj5G3XITxX30reAblczoio3hSPounIrUvczhujpGrdd2o94Qc_3K2_1B7zfAnAAD__7FJjN8), while Minnesota forfeits nearly $200 million in areas its own auditor flagged as high-risk. The [deferral advances](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckD2u2zAQhE8jdTTklUXKBYs06l7alMKKu7I34I8gLm282wfOEV43xczgw_fna_1CiZIfvzGxDy9ZqdBaOaPyhqqRH2dpmarK46m8wgDWDM4ArDmu0JMPZEfo2V_dfHP2Ntmpf_qZ7N0y0mzH-0gwBAswXyfaLcLV3V0v_vM0OAAYJztMl3l0RPvgNmvHfUTobkM7CJXrJZRc-Xyhyosl5_JJJV9CSX30T9WjduOvDpYOlr-tqj458_szSx0sGEJpWXGTKPrdwfLGqmz2ExsZzGRwa5U7WPRs6TBISbI5sFWu5mo2iVFKNolJAgqZA78TZ60mYJS9nFmwPz0d70-xWtfdhkdCif_p9AdCXx7-BQAA__-KFokA) Vice President JD Vance's anti-fraud task force, which has concentrated on Democratic-run states. Kennedy, joined by CMS chief Mehmet Oz, also signaled expanding HHS authority to exclude bad actors from federal health programs. ★★★
Trump Unleashes Century-Old Tariff
President Trump invoked [Section 338](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLHSnSAQRp9GOxzuomBDkcbuT5vSQXfxMkFgYNU_b5-5eYR0X_OdOXN-fa1fLsSQjp_uJLvfYcWMa6PkmDbHHOmo-UrYOBxvphUkaCGNAFhTXKFHu6NW0JN9mXk0epz01L8tzPukcNPT6JTCF22TGeVm_Gv2s9kB-2A_JGkAQE1aTsOsDKKXZtNaeeWgG-VV0DG1Yc-pUb0dh5tCSvmzchr2fPbRvplL69SPDpYOlud5Bp-_Ez2f29nBUnIMHPbWwcL1Ooug7-ISEgp2NXgvSnR_tpx_i5Ifqv6KgqtDEg-5kpNIWZRKLSAlFlcj7KvF8oQYQ9OmG-VxuhD_yfB_9Lst_A0AAP__V4-DxA) of the 1930 Tariff Act for the first time in history, slapping 50% tariffs on Canadian goods from wine to hockey sticks. The obscure provision lets a president penalize countries that discriminate against U.S. commerce. Trump [signed three orders](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0L2OpDAQBOCnMRnI0wZ7JnBwCdlceiFq7AZa8g_CHrh9-xX7CJt9QalUqn_v6Y0cOK1_MZJ1J08--6lQwkoz1hpoPfIn-VJ53SpNIEG30rQAUwoTNN46rxU0ZB_m2RvdD3poNutwmI2cjVzooZWX4ORr9vQiSbh4Nzds7yZpAEANWg7dUxnvF2lmrdWiEEQvP7vHSqVzORU6Tqx8EqeUb-XUuRybYLda9yLUHwGjgPG6ru7CsnFaa070HyMnOu6ogHHPgd2XgJFcTjne6vWgpVECxnp84t5y3HOhdpBtxYOXpbQ5tQ4TehQwNof1-8UhcNFG9HKNyOFnR_3FdaeF7wAAAP__fyR_nQ) Monday, citing Canada's treatment of American autos, alcohol, and dairy. The levies take effect roughly 30 days out, handing Ottawa an incentive to negotiate. Prime Minister Mark Carney said the two leaders agreed to [intensify talks](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckD2yozAQhE8jMrnkEUgvUbAJ2dt0Q2qMBjy7-qHQYMq338JHeFl30P119Z_v6Rs5cVl_Y6Ywv3iKNU6NCgo9UCTRutejxCa8PoUmMOC08RpgKmmCLoY5Ogsdhbv_6r3rBzd0z-DAWYgR52GxzoOBOy7zg7C_295Zix2Hq8l4ALCDM8Pty_oYF-MfztnFIqjeHFtEoXaba2m0v1D4RVxKvVQtt7nmLoWnyNaU_aVgVDCe53k7sT25rFKLcP7Es4Kx0NkUjBdVwfj3SJe5Kxgz7v_0jHuht274blr2I2-ai1BpvLy17BhJF1qr8Ifc9NE05602anowCsZuD3E7OSVuzqverBk5fQbKDz59BfgfAAD__zUrh-4). Analysts warn the untested authority may face legal challenges, but the White House called it a defensive response to discrimination. ★★★

The Senate Intelligence Committee [advanced Jay Clayton's](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLHS4yAMhJ8Gd2SIcCApKK5x9197pYeA7OgfEJmg2PO__Y1zb3CdVOzut_vna_6KVIjX37FiSBvNueW5I0fBexQpuL7am3MXWh-CMxhw2ngNMHOZYcghZWdhwHD219G78eIuwyPcRpvu-bwsozV4XQykWzRLwnhON0SfBgqHk_EAYC_OXE5X63NejL87ZxcbQY3m_cxRsJ9S446vLQptSMztuBqfUqtDCQ-RZ1f2l4JJwbTv-2mP_UG8SmOh-pFXBRPj3hVMR6qC6ftdjuesYPrXVRMLlkIrckKdWq0kgqhj3iIn7Po7_uhU4o807ppbJf5Q6MykYBpeIT93KoW682o0a41UPoTyH6NuAf4GAAD__yAXidE) nomination for director of national intelligence in a 9-8 party-line vote, teeing up a floor vote before the August recess.

Chairman Tom Cotton praised the former SEC chair as a [highly qualified nominee](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckDHSpCAUhE-jGRYDik5AsInZbLqhhfDQV4NAwVN3b781c4Q_66S7v_r-vJaXwYBx-20O0PbCxSW3VIiGYDVEAbaSzugq4bYTLIILxfjIhFhiWETrtHVKihb0Y5z6UfWDGtpd99I83eTdyv0wTUau3vO-Hx5Pr-wTAFrUnyU-CiHkoPjQTXJ0zvNxVUp6aUTT8zM7Q1A7m2KFchnCCzDG9EkpdjYdbdA7Ua6N_NWIuRHzfd-dT38j3J_a0Yg5p4CEtjZipnIeuTIXkWW0b2YDmFLZG_6x_SwuACtw4YVxY9nQzuL3pzJKmZlIyAhKSYXVs1yAIZhogeWStmKOtmiXbwwBqxqbnm-HwfBFpB9YvbT4HwAA___yiYza) with deep national-security experience. Clayton's confirmation could revive Section 702 of FISA, the warrantless foreign-surveillance tool Democrats stalled after Trump named Bill Pulte acting DNI. Democrats [uniformly opposed](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckL-OvCAQx58GOw0OCGxB8Wvo9tdeaVBGdy4IZmH19u0v3r3BdZ_JJN9_H_fx7ilSWv_7De180BhyGAsmX3HytUZcn_mVQqm0PiqOwEG1XLcAY4ojNMHOQQlo0PbaSK3koIbmYY1XkpvFywmlRm2ECWj0JIaw3HqDt4bspcQ1AIhB8aEzQoewcD0pJRbhgUn-2oOvWLo5p4LPw1c6kFLKF-XUzXlron3Uuhcm_jFwDNx5nl3Cs2z-6_ozcHuOVGkuDNxvq_bTv9s5-nfNqQ2JGLgrCgPH9cU9A0eBgetBCcWvs3nasJ8UIxWlmeTr5in--Nc_THZY-A4AAP__PI94cg) Clayton after he declined to say Joe Biden won in 2020. Republicans can confirm him without Democratic votes, provided no GOP senators defect on the floor.
Mace Snubs Trump's Senate Pick

Rep. Nancy Mace [endorsed Ralph Norman](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJycUL2yniAQfRrtcMiiYEORxu5Lm9JZ2VWZIDiAmsfPmPsGtzunOL-_P_MHffBx-4UHW3f7mRLNhSNWXrDWwFtOV6RS_bZXnkGCFtIIgDmGGVqyjrSClu0PM_ZG94Me2t0agzyuJJUzuqdxZQP0UnR6VTTo1tvXSRoAUIOWQzcqQ7RKs2itVoXQ9PI6CSuXzqVYON9Y_c0-xvSiFDuXjjbYvdazNOpnA1MD0_M83Zr-Rn5e2dHAdKbgq3elgelAx6LEaymi5us4izgzr5wzk_haLBxG8m-qWND9KSJjOHcRUz4wCh9LZaQ2WzofH4Iv2jS93A704X-b-o0Dbwv_AgAA__9mW4Rv) in South Carolina's special Senate election to replace the late Lindsey Graham, breaking with Trump-backed Darline Graham Nordone. ★★★

Fox News' [inaugural rankings](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLGunTAQRL8GOiOzBptbuEhDd9OmRHvtBawYG-EF8vkR7_3B60Yjzejo_HlPbwwxpOU3bmTdFSaf_VQoIdMHmSMtRz6TLxyWlWkCCVpIIwCmFCeovXVeK6jJtmbojO563derbcGZtpWInwHQtUrrvlXqNcj2pYGcqYN9nqQBANVr2TeDMt7P0ny0VrNCqDp57h6ZSuNyKnRcyOGikFJ-Uk6Ny1sd7cq8l0r9qmCsYLzvu5nzv0T3M9sqGPccAwdXKhg9bdkdyEWUFf-SOHfhcowhFTGjoyI4l_K0e0ROdIiD9oiONkostrOwuEMS327EgY7qw_r9DjGGok3VyWXDEL-4-AcqLwv_AwAA__8QGoa-) tag Senate races in Maine, Alaska, Iowa, and Ohio as toss-ups. In Maine, longtime Republican Susan Collins faces progressive Troy Jackson -- replacing ex-nominee Graham Platner -- in what looms as a premier 2026 battleground.

★★★

Growing up in a small rural town, I didn’t see many people like me. I didn’t even come out to my loved ones until college — it felt too risky to be openly gay back then.
_But I knew I wanted to be a mom._ When my son Josh was little, I went through a years-long legal battle — with a judge claiming that having two moms wasn’t in the “best interests” of my child. Every night, I put my son to bed, not sure if he would be ripped away from me the next day.

Minnesota’s 2nd district calls me “Congresswoman.” And if you help me get across the finish line this November, Minnesotans will call me “Senator.” I’d be the first lesbian woman to represent Minnesota — but hopefully not the last. I want to share my story with you, and then,= | | = Growing up in a small rural town, I didn’t see many people like me. I didn’t even come out to my loved ones until college — it felt too risky to be openly gay back then. But I knew I wanted to be a mom. When my son Josh was little, I went through a years-long legal battle — with a judge claiming that having two moms wasn’t in the “best interests” of my child. Every night, I put my son to bed, not sure if he would be ripped away from me the next day. = That was the hardest fight of my life. Thankfully, we won, and our amazing son Josh could stay. Our victory helped pave the way for other LGBTQ+ families to be recognized under the law, too. Years later, I met my wife Cheryl when she was coaching our kids’ basketball team. In 2008, we tied the knot — our kids proudly giving us away. It was one of the best days of my life. = Just weeks after, Proposition 8 passed, and suddenly our marriage was at risk of being erased. But people spoke up. Neighbors had hard conversations. Communities pushed for change. And together, we built a country that recognizes that love is love. All these years later, I still carry that same determination with me as I run for U.S. Senate. It’s how I flipped Minnesota’s 2nd district in 2018 and won four consecutive elections against Republicans. It’s how I took on Big Pharma — who spent millions trying to defeat me — and won. And it’s how we’re going to win this race for U.S. Senate come November — to defeat Trump’s top pick Michele Tafoya and the harmful agenda she wants to bring to Minnesota’s doorstep.
